1.1: The scroll of the genealogy of Yeshua the Messiah, the son of Daveed, the son of Avraham.
1.2: Avraham fathered Yitzchak, and Yitzchak fathered Ya’akov, and Ya’akov fathered Yehudah and his brothers.
1.3: And Yehudah fathered Peretz and Zerach out of Tamar, and Peretz fathered Chetzron, and Chetzron fathered Ram.
1.4: And Ram fathered Amminadav, and Amminadav fathered Nachshon, and Nachshon fathered Salmon.
1.5: And Salmon fathered Bo’az out of Rachav, and Bo’az fathered Oved out of Rut, and Oved fathered Yishai.
1.6: And Yishai fathered Daveed the king. And Daveed the king fathered Shlomo out of I her who had been the wife of Uriyah.
1.7: And Shlomo fathered Rechav’am, and Rechav’am fathered Aviyah, and Aviyah fathered Asa.
1.8: And Asa fathered Yehoshaphat, and Yehoshaphat fathered Yoram, and Yoram fathered Uziyahu.
1.9: And Uziyahu fathered Yotam, and Yotam fathered Achaz, and Achaz fathered Chizkiyahu.
1.10: And Chizkiyahu fathered Menashe, and Menashe fathered Amon, and Amon fathered Yoshiyahu.
1.11: Yoshiyahu fathered Yekonyahu and his brothers, at the time of the time of the deportation to Bavel.
1.12: And after the deportation to Bavel, Yekonyahu fathered Sh’altiel, and Sh’altiel fathered Zerubavel.
1.13: And Zerubavel fathered Avihud, and Avihud fathered Elyakim, Elyakim fathered Azur.
1.14: And Azur fathered Tzadok, and Tzadok fathered Yakhin, and Yakhin fathered Elihud.
1.15: And Elihud fathered El’azar, and El’azar fathered Mattan, and Mattan fathered Ya’akov.
1.16: And Ya’akov fathered Yosef, the husband of Miriam, by whom was born Yeshua, Who is called Messiah.
1.17: Therefore all the generations from Avraham to Daveed I were fourteen generations, and from Daveed to the deportation to Bavel fourteen generations, and from the deportation to Bavel to I the time of Messiah fourteen generations.
1.18: Now the birth of Yeshua the Messiah was as follows: When His mother Miriam had been betrothed to Yosef, before they came together, she was found to have conceived by the Holy Spirit.
1.19: And Yosef her husband being righteous, and not willing to disgrace her, intended to release her secretly.
1.20: But when he had considered these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, " Yosef, son of Daveed, do not be afraid to take alongside Miriam as your wife, for that which has been conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit.
1.21: " And she will bring forth a Son, and you will call His name Yeshua, for it is He Who will save His people from their sins. "
1.22: Now all this took place so that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying,
1.23: " BEHOLD, THE VIRGIN SHALL CONCEIVE, AND SHE WILL BRING FORTH A SON, AND THEY SHALL CALL HIS NAME IMMANU'EL, " which translated means, " GOD WITH US. "
1.24: And Yosef arose from his sleep, and did as the angel of the Lord commanded him, and took I her alongside as his wife,
1.25: and I he did not know her until she bore her son, and he called His name Yeshua.

2.1: Now after Yeshua was born in Beit - Lechem in I the land of Yehudah in the days of Herodes the king, behold, magi in the east arrived in Yerushalayim, saying,
2.2: " Where is He Who has been born King of the Yehudim? For we saw His star in the east, and have come to worship Him.
2.3: And when Herodes the king heard it, he was troubled, and all Yerushalayim with him.
2.4: And having gathered together all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he inquired of them where the Messiah was to be born.
2.5: And they said to him, " In Beit - Lechem of I the land of Yehudah, for so it has been written by the prophet,
2.6: " AND YOU, BEIT - LECHEM, LAND OF YEHUDAH, ARE BY NO MEANS LEAST AMONG THE LEADERS OF YEHUDAH, FOR OUT OF YOU WILL COME FORTH A LEADER WHO WILL SHEPHERD MY PEOPLE YISRAEL. "
2.7: Then Herodes secretly called the magi, and ascertained from them the time the star appeared.
2.8: And he sent them to Beit - Lechem, and said, " Go and make careful search for the Child, and when you have found I Him, report to me, that I may come and worship Him. "
2.9: And having heard the king, they departed. And behold, the star which they had seen in the east went on before them, until it came and stood over where the Child was.
2.10: And when they saw the star, they rejoiced with an exceedingly great joy.
2.11: And they came into the house and saw the Child with Miriam His mother, and they fell down and worshipped Him. And opening their treasures they presented to Him gifts of gold and frankincense and myrrh.
2.12: And having been warned in a dream not to return to Herodes, they departed for their own country by another way.
2.13: Now when they had departed, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to Yosef in a dream, saying, " Arise and take alongside the Child and His mother and escape to Mitzrayim, and remain there until I tell you. For Herodes is about to look for the Child in order to utterly ruin Him. "
2.14: And he arose and took alongside the Child and His mother by night, and departed for Mitzrayim.
2.15: And he was there until the death of Herodes, that it might be fulfilled what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet, saying, " OUT OF MITZRAYIM DID I CALL MY SON. "
2.16: Then Herodes, having seen that he was tricked by the magi, became very enraged, and sent forth and slew all the male children who were in Beit - Lechem and in all its regions, from two years and under, according to the time which he had ascertained from the magi.
2.17: Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Yirmayahu the prophet, saying,
2.18: " A VOICE WAS HEARD IN RAMAH, WEEPING AND GREAT MOURNING, RACHEL WEEPING FOR HER CHILDREN. AND SHE WOULD NOT BE COMFORTED, BECAUSE THEY WERE NO MORE. "
2.19: But when Herodes was dead, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to Yosef in a dream in Mitzrayim, saying,
2.20: " Arise, and take alongside the Child and His mother and go into the land of Yisrael; for those who sought the Child’s life are dead. "
2.21: And he arose and took alongside the Child and His mother and entered into the land of Yisrael.
2.22: But when he heard that Archelaos reigned over I the land of Yehudah in place of his father Herodes, he was afraid to go there. And being warned in a dream, he departed for the regions of Galil,
2.23: and came and resided in a city called Natzeret, that it might be fulfilled what was spoken through the Prophets, " He shall be called a Natzrati. "

3.1: Now in those days Yochanan the Immerser came, proclaiming in the wilderness of Yehudah, saying,
3.2: " Repent, for the Kingdom of Heaven has drawn near. "
3.3: For this is the one spoken of by Yeshayahu the prophet, saying, " THE VOICE OF ONE CRYING IN THE WILDERNESS, 'MAKE READY THE WAY OF ADONAI, MAKE HIS PATHS STRAIGHT! ' "
3.4: Now Yochanan himself had a garment of camel’s hair, and a leather belt around his waist; and his nourishment was locusts and wild honey.
3.5: Then Yerushalayim was going out to him, and all Yehudah, and all the district around the Yarden;
3.6: and they were being immersed by him in the Yarden River, as they confessed their sins.
3.7: But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming for immersion, he said to them, " Offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?
3.8: " Therefore, bring forth fruit worthy of repentance,
3.9: " and do not think that you can say to yourselves, 'We have a father, Avraham. ' For I say to you that God has the power to raise up children to Avraham out of these stones.
3.10: " Already the axe is even laid at the root of the trees; every tree therefore that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
3.11: " As for me, I immerse you with water for repentance. But He Who is coming after me is mightier than I, Whose sandals I am not fit to remove. He will immerse I some of you with the Holy Spirit, and I others of you with fire,
3.12: " and His winnowing fork is in His hand, and He will thoroughly cleanse His threshing floor. And He will gather His wheat into the barn, but He will burn up the chaff with inextinguishable fire. "
3.13: Then Yeshua arrived from Galil at the Yarden unto Yochanan to be immersed by him.
3.14: But Yochanan tried to prevent Him, saying, " I have need to be immersed by You, and do You come to me? "
3.15: But Yeshua answering said to him, " Permit it now, for in this way it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness. " Then he permitted Him.
3.16: And after being immersed, Yeshua went up immediately from the water; and behold, the Heavens were opened, and He saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove, coming upon Him.
3.17: And behold, a voice out of the Heavens, saying, " This is My beloved Son, in Whom I am well - pleased. "

4.1: Then Yeshua was led up to the wilderness by the Spirit, to be tempted by the Devil,
4.2: and having fasted forty days and forty nights, He then became hungry.
4.3: And the Tempter came and said to Him, " If You are the Son of God, speak that these stones become bread. "
4.4: But He answered and said, " It is written, 'MAN SHALL NOT LIVE BY BREAD ALONE, BUT ON EVERY WORD THAT PROCEEDS OUT OF THE MOUTH OF GOD. ' "
4.5: Then the Devil took Him alongside into the holy city, and he had Him stand on the pinnacle of the Temple,
4.6: and said to Him, " If You are the Son of God, throw Yourself down. For it is written, 'HE SHALL GIVE HIS ANGELS CHARGE CONCERNING YOU'; and 'THEY SHALL BEAR YOU ON I their HANDS LEST YOU STRIKE YOUR FOOT AGAINST A STONE. ' "
4.7: Yeshua said to him, " Again, it is written, 'YOU SHALL NOT PUT ADONAI YOUR GOD TO THE TEST. ' "
4.8: Again, the Devil took Him alongside to a very high mountain, and showed Him all the kingdoms of the world, and their glory.
4.9: And he said to Him, " I will give you all these things if You will fall down and worship me. "
4.10: Then Yeshua said to him, " Begone, HaSatan! For it is written, 'YOU SHALL WORSHIP ADONAI YOUR GOD AND SERVE HIM ONLY. ' "
4.11: Then the Devil left Him, and behold, angels came and were ministering to Him.
4.12: Now when He heard that Yochanan had been delivered up I into custody, He withdrew into Galil;
4.13: and leaving Natzeret, He came and settled in K’far - Nachum, which is by the sea, in the regions of Zevulun and Naftali,
4.14: that it might be fulfilled what was spoken through Yeshayahu the prophet, saying,
4.15: " THE LAND OF ZEVULUN AND THE LAND OF NAFTALI, BY THE WAY OF THE SEA, BEYOND THE YARDEN, GALIL OF THE NATIONS - -
4.16: " THE PEOPLE SITTING IN DARKNESS SAW A GREAT LIGHT, AND TO THOSE SITTING IN THE REGION AND SHADOW OF DEATH, UPON THEM A LIGHT AROSE. "
4.17: From that time Yeshua began to proclaim and say, " Repent, for the Kingdom of Heaven has drawn near! "
4.18: And walking by the Sea of Galil, He saw two brothers, Shimon who was called Petros, and Andreas his brother, casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
4.19: And He said to them, " Follow Me, and I will make you fishers of men. "
4.20: And they immediately left the nets, and followed Him.
4.21: And going on from there He saw two other brothers, Ya’akov I the son of Zavdai, and Yochanan his brother, in the boat with Zavdai their father, mending their nets. And He called them,
4.22: and they immediately left the boat and their father and followed Him.
4.23: And I He was going about in all Galil, teaching in their synagogues, and proclaiming the good news of the Kingdom, and healing every disease and every kind of sickness among the people.
4.24: And the news of Him went out into all Suria. And they brought to Him all those having illness, suffering from various diseases and torments, demoniacs, epileptics, paralytics, and He healed them.
4.25: And great crowds followed Him from Galil and Dekapolis and Yerushalayim and I the land of Yehudah and beyond the Yarden.

5.1: And when He saw the crowds, He went up on the mount, and after He sat down, His disciples came to Him.
5.2: And opening His mouth, He taught them, saying:
5.3: " Blessed are the poor in spirit! For theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.
5.4: " Blessed are they who mourn! For they shall be comforted.
5.5: " Blessed are the meek! For they shall inherit the Earth.
5.6: " Blessed are they who hunger and thirst for righteousness! For they will be fed.
5.7: " Blessed are the merciful! For they shall obtain mercy.
5.8: " Blessed are the pure in heart! For they shall see God.
5.9: " Blessed are the peacemakers! For they shall be called sons of God.
5.10: " Blessed are they who have been persecuted for the sake of righteousness! For theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.
5.11: " Blessed are you when I men insult you, and persecute you, and say all kinds of evil against you falsely, on account of Me.
5.12: " Rejoice and be glad, for your reward in Heaven is great. For in this way they persecuted the prophets who were before you.
5.13: " You are the salt of the Earth, but if the salt becomes tasteless, how will it be made salty I again? For it has strength for nothing any more, but to be thrown out, and to be trampled under by men.
5.14: " You are the light of the world. A city situated on a mountain cannot be hidden.
5.15: " Nor do they take a lamp and put it under a peck - measure, but on a lampstand, and it gives light to all who are in the house.
5.16: " So let your light shine before men, so that they may see your good works, and may glorify your Father Who is in Heaven.
5.17: " Do not think that I came to abolish the Torah or the Prophets; I did not come to abolish, but to fulfill.
5.18: " Truly I say to you, until Heaven and Earth pass away, not the smallest letter or stroke shall pass away from the Torah, until all is accomplished.
5.19: " Whoever then shall break one of these commandments, the least, and shall teach others to do so, he shall be called least in the Kingdom of Heaven. But whoever keeps and teaches I them, he shall be called great in the Kingdom of Heaven.
5.20: " For I say to you, that unless your righteousness surpasses I that of the scribes and Pharisees, you shall by no means enter into the Kingdom of Heaven.
5.21: " You have heard that it was said to the ancients: 'You shall not commit murder' and 'Whoever commits murder shall be guilty to judgment. '
5.22: " But I say to you, everyone who is angry with his brother without a cause shall be guilty to judgment. And whoever says to his brother, ‘Raca, ’ shall be guilty before the Sanhedrin; but whoever says 'You fool' shall be guilty I enough to be thrown into Gey - Hinnom.
5.23: " Therefore, if you are presenting your offering at the altar, and there remember that your brother has something against you,
5.24: " leave your offering there before the altar, and go. First be reconciled to your brother, and then come and present your offering.
5.25: " Be well - minded with your opponent quickly, while you are with him on the road, in order that your opponent may not deliver you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer, and you be thrown into prison.
5.26: " Truly I say to you, in no way shall you come out from there unless you pay the last kodrantes.
5.27: " You have heard that it was said to the ancients: 'YOU SHALL NOT COMMIT ADULTERY. '
5.28: " But I say to you, everyone who looks on a woman to lust for her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
5.29: " And if your right eye makes you stumble, tear it out and throw it from you. For it is profitable for you that one of your members perish, then for your whole body to be thrown into Gey - Hinnom.
5.30: " And if your right hand makes you stumble, cut it off and throw it from you. For it is profitable that one of your members perish, then for your whole body to go into Gey - Hinnom.
5.31: " It was also said, 'WHOEVER SENDS HIS WIFE AWAY, LET HIM GIVE HER A BILL OF DIVORCE. '
5.32: " But I say to you, that everyone who divorces his wife, except for the cause of fornication, makes her commit adultery. And whoever shall marry the one put away commits adultery.
5.33: " Again, you have heard that it was said to the ancients: 'YOU SHALL NOT MAKE FALSE OATHS, BUT YOU SHALL MAKE YOUR OATHS TO ADONAI. '
5.34: " But I say to you, make no oath at all, neither by Heaven, for it is the throne of God,
5.35: " nor by the Earth, because it is the footstool of His feet, nor by Yerushalayim, because it is the city of the great King.
5.36: " Nor shall you swear by your head, because you do not have the power to make one hair white or black.
5.37: " But let your statement be, 'Yes, yes' I or 'No, no. ' For whatever is more than these is of evil.
5.38: " You have heard that it was said: 'AN EYE FOR AN EYE, AND A TOOTH FOR A TOOTH. '
5.39: " But I say to you, do not resist the evil, but whoever strikes you on the right cheek, turn the other to him also.
5.40: " And if anyone wants to sue you and take your inner garment, let him have your coat also.
5.41: " And whoever shall impress you to go one mile, go two with him.
5.42: " To he who is asking of you be giving, and he who is wishing to borrow from you, do not turn I him away.
5.43: " You have heard that it was said: 'You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy. '
5.44: " But I say to you, love your enemies, and pray for those who persecute you,
5.45: " so that you may be sons of your Father in Heaven, because He cause His sun to rise on I the evil and I the good, and sends rain on I the righteous and I the unrighteous.
5.46: " For if you love those loving you, what reward do you have? Do not the tax - collectors do the same?
5.47: " And if you greet your brethren only, what do you do more? Do not even I those of the nations do the same?
5.48: " Therefore you be brought to goal, just as your Heavenly Father has been at the goal.

6.1: " Beware of practicing your righteousness before men to be noticed by them. Otherwise you have no reward with your Father Who is in Heaven.
6.2: " When therefore you do give alms, do not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, so that they may be glorified by men. Truly I say to you, that they have their reward.
6.3: " But when you do give alms, do not let your left hand know what your right hand does,
6.4: " so that your alms may be in secret, and your Father seeing in secret will reward you.
6.5: " And when you pray, you shall not be as the hypocrites. For they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and in the corners of the open streets, in order to be seen of men. Truly I say to you, they have their reward in full.
6.6: " But you, when you pray, go into your inner room. And when you have shut the door, pray to your Father in secret, and your Father Who sees in secret will reward you.
6.7: " But when you pray, do not use meaningless babble, as the nations do, for they suppose that they will be heard for their many words.
6.8: " Therefore do not be like them, for your Father knows what things you have need of before you ask Him.
6.9: " Pray, therefore, in this way: 'Our Father Who is in Heaven, hallowed be Your name.
6.10: " Let Your Kingdom come, I and Your Will be done on Earth as it is in Heaven.
6.11: " Give us this day our daily bread,
6.12: " and forgive us our debts as we also forgive our debtors.
6.13: " And do not lead us into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. I For Your’s is the Kingdom, and the power, and the glory, forever. Amein.
6.14: " For if you forgive men for their trespasses, your Heavenly Father will also forgive you.
6.15: " But if you will not forgive men, then your Father will not forgive your trespasses.
6.16: " And when you fast, do not put on a sullen countenance as the hypocrites, for they disfigure their faces so that they may appear to men to be fasting. Truly I say to you, they have their reward in full.
6.17: " But you, when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face,
6.18: " so as not to appear to men to be fasting, but to your Father in secret, and your Father Who sees in secret will reward you.
6.19: " Do not store up for yourselves treasures upon Earth, where moth and rust disfigure, and where thieves break in and steal.
6.20: " But store up for yourselves treasures in Heaven, where neither moth nor rust disfigure, and where thieves do not break in or steal.
6.21: " For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
6.22: " The lamp of the body is the eye. If therefore your eye is clear, your whole body will be full of light.
6.23: " But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in you is darkness, how great is the darkness!
6.24: " No one has the power to serve two lords. For either he will hate the one, and he will love the other; or he will cleave to one, and he will despise the other. You cannot serve I both God and mammon.
6.25: " Because of this, I say to you, do not be anxious for your life, what you eat or what you drink; nor for your body, I or what you put on. Is not the soul more than food, and the body than clothing?
6.26: " Look at the birds of the air, that they do not sow, nor do they reap, nor gather into barns, and I yet your Heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not worth more than they?
6.27: " And which of you by being anxious can add one cubit to his stature?
6.28: " And why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they neither toil nor do they spin.
6.29: " But I say to you that even Shlomo in all his glory did not array himself like one of these.
6.30: " If God so clothes the grass of the field, which is I alive today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, I will He not much more I do so for you, O you of little faith?
6.31: " Then do not be anxious, saying, 'What shall we eat? ' or 'What shall we drink' or 'With what shall we clothe ourselves? '
6.32: " For after all these things the nations seek. For your Heavenly Father knows that you have need of all these things.
6.33: " But seek first His Kingdom and His righteousness, and all these things shall be added to you.
6.34: " Therefore do not be anxious for tomorrow; for tomorrow shall be anxious for its own things. Each day has enough evil of itself.

7.1: " Do not judge, that you may not be judged,
7.2: " for with whatever judgment you judge, you will be judged; and by your standard of measure, it will be measured to you.
7.3: " Why do you look on the twig that I is in your brother’s eye, but do not see the log that is in your own eye?
7.4: " Or how will you say to your brother, 'Allow me to cast out the twig from your eye, ' and behold, the log is in your own eye?
7.5: " Hypocrite, first cast the log out of your eye, and then you will see clearly to cast the twig out of your brother’s eye.
7.6: " Do not give what is holy to dogs, and do not throw your pearls before pigs, lest they trample them under their feet, and I then turn and tear you to pieces.
7.7: " Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
7.8: " For everyone who asks, receives; and he who seeks finds; and to him who knocks it shall be opened.
7.9: " Or what man is there among you, if his son shall ask him for a loaf I of bread, will give him a stone?
7.10: " Or if he shall ask for a fish, he will not give him a snake, will he?
7.11: " If you then, being evil, know to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father Who is in Heaven give good things to those that ask Him?
7.12: " Therefore, however you want people to treat you, so treat them, for this is the Torah and the Prophets.
7.13: " Enter through the narrow gate; for the gate is wide, and the road is broad that leads to perdition, and many are the ones who go through it.
7.14: " For the gate is small, and the road is narrow that leads to life, and few are the ones who find it.
7.15: " But beware of the false prophets who come to you in sheep’s clothing, for inside they are ravenous wolves.
7.16: " From their fruits you shall know them. Are grapes gathered from thorns, or figs from thistles?
7.17: " Even so, every good tree yields beautiful fruit; but the bad tree yields evil fruit.
7.18: " A good tree does not have the power to produce evil fruit, nor can a bad tree produce beautiful fruit.
7.19: " Every tree that does not yield beautiful fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
7.20: " So then, surely from their fruits you shall know them.
7.21: " Not everyone who says to Me, 'Lord, Lord, ' will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven; but he who does the will of My Father Who is in Heaven.
7.22: " Many will say to Me on that day, 'Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in Your name, and in Your name cast out demons, and in Your name perform many miracles? '
7.23: " And then I will declare to them, 'I never knew you; depart from Me, you who are working lawlessness. '
7.24: " Therefore, everyone who hears these words of Mine, and does them, I will compare him to a wise man who built his house on the rock.
7.25: " And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat against that house; but it did not fall, for it had its foundation on the rock.
7.26: " And everyone who hears these words of Mine, and who does not do them, I he shall be compared to a foolish man who built his house on the sand.
7.27: " And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat against that house; and it fell, and great was its fall. "
7.28: And it happened, when Yeshua had finished these words, the crowds were astonished at His teaching;
7.29: for He was teaching them as I One having authority, and not as the scribes.

8.1: And when He had come down from the mount, great crowds followed Him.
8.2: And behold, a leper came to Him, and bowed down to Him, saying, " Lord, if You will, You can cleanse me. "
8.3: And He stretched out His hand and touched him, saying, " I am willing, be cleansed! " And immediately his leprosy was cleansed.
8.4: And Yeshua said to him, " See that you tell no one; but go, show yourself to the priest, and present the offering which Moshe commanded, for a testimony to them. "
8.5: And when He had entered K’far - Nachum, a centurion came to Him, begging Him,
8.6: and saying, " Lord, my servant is lying paralyzed in the house, suffering grievous torments. "
8.7: And He said to him, " I will come and heal him. "
8.8: But the centurion answered and said, " Lord, I am not worthy that You should enter under my roof; but only speak a word, and my servant will be healed.
8.9: " For I am also a man under authority, having soldiers under me; and I say to this one, 'Go! ' and he goes, and to another 'Come! ' and he comes, and to my slave 'Do this! ' and he does. "
8.10: Now when Yeshua heard I this, He marveled, and said to those who were following, " Truly I say to you, I have not found such great faith with anyone in Yisrael.
8.11: " And I say to you, that many shall come from the east and west, and will recline with Avraham and Yitzchak and Ya’akov in the Kingdom of Heaven;
8.12: " but the sons of the Kingdom shall be cast out into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth. "
8.13: And Yeshua said to the centurion, " Go, and as you have believed, so let it be done to you. " And his servant was healed in that hour.
8.14: And when Yeshua had come to the house of Petros, He saw his mother - in - law lying in bed with a fever.
8.15: And He touched her hand, and the fever left her; and she arose and served them.
8.16: And when evening had come, they brought to Him many who were demon - possessed; and He cast out the spirits with a word, and healed all who were ill
8.17: in order that what was spoken of through Yeshayahu the prophet might be fulfilled, saying, " HE HIMSELF TOOK OUR INFIRMITIES, AND BORE OUR DISEASES. "
8.18: Now when Yeshua saw crowds around Him, He gave orders to depart to the other side.
8.19: And a certain scribe came and said to Him, " Teacher, I will follow You wherever you may go. "
8.20: And Yeshua said to him, " The foxes have holes and the birds of the air nests; but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay His head. "
8.21: And another of the disciples said to Him, " Lord, allow me first to depart and bury my father. "
8.22: But Yeshua said to him, " Follow Me, and let the dead bury their own dead. "
8.23: And when He entered into the boat, His disciples followed Him.
8.24: And behold, there arose a great storm on the sea, so that the boat was being covered by the waves; but He Himself was asleep.
8.25: And they went and woke Him, saying, " Save I us, Lord! We are perishing! "
8.26: And He said to them, " Why are you afraid, you men of little faith? " Then He arose and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.
8.27: And the men marveled, saying, " What sort of Man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey Him? "
8.28: And when he had come to the other side, into the country of the Gadarenes, two who were demon - possessed met Him as they were coming out of the tombs. I They were so exceedingly violent that no one was able to pass through that road.
8.29: And behold, they screamed out, saying, " What have You to do with us, O Son of God? Have you come here to torment us before the time? "
8.30: Now there was at a distance a herd of many pigs feeding,
8.31: and the demons begged Him, saying, " If You cast us out, send us away into the herd of pigs. "
8.32: And He said to them, " Begone! " And they came out and went into the pigs. And, behold, the whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea and perished in the waters.
8.33: And the herdsmen fled, and went into the city and reported everything, and what I had happened to the demoniacs.
8.34: And behold, the whole city came out to meet Yeshua; and when they saw Him, they begged that I He might leave their region.

9.1: And getting into a boat, He crossed over and came to His own city.
9.2: And behold, they brought to Him a paralytic lying on a cot; and Yeshua seeing their faith said to the paralytic, " Take courage, My son, your sins are forgiven. "
9.3: And behold, some of the scribes said to themselves, " This I Oneblasphemes! "
9.4: And Yeshua, knowing their thoughts, said, " Why do you think evil in your hearts?
9.5: " For which is easier, to say, 'Your sins are forgiven, ' or to say, 'Rise and walk'?
9.6: " But in order that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on Earth to forgive sins " - - He then said to the paralytic - - " Rise, take up your bed and go home. "
9.7: And he rose and went to his house.
9.8: But when the crowds saw I this, they were filled with awe, and glorified God, Who had given such authority to men.
9.9: And as Yeshua passed on from there, He saw a man called Mattityahu sitting at the tax office; and He said to him, " Follow Me. " And he rose and followed Him.
9.10: And it happened as He reclined in the house, behold, many tax - collectors and sinners came and were reclining with Yeshua and His disciples.
9.11: And when the Pharisees saw I this, they said to His disciples, " Why does your Teacher eat with tax - collectors and sinners? "
9.12: But when He heard this, He said, " Those who are healthy have no need of a physician, but those who are sick. "
9.13: " But go and learn what I thismeans, 'I DESIRE MERCY, AND NOT SACRIFICE. ' For I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners. "
9.14: Then the disciples of Yochanan came to Him, saying, " Why do we and the Pharisees fast, but your disciples do not fast? "
9.15: And Yeshua said to them, " Can the attendants of the bridegroom mourn as long as the bridegroom is with them? But the days will come when the bridegroom will have been taken away from them; and then they will fast.
9.16: " But no one puts a patch of new cloth onto an old garment; for the patch tears away from the garment, and a worse tear is made.
9.17: " Neither is new wine put into old wineskins; otherwise, the wineskins burst, and the wine is spilled, and the wineskins are ruined. But they put new wine into fresh wineskins, and both are preserved. "
9.18: While He was saying these things to them, behold, an official came in and bowed before Him, saying, " My daughter has just died; but come and lay Your hand on her and she will live. "
9.19: And Yeshua rose and followed him, with His disciples.
9.20: And behold, a woman who had been suffering from a hemorrhage for twelve years, came up behind Him and touched the tzit - tzit of His garment;
9.21: for she was saying to herself, " If I only touch His garment, I will be healed. "
9.22: But Yeshua turning and seeing her, said, " Take courage, daughter; your faith has healed you. " And the woman was healed from that hour.
9.23: And when Yeshua came into the official’s house, and saw the flute players, and the crowds in noisy disorder,
9.24: He said, " Depart, for the little girl has not died, but she sleeps. " And they laughed at Him.
9.25: But when the crowds had been put outside, He went in and took hold of her hand, and the girl arose.
9.26: And this report went out into all that land.
9.27: And as Yeshua passed on from there, two blind men followed Him, crying and saying, " Have mercy on us, Son of Daveed! "
9.28: And after He had entered the house, the blind men came up to Him, and Yeshua said to them, " Do you believe that I am able to do this? " They said to Him, " Yes, Lord. "
9.29: Then He touched their eyes, saying, " According to your faith will it be done to you. "
9.30: And their eyes were opened. And Yeshua charged them, " See that no one knows I about this! "
9.31: But they went out, and spread the news about Him in all that land.
9.32: And as they were going out, behold, a dumb - man I who wasdemon possessed was brought to Him.
9.33: And after the demon had been cast out, the dumb man spoke. And the crowds marveled, saying, " Never was anything like this seen in Yisrael. "
9.34: But the Pharisees were saying, " He casts out demons by the prince of demons. "
9.35: And Yeshua went about all the cities and villages, teaching in their synagogues, and proclaiming the good news of the Kingdom, and healing every kind of disease and every kind of sickness.
9.36: And seeing the crowds, He felt compassion for them, because they were distressed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.
9.37: Then He said to His disciples, " The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few.
9.38: " Therefore beseech the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into His harvest. "

10.1: And having summoned His twelve disciples, He gave them authority over unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal every kind of disease and every kind of sickness.
10.2: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these: first, Shimon, who is called Petros, and Andreas his brother; Ya’akov the son of Zavdai, and Yochanan his brother;
10.3: Philippos and Bar - Talmai; Toma and Mattityahu the tax - collector; Ya’akov the son of Chalfai; and Taddai;
10.4: Shimon the Zealot, and Yehudah I fromK’riot, who delivered Him up.
10.5: These twelve Yeshua sent out, charging them, saying " Do not go in I themanner of the nations, and do not enter I anycity of the Shomronim;
10.6: " but go rather to the lost sheep of the House of Yisrael.
10.7: " And proclaim as you go, saying, 'The Kingdom of Heaven is at hand. '
10.8: " Heal I thesick, raise I thedead, cleanse I thelepers, cast out demons. You received without paying, give without pay.
10.9: " Do not acquire gold, nor silver, nor copper for your money belts,
10.10: " nor a bag for I yourjourney, nor two tunics, nor two sandals, nor a staff; for the laborer is worthy of his nourishment.
10.11: " And into whatever city or village you enter, inquire who is worthy in it; and remain there until you go away.
10.12: " And as you enter the house, greet it.
10.13: " And if the house is worthy, let your peace come upon it; but if it is not worthy, let your peace return to you.
10.14: " And whoever will not receive you, nor will hear your words, as you go out of that house or city, shake off the dust from your feet.
10.15: " Truly, I say to you, it will be more tolerable for the land of S’dom and ‘Amora on the day of judgment than for that city.
10.16: " Behold, I send you out as sheep in the middle of wolves; therefore be shrewd as serpents, and innocent as doves.
10.17: " But beware of men; for they will deliver you to sanhedrins and scourge you in their synagogues.
10.18: " And you will even be brought before governors and kings for My sake, for a testimony to them and to the nations.
10.19: " But when they deliver you up, do not be anxious about how or what you are to speak; for what you are to speak will be given to you in that hour.
10.20: " For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father Who speaks in you.
10.21: " And brother will deliver up brother to death, and a father I hischild. And children will rise up against parents, and will put them to death.
10.22: " And you will be hated by all on account of My name. But the I oneenduring to the end will be saved.
10.23: " But whenever they persecute you in this city, flee to the next; for truly I say to you, you will not have completed your goal I of going throughthe cities of Yisrael until the Son of Man comes.
10.24: " A disciple is not above his teacher, nor a slave above his lord.
10.25: " It is enough for the disciple to be like his teacher, and the slave like his lord. If they have called the master of the house Ba’al - zibbul, how much more the members of his household!
10.26: " Therefore do not fear them, for there is nothing covered that will not be uncovered, or hidden that will not be known.
10.27: " What I say to you in the darkness, speak in the light; and what you hear in I yourear, proclaim upon the roofs.
10.28: " And do not fear those who have the power to kill the body, but do not have the power to kill the soul; but rather fear Him Who has the power to utterly ruin both body and soul in Gey - Hinnom.
10.29: " Are not two sparrows sold for an assarion? And not one of them will fall to the ground apart from your Father.
10.30: " But even the hairs of your head are all numbered.
10.31: " Therefore, fear not; you are of more value than many sparrows.
10.32: " Everyone therefore who shall acknowledge Me before men, I also will acknowledge before My Father Who is in Heaven.
10.33: " But whoever shall deny Me before Men, I will also deny Him before My Father Who is in Heaven.
10.34: " Do not think that I have come to bring peace on the Earth; I did not come to bring peace, but a sword.
10.35: " For I have come to SET A MAN AGAINST HIS FATHER, AND A DAUGHTER AGAINST HER MOTHER, AND A DAUGHTER - IN - LAW AGAINST HER MOTHER IN LAW;
10.36: " and A MAN'S ENEMIES WILL BE THOSE OF HIS OWN HOUSEHOLD.
10.37: " He who loves I hisfather and mother more than Me is not worthy of Me; and he who loves I hisson or daughter more than Me is not worthy of Me.
10.38: " And he who does not take his cross and follow after Me is not worthy of Me.
10.39: " He who has found his life shall lose it, and he who has lost his life for My sake shall find it.
10.40: " He who receives you receives Me, and he who receives Me receives Him Who sent Me.
10.41: " He who receives a prophet in I thename of a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward; and he who receives a righteous man in the name of a righteous man will receive a righteous man’s reward.
10.42: " And whoever in the name of a disciple gives to one of these little ones even a cup of cold water to drink, truly I say to you he shall not loose his reward.

11.1: And it came about that when Yeshua had finished instructing His twelve disciples, He went on from there to teach and proclaim in their cities.
11.2: Now when Yochanan heard in prison about the works of Messiah, he sent two of his disciples,
11.3: and said to Him, " Are you the Coming One, or shall we look for another?
11.4: And Yeshua answered and said to them, " Go, and report to Yochanan what you hear and see:
11.5: " theBLIND RECOVER SIGHT, and I thelame walk, I thelepers are cleansed, and I thedeaf hear, I thedead are raised, and I thepoor have GOOD NEWS PROCLAIMED to them.
11.6: " And blessed is he who shall not be offended in Me. "
11.7: And as they went away, Yeshua began to speak to the crowds concerning Yochanan, " What did you go out into the wilderness to look upon? A reed shaken by the wind?
11.8: " But what did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft I clothing? Behold, those who wear soft I clothingare in kings’ houses.
11.9: " But why then did you go out? Yes, I tell you, and one who is more than a prophet.
11.10: " This is the one concerning whom it is written, 'BEHOLD, I SEND MY MESSENGER BEFORE YOUR FACE, WHO SHALL PREPARE YOUR WAY BEFORE YOU. '
11.11: " Truly, I say to you, among those born of women there has not arisen one greater than Yochanan the Immerser; yet he who is least in the Kingdom of Heaven is greater than he.
11.12: " And from the days of Yochanan the Immerser until now the Kingdom of Heaven suffers violence, and the violent seize it.
11.13: " For all the Prophets and the Torah prophesied until Yochanan.
11.14: " And if you are willing to accept, he himself is Eliyahu who was to come.
11.15: " He who has ears to hear, let him hear.
11.16: " But to what shall I compare this generation? It is like children sitting in the market places, which call out to the others,
11.17: " and say, 'We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we lamented, and you did not mourn. '
11.18: " For Yochanan came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, 'He has a demon! '
11.19: " The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, 'Behold, a gluttonous man and a drunkard, a friend of tax - collectors and sinners! ' Yet wisdom is justified by her deeds. "
11.20: Then He began to reproach the cities in which most of His miracles had been done, because they did not repent.
11.21: " Woe to you, Korazin! Woe to you, Beit - Tzaidah! For if the miracles had occurred in Tzor and Tzidon which occurred in you, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
11.22: " Nevertheless, I tell you it shall be more tolerable for Tzor and Tzidon on I theday of judgment than for you.
11.23: " And you, K’far - Nachum, will you be exalted to Heaven? You shall be brought down to Sheol; for if the miracles had occurred in S’dom which occurred in you, it would have remained until this day.
11.24: " Nevertheless I say to you that it shall be more tolerable for the land of S’dom on I theday of judgment than for you. "
11.25: At that time Yeshua answered and said, " I praise You, Father, Lord of Heaven and Earth, that you hid these things from wise and intelligent I ones, and revealed them to babes.
11.26: " Yes, Father, for thus it was well - pleasing in Your sight.
11.27: " All things have been committed to Me by My Father; and no one knows the Son except the Father; nor does anyone know the Father, except the Son, and anyone to whom the Son wishes to reveal I Him.
11.28: " Come to Me, all who are weary and heavy - laden, and I will give you rest.
11.29: " Take up My yoke upon you, and learn from Me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and YOU SHALL FIND REST FOR YOUR SOULS.
11.30: " For My yoke is easy, and My burden is light. "

12.1: At that season Yeshua went on the Shabbat through the grainfields, and His disciples became hungry and began to pluck the heads I of grainand eat.
12.2: But when the Pharisees saw it, they said to Him, " Behold, Your disciples do what is not permitted to do on a Shabbat. "
12.3: But He said to them, " Have you not read what Daveed did, when he was hungry, and those who were with him:
12.4: " how he entered the House of God, and they ate the consecrated bread, which was not permitted for him to eat, nor for those who were with him, but for the priests alone?
12.5: " Or have you not read in the Torah how on the Shabbat the priests in the Temple profane the Shabbat, and are innocent?
12.6: " But I say to you that something greater than the Temple is here.
12.7: " But if you had known what this means, 'I DESIRE MERCY, AND NOT SACRIFICE, ' you would have not condemned the innocent.
12.8: " For the Son of Man is Lord of the Shabbat. "
12.9: And departing from there, He went into their synagogue.
12.10: And behold, I there wasa man with a withered hand. And they asked Him, " Is it permitted to heal on the Shabbat? " - - in order that they might accuse Him.
12.11: And He said to them, " What man shall there be among you, if he has one sheep and it falls into a pit on the Shabbat, will he not take hold of it, and lift it out?
12.12: " Of how much more value then is a man than a sheep! So then, it is permitted to do good on the Shabbat. "
12.13: Then He said to the man, " Stretch out your hand. " And the man stretched it out, and it was restored, healthy like the other.
12.14: But the Pharisees went out, and counseled together against Him, how they might utterly ruin Him.
12.15: But Yeshua, having known I this, withdrew from there. And many followed them, and He healed them all,
12.16: and warned them not to make Him known,
12.17: in order that what was spoken through Yeshayahu the prophet might be fulfilled, saying,
12.18: " BEHOLD, MY SERVANT WHOM I HAVE CHOSEN; MY BELOVED IN WHOM MY SOUL IS WELL - PLEASED. I WILL PUT MY SPIRIT UPON HIM, AND HE SHALL ANNOUNCE JUDGMENT TO THE NATIONS.
12.19: " HE WILL NOT QUARREL NOR CRY OUT, NOR WILL ANYONE HEAR HIS VOICE IN THE STREETS;
12.20: " A BATTERED REED HE WILL NOT BREAK, AND A SMOLDERING WICK HE WILL NOT PUT OUT, UNTIL HE BRINGS FORTH JUDGMENT TO VICTORY.
12.21: " AND IN HIS NAME THE NATIONS WILL HOPE. "
12.22: Then there was brought to him a demon - possessed man, blind and dumb, and He healed Him, so that the dumb man spoke and saw.
12.23: And all the crowds were amazed, and said, " Can this be the Son of Daveed? "
12.24: But when the Pharisees heard it, they said, " This man casts out demons only by Ba’al - zibbul, the ruler of the demons. "
12.25: And knowing their thoughts He said to them, " Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste; and every city or house divided against itself shall not stand.
12.26: " And if HaSatan casts out HaSatan, he is divided against himself; how then shall his kingdom stand?
12.27: " And if I by Ba’al - zibbul cast out demons, by whom do your sons cast them out? Consequently they shall be your judges.
12.28: " But if I cast out demons by the Spirit of God, then the Kingdom of God has come upon you.
12.29: " Or how can anyone enter the strong man’s house and carry off his property, unless he first binds the strong I man? And then he will plunder his house.
12.30: " He who is not with Me is against Me; and he who does not gather with Me scatters.
12.31: " Therefore, I say to you, every sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven to men, but blasphemy against the Spirit shall not be forgiven.
12.32: " And whoever shall speak a word against the Son of Man, it shall be forgiven to him; but whoever shall speak against the Holy Spirit, it shall not be forgiven to him, either in this age or in the I ageto come.
12.33: " Either make the tree good, and its fruit good; or make the tree bad, and its fruit bad; for the tree is known by its fruit.
12.34: " You offspring of vipers! How can you, being evil, speak what is good? For the mouth speaks out the abundance of the heart.
12.35: " The good man out of the good treasure of the heart brings forth what is good; and the evil man out of the evil treasure brings forth what is evil.
12.36: " And I say to you, that every idle word that men shall speak, they shall render account for it on the day of judgment.
12.37: " For by your words you shall be justified, and by your words you shall be condemned. "
12.38: Then some of the scribes and Pharisees answered Him, saying, " Teacher, we wish to see a sign from You. "
12.39: But He answered and said to them, " An evil and adulterous generation craves for a sign; but no sign shall be given to it but the sign of Yonah the prophet.
12.40: " for just as YONAH WAS THREE DAYS AND THREE NIGHTS IN THE STOMACH OF THE SEA MONSTER, so shall the Son of Man be three days and three nights in the heart of the Earth.
12.41: " The men of Nineveh shall stand up with this generation at the judgment, and shall condemn it because they repented at the proclamation of Yonah; and behold, something greater than Yonah is here.
12.42: " TheQueen of I theSouth shall rise up with this generation at the judgment and condemn it, because she came from the ends of the Earth to hear the wisdom of Shlomo; and behold, something greater than Shlomo is here.
12.43: " Now when the unclean spirit goes out of a man, it passes through waterless places, seeking rest, and finds none.
12.44: " Then it says, 'I will return to my house from which I came. ' And when it comes and finds it unoccupied, swept, and put in order,
12.45: " then it goes, and takes alongside itself seven other spirits more wicked than itself. And they enter in and live there; and the last state of that man becomes worse than the first. So shall it also be with this evil generation. "
12.46: While He was still speaking to the crowds, behold, His mother and brothers were standing outside, seeking to speak to Him.
12.47: And someone said to Him, " Behold, Your mother and Your brothers are standing outside seeking to speak with You. "
12.48: But He answered the one who was telling Him and said, " Who is My mother, and who are My brothers? "
12.49: And stretching out His hand toward His disciples, He said, " Behold, My mother and My brothers!
12.50: " For whoever does the will of My Father Who is in Heaven, he is My brother, and sister, and mother. "

13.1: On that day Yeshua went out of the house, and was sitting by the sea.
13.2: And great crowds gathered to Him, so that He got into a boat and sat down, and the whole crowd was standing on the beach.
13.3: And He spoke many things to them in parables, saying: " Behold, the sower went out to sow;
13.4: " and as he sowed, some I seedsfell along the road, and the birds came and devoured them.
13.5: " And others fell upon the rocky places, where they did not have much soil; and immediately they sprang up, because they had no depth of soil.
13.6: " But when the sun had risen they were scorched; and because they had no root they withered away.
13.7: " And others fell among the thorns, and the thorns came up and choked them.
13.8: " And others fell on the good soil, and yielded fruit, some a hundred fold, and some sixty, and some thirty.
13.9: " He who has ears, let him hear. "
13.10: And the disciples came and said to Him, " Why do you speak to them in parables? "
13.11: And He answered and said to them, " To you it has been granted to know the mysteries of the Kingdom of Heaven, but to them it has not been granted.
13.12: " For whoever has, to him will be given I more, and he shall have an abundance; but whoever does not have, even what he has shall be taken away from him.
13.13: " Therefore, I speak to them in parables; because while seeing they do not see, and while hearing they do not hear, nor do they understand.
13.14: " And in their case the prophecy of Yeshayahu is being fulfilled, which says, 'YOU WILL KEEP ON HEARING, BUT YOU WILL NEVER UNDERSTAND; AND YOU WILL KEEP ON SEEING, BUT WILL NEVER PERCEIVE. '
13.15: " FOR THE HEART OF THIS PEOPLE HAS BECOME DULL, AND WITH THEIR EYES THEY ARE HEAVY OF HEARING, AND THEY HAVE CLOSED THEIR EYES LEST THEY SHOULD PERCEIVE WITH THEIR EYES, AND HEAR WITH THEIR EARS, AND UNDERSTAND WITH THEIR HEART AND RETURN, AND I SHOULD HEAL THEM.
13.16: " But blessed are your eyes because they see; and your hears because they hear.
13.17: " For truly I say to you, that many prophets and righteous men earnestly desired to perceive what you see, and did not perceive; and to hear what you hear, and did not hear.
13.18: " Hear then the parable of the sower.
13.19: " When anyone hears the words of the Kingdom and does not understand, the evil I onecomes and snatches away what has been sown in his heart. This is the one on whom I seedwas sown along the road.
13.20: " And the one on whom I seedwas sown on the rocky places, this is the man who hears the word, and immediately receives it with joy;
13.21: " yet he has no root in himself, but I itis temporary, and when tribulation or persecution arises because of the word, immediately he is offended.
13.22: " And the one on whom I seedwas sown among the thorns, this is the man who hears the word, and the anxiety of this age and the deceitfulness of riches choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
13.23: " And the one on whom I seedwas sown on the good soil, this is the man who hears the word and understands it; who indeed bears fruit, and brings forth, some a hundredfold, and some sixty, and some thirty. "
13.24: He put before them another parable, saying, " The Kingdom of Heaven may be compared to a man who sowed good seed in his field;
13.25: " but while the men were sleeping, his enemy came and sowed tares also among the wheat, and went away.
13.26: " But when the herb sprang up and bore fruit, then the tares appeared also.
13.27: " And the slaves of the householder came and said to him, 'Lord, did you not sow good seed in your field? How then does it have tares? '
13.28: " And he said to them, 'An enemy has done this! ' And the slaves said to him, 'Do you wish us, then, to go and collect them up? '
13.29: " But he said, 'No; lest while you collect up the tares, you may root up the wheat with them.
13.30: " 'Allow both to grow together until the harvest; and in the time of the harvest I will say to the reapers, " First collect up the tares and bind them in bundles to burn them up; but gather the wheat into my barn. " ' "
13.31: He put before them another parable, saying, " The Kingdom of Heaven is like a mustard grain, which a man took and sowed in his field;
13.32: " and this is the smallest of all seeds; but when it is grown, it is greatest of the garden plants and becomes a tree, so that THE BIRDS OF the AIR come and NEST IN ITS BRANCHES. "
13.33: He spoke another parable to them, " The Kingdom of Heaven is like leaven, which a woman took, and hid in three measures of meal, until it was all leavened. "
13.34: All these things Yeshua spoke to the crowds in parables; and He did not speak to them without a parable,
13.35: so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying, " I WILL OPEN MY MOUTH IN PARABLES; I WILL UTTER THINGS THAT HAVE BEEN HIDDEN SINCE THE FOUNDATION OF THE WORLD. "
13.36: Then He left the crowds and went into the house. And His disciples came to Him, saying, " Explain to us the parable of the tares of the field. "
13.37: And He answered and said, " The One Who sows the good seed is the Son of Man,
13.38: " and the field is the world; and the good seed, these are sons of the Kingdom; and the tares are the sons of the evil I one;
13.39: " and the enemy who sowed them is the Devil, and the harvest is the consummation of the age; and the reapers are angels.
13.40: " Therefore just as the tares are collected up and burned with fire, so shall it be at the consummation of the age.
13.41: " The Son of Man will send forth His angels, and they will collect out of His Kingdom all stumbling blocks, and those who commit lawlessness,
13.42: " and will cast them into the furnace of fire; there men will be weeping and gnashing their teeth.
13.43: " Then the righteous will shine forth as the sun in the Kingdom of their Father. He who has ears, let him hear.
13.44: " The Kingdom of Heaven is like a treasure hidden in the field, which a man found and hid; and from joy over it he goes and sells all that he has, and buys that field.
13.45: " Again, the Kingdom of Heaven is like a merchant in search of fine pearls,
13.46: " and upon finding one pearl of precious value, he went and sold all that he had, and bought it.
13.47: " Again, the Kingdom of Heaven is like a dragnet cast into the sea, and gathering species of every kind;
13.48: " and when it was filled, they drew it up on the beach; and they sat down, and collected the good into containers, but the worthless they threw away.
13.49: " So it will be at the consummation of the age; the angels shall come out and separate the wicked from among the righteous,
13.50: " and will cast them into the furnace of fire; there men will be weeping and gnashing their teeth.
13.51: " Have you understood all these things? " They said to Him, " Yes. "
13.52: And He said to them, " Therefore every scribe who has been trained as a disciple of the Kingdom of Heaven is like a master of the house, who brings forth out of his treasure things renewed and old. "
13.53: And it came about that when Yeshua had finished these parables, He departed from there.
13.54: And coming to His home town, He taught them in their synagogue, so that they became astonished, and said, " Where I didthis Man I getthis wisdom, and miraculous powers?
13.55: " Is this not the craftsman’s son? Is not His mother called Miriam, and His brothers, Ya’akov and Yosef and Shimon and Yehudah?
13.56: " And His sisters, are they not all with us? Where then I didthis Man I getall these things? "
13.57: And they were offended by Him. But Yeshua said to them, " A prophet is not without honor except in his home country, and in his household. "
13.58: And He did not perform many miracles there because of their unbelief.

14.1: At that time Herodes the tetrarch heard the news about Yeshua,
14.2: and said to his servants, " This is Yochanan the Immerser, he has risen from the dead; and that is why miraculous powers are at work in him. "
14.3: For when Herodes had Yochanan seized, he bound him, and put him in prison on account of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philippos.
14.4: For Yochanan had been saying to him, " It is not permitted for you to have her. "
14.5: And although he wanted to put him to death, he feared the crowds, because they considered him a prophet.
14.6: But when Herodes’ birthday came, the daughter of Herodias danced in the middle of I the company, and pleased Herodes,
14.7: wherefore he promised with an oath to give her whatever she asked.
14.8: And having been prompted by her mother, she said, " Give me here upon a platter the head of Yochanan the Immerser. "
14.9: And he was distressed, but because of his oaths and his dinner guests, he commanded I itto be given.
14.10: And he sent and had Yochanan beheaded in the prison.
14.11: And his head was brought upon a platter and given to the girl; and she brought I itto her mother.
14.12: And his disciples came and took away the corpse and buried it; and they went and reported to Yeshua.
14.13: Now when Yeshua heard, He withdrew from there in a boat to a solitary place by Himself; and when the crowds heard, they followed Him on foot from the cities.
14.14: And when He went ashore, He saw a great crowd, and was moved with compassion for them, and healed their sick.
14.15: And when it was evening, the disciples came to Him, saying, " The place is desolate, and the hour is already past; so send the crowds away, that they may go into the villages and buy food for themselves. "
14.16: But Yeshua said to them, " They do not need to go away; you give them I foodto eat! "
14.17: And they said to Him, " We have nothing here except five loaves and two fish. "
14.18: And He said, " Bring them here to Me. "
14.19: And commanding the crowds to sit down on the grass, He took the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up toward Heaven, He blessed them, and breaking the loaves He gave them to His disciples, and the disciples I gave themto the crowds.
14.20: And they all ate and were fed. And they took up what was left over of the broken pieces, twelve full baskets.
14.21: And there were about five thousand men who ate, separately from I thewomen and children.
14.22: And immediately He made the disciples get into the boat, and go before Him to the other side, while He dismissed the crowds.
14.23: And after He had dismissed the crowds, He went up to the mountainside by Himself to pray; and when it was evening, He was there alone.
14.24: But the boat was already many stadia away from the land, tormented by the waves, for the wind was against it.
14.25: And in the forth watch of the night He came to them, walking on the sea.
14.26: And when the disciples saw Him walking on the sea, they were frightened, saying, " It is a phantasm! " And they cried out for fear.
14.27: But immediately Yeshua spoke to them, saying, " Take courage, I AM; do not be afraid. "
14.28: And Petros answered Him and said, " Lord, if it is You, command Me to come to You on the water. "
14.29: And He said, " Come! " And Petros got out of the boat, and walked on the water and came toward Yeshua.
14.30: But seeing the wind, he became afraid, and beginning to sink he cried out, saying, " Lord, save me! "
14.31: And immediately Yeshua stretched out His hand and took hold of him, and said to him, " O you of little faith, why did you doubt? "
14.32: And when they got into the boat, the wind ceased.
14.33: And those who were in the boat worshipped Him, saying, " Truly, You are the Son of God! "
14.34: And when they had crossed over, they came to land at Gionsar.
14.35: And when the men of that place recognized Him, they sent into all of that surrounding region I wordand brought to Him all who were sick;
14.36: and they begged Him that they might just touch the tzit - tzit of His garment; and as many touched I itwere cured.

15.1: Then I somePharisees and scribes came to Yeshua from Yerushalayim, saying,
15.2: " Why do Your disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? For they do not wash their hands when they eat bread.
15.3: And He answered and said to them, " And why do you also transgress the commandment of God on account of your tradition?
15.4: " For God said, 'HONOR YOUR FATHER AND MOTHER, ' and, 'HE WHO SPEAKS EVIL OF FATHER OR MOTHER, LET HIM SURELY BE PUT TO DEATH. '
15.5: " But you say, 'Whoever shall say to father or mother, " Anything of mine you might have been helped by has been given as an offering I to God, "
15.6: " 'he is not to honor his father or mother. ' And you invalidate the Word of God on account of your tradition.
15.7: " You hypocrites, rightly did Yeshayahu prophecy of you, saying,
15.8: " 'THIS PEOPLE HONORS ME WITH THEIR LIPS, BUT THEIR HEART IS FAR FROM ME.
15.9: " 'BUT IN VAIN THEY WORSHIP ME, TEACHING AS DOCTRINES THE INJUNCTIONS OF MEN. ' "
15.10: And after He called the crowd to Him, He said to them, " Hear, and understand.
15.11: " Not what enters into the mouth makes the man common, but what proceeds out of the mouth, this makes the man common. "
15.12: Then the disciples came and said to Him, " Do You know that the Pharisees were offended when they heard this word? "
15.13: But He answered and said, " Every plant which My Heavenly Father has not planted shall be rooted up.
15.14: " Let them alone; they are blind guides of the blind. And if a blind man guides a blind man, both will fall into a pit. "
15.15: And Petros answered and said to Him, " Explain the parable to us. "
15.16: And He said, " Are you also still without understanding?
15.17: " Do you not think that everything that goes into the mouth, and passes into the stomach, is cast out into the latrine?
15.18: " But the things that proceed out of a man come from the heart; and those make the man common.
15.19: " For out of the heart come evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, and slander.
15.20: " These are the things which make the man common; but to eat with unwashed hands does not make the man common. "
15.21: And Yeshua went away from there, and withdrew into the district of Tzor and Tzidon.
15.22: And behold, a Canaanite woman from that region came out and cried, " Have mercy on Me, O Lord, Son of Daveed; my daughter is badly demon - possessed. "
15.23: But He did not answer her a word. And His disciples came and kept asking Him, saying " Send her away, for she is crying after us. "
15.24: But He answered and said, " I was sent only to the lost sheep of the House of Yisrael. "
15.25: But she came and bowed down before Him, saying, " Lord, help me! "
15.26: And He answered and said, " It is not good to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs. "
15.27: But she said, " Yes Lord; but even the dogs eat on the crumbs which fall from their lord’s table. "
15.28: Then Yeshua answered and said to her, " O woman, your faith is great! Be it done for you as you wish. " And her daughter was healed at that hour.
15.29: And departing from there, Yeshua went along by the Sea of Galil, and having gone up to the mountainside, He was sitting there.
15.30: And great crowds came to Him, bringing with them lame, crippled, blind, dumb, and many others, and they laid them down at His feet; and He healed them,
15.31: so that the crowd marveled as they saw the dumb speaking, the crippled whole, and the lame walking, and the blind seeing; and they glorified the God of Yisrael.
15.32: And Yeshua called His disciples to Him, and said, " I feel compassion for the crowds, because they have remained with Me now three days and have nothing to eat; and I do not wish to send them away hungry, lest they faint on the road. "
15.33: And the disciples said to Him, " Where would we get so many loaves in I sucha desolate wilderness to feed such a great crowd? "
15.34: And Yeshua said to them, " How many loaves do you have? " And they said, " Seven, and a few small fish. "
15.35: And He directed the crowd to sit down on the ground;
15.36: and He took the seven loaves and the fish; and giving thanks He broke them and started giving them to the disciples, and the disciples I gave themto the crowds.
15.37: And they all ate and were fed; and they took up what was left over of the broken pieces, seven large baskets full.
15.38: And those who ate were four thousand men, separately from the women and children.
15.39: And sending away the crowds, He got into the boat and came to the region of Magadan.

16.1: And the Pharisees and the Sadducees came up, and testing Him asked Him to show them a sign from Heaven.
16.2: But He answered and said to them, " When it is evening, you say, 'Fair weather, for the sky is red. '
16.3: " And in the morning, 'Stormy weather today, for the sky is red and threatening. ' You know how to discern the appearance of the sky, but you cannot I discernthe signs of the times.
16.4: " An evil and adulterous generation seeks after a sign, but no sign will be given to it except the sign of Yonah. " And He left them and went away.
16.5: And the disciples came to the other side and had forgotten to take loaves I of bread.
16.6: And Yeshua said to them, " Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees. "
16.7: And they began to reason among themselves, saying, " Because we took no loaves I of bread. "
16.8: But Yeshua, aware of this, said, " You of little faith, why do you reason among yourselves that you have no loaves I of bread?
16.9: " Do you not understand or remember the five loaves of the five thousand, and how many baskets you took up?
16.10: " Or the seven loaves of the four thousand, and how many large baskets you took up?
16.11: " How is it that you do not understand that I did not speak to you about loaves I of bread? But beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees. "
16.12: Then they understand that He did not tell them to beware of the leaven of loaves I of bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
16.13: Now when Yeshua came into the district of Caesarea Philippoi, He asked His disciples, " Who do men say that the Son of Man is? "
16.14: And they said, " Some say Yochanan the Immerser; and others, Eliyahu; and others, Yiremayahu, or one of the prophets. "
16.15: He said to them, " But who do you say that I am? "
16.16: And Shimon Petros answered and said, " You are the Messiah, the Son of the Living God. "
16.17: And Yeshua answered and said to him, " Blessed are you, Shimon Bar - Yonah, because flesh and blood did not reveal I itto you, but My Father Who is in Heaven.
16.18: " And I tell you, you are Petros, but upon this Rock I will rebuild My assembly; and the gates of Sheol shall not prevail against it.
16.19: " I will give you the keys of the Kingdom of Heaven, and whatever you shall prohibit on Earth shall be prohibited in Heaven, and whatever you shall permit on Earth shall be permitted in Heaven. "
16.20: Then He strictly charged the disciples that they should tell no one that He was the Messiah.
16.21: From that time Yeshua the Messiah began to show His disciples that He must go to Yerushalayim, and suffer many things from the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised up on the third day.
16.22: And Petros took Him aside and began to rebuke Him, saying, " God forbid, Lord! This shall never happen to You. "
16.23: But He turned and said to Petros, " Get behind Me, adversary! You are a stumbling block to Me; for you do not think of the things of God, but man’s. "
16.24: Then Yeshua said to His disciples, " If anyone wishes to come after Me, let him deny himself, and take up His cross and follow Me. "
16.25: " For whoever wishes to save his life shall loose it; but whoever looses his life for My sake shall find it.
16.26: " For what will it profit a man, if he gains the whole world, and forfeits his own soul? Or what will a man give in exchange for his own soul?
16.27: " For the Son of Man is going to come in the glory of His Father with His angels; and will then recompense every man according to his actions.
16.28: " Truly I say to you, there are some of those who are standing here who shall not taste death until they see the Son of Man coming in His Kingdom. "

17.1: And six days later Yeshua took alongside with Him Petros and Ya’akov and Yochanan his brother, and led them up to a high mountain by themselves.
17.2: And He was transfigured before them, and His face shone like the sun, and His garments became as white as light.
17.3: And behold, Moshe and Eliyahu appeared to them, talking with them.
17.4: And Petros answered and said to Yeshua, " Lord, it is good for us to be here. If you wish, I will make three tabernacles here: one for You, one for Moshe, and one for Eliyahu. "
17.5: While he was still speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them; and behold, a voice out of the cloud, saying, " This is My Beloved Son, with Whom I am well - pleased; listen to Him! "
17.6: And when the disciples heard, they fell on their faces and were terrified.
17.7: And Yeshua came and touched them, and said, " Arise, and do not be terrified. "
17.8: And lifting up their eyes, they saw no one except Yeshua Himself alone.
17.9: And as they were coming down from the mountain, Yeshua commanded them, saying, " Tell no one the vision, until the Son of Man has risen from the dead. "
17.10: And His disciples asked Him, saying, " Why then do the scribes say that Eliyahu must come first? "
17.11: And He answered and said, " Eliyahu is coming and will restore all things;
17.12: " but I tell you that Eliyahu has already come, and they did not recognize him, but did to him whatever they wanted. So also the Son of Man is going to suffer at their hands. "
17.13: The disciples understood that He had spoken to them about Yochanan the Immerser.
17.14: And when they came to the crowd, a man came up to Him, falling on his knees before Him, and saying,
17.15: " Lord, have mercy on my son, for he is an epileptic and suffers terribly; for he often falls into the fire, and often into the water.
17.16: " And I brought him to Your disciples, and they could not cure him. "
17.17: And Yeshua answered and said, " O faithless and perverted generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I bear with you? Bring him here to Me. "
17.18: And Yeshua rebuked him, and the demon came out of him, and he was cured at that hour.
17.19: Then the disciples came to Yeshua privately and said, " Why could we not cast it out? "
17.20: And He said to them, " Because of the littleness of your faith. For truly I say to you, if you have faith as a mustard grain, you shall say to this mountain, 'Move from here to there, ' and it shall move; and nothing shall be impossible to you.
17.21: I " But this kind does not go out except by prayer and fasting. "
17.22: And as they were gathering together in Galil, Yeshua said to them, " The Son of Man is going to be delivered up into the hands of men;
17.23: " and they will kill Him, and He will be raised on the third day. " And they were deeply distressed.
17.24: And when they had come to K’far - Nachum, those who took the half - shekel I temple taxcame to Petros, and said, " Does your Teacher not pay the half - shekel I tax? "
17.25: He said, " Yes. " And when he came into the house, Yeshua spoke to him first, saying, " What do you think, Shimon? From whom do the kings of the Earth take toll or poll - tax, from their sons or from others? "
17.26: And upon his saying, " From others, " Yeshua said to him, " Then the sons are free.
17.27: " But, lest we give them offense, go to the sea and cast a hook, and take the first fish that comes up; and when you open its mouth, you will find a shekel. Take that and give it to them for you and Me. "

18.1: At that time the disciples came to Yeshua, saying, " Who then is the greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven? "
18.2: And He called a child to Himself and set him in the middle of them,
18.3: and said, " Truly I say to you, unless you turn and become like children, you shall not enter the Kingdom of Heaven.
18.4: " Whoever then humbles himself like this child, he is the greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven.
18.5: " And whoever receives one such child in My name, receives Me;
18.6: " but whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, it is better for him that a heavy millstone be hung around his neck, and that he be drowned in the depth of the sea.
18.7: " Woe to the world because of I itsstumbling - blocks! For it is necessary that stumbling - blocks come; but woe to that man through whom the stumbling - block comes!
18.8: " And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it from you; it is better for you to enter life crippled or lame, than having two hands or feet, to be cast into the eternal fire.
18.9: " And if your eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it from you. It is better for you to enter life with one eye, than having two eyes, to be cast in to the fire of Gey - Hinnom.
18.10: " See that you do not despise one of these little ones, for I tell you that their angels in Heaven continually behold the face of My Father Who is in Heaven.
18.11: " For the Son of Man has come to save that which was lost.
18.12: " What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep, and one of them has wandered astray, does he not leave the ninety - nine on the mountains and go and search for the one that is wandering astray?
18.13: " And if it happens that he finds it, truly I say to you, he rejoices over it more than over the ninety - nine which have not gone astray.
18.14: " Thus it is not I thewill of your Father Who is in Heaven that one of these little ones be lost.
18.15: " And if your brother sins, go and expose him in private. If he listens to you, you have won your brother I over.
18.16: " But if he does not listen, take one or two more along with you, so that BY THE MOUTH OF TWO OR THREE WITNESSES EVERY SPOKEN WORD MAY BE CONFIRMED.
18.17: " And if he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the assembly; and if he refuses to listen even to the assembly, let him be to you as I one of thenations and a tax - collector.
18.18: " Truly I say to you, whatever you prohibit on Earth shall be prohibited in Heaven; and whatever you permit on Earth shall be permitted in Heaven.
18.19: " Again I say to you, that if you agree on Earth about anything that they may ask, it shall be done for them by My Father Who is in Heaven.
18.20: " For where two or more have gathered together in My name, there I am in the middle of them. "
18.21: Then Petros came and said to Him, " Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Up to seven times? "
18.22: Yeshua said to him, " I do not say to you, up to seven times, but up to seventy times seven.
18.23: " Because of this the Kingdom of Heaven may be compared to a man, a king, who wished to settle accounts with his slaves.
18.24: " And when he had begun to settle I them, there was brought to him one debtor of ten thousand talents;
18.25: " but since he did not have I the abilityto repay, his lord commanded him to be sold, and his wife and his children and all that he had, and repayment to be made.
18.26: " The slave therefore falling down, bowed himself before him, saying, 'Be patient with me, and I will repay you everything. '
18.27: " And the lord of that slave felt compassion and released him and forgave him the debt.
18.28: " But the slave went out and found one of his fellow slaves who owed him a hundred denarii; and he seized him and choked I him, saying, 'Pay back what you owe. '
18.29: " So his fellow slave fell down and entreated him, saying, 'Have patience with me, and I will repay you. '
18.30: " He was unwilling, however, but went and cast him in prison until he should repay what was owed.
18.31: " So when his fellow slaves saw what had happened, they were deeply distressed and came and reported to their lord all that had happened.
18.32: " Then summoning him, his lord said to him, 'You evil slave! I forgave you all your debt because you entreated me.
18.33: " 'Should you not also have had mercy on your fellow slave, even as I had mercy on you? '
18.34: " And his lord, angered, handed him over to the torturers until he should repay all that was owed him.
18.35: " So shall My Heavenly Father also do to you, if each of you does not forgive his brother from his heart. "

19.1: And it came about that when Yeshua had completed these words, He departed from Galil, and came into the region of Yehudah, beyond the Yarden;
19.2: and great crowds followed them, and He healed them there.
19.3: And Pharisees came to Him, testing Him and saying, " Is it permissible to divorce one’s wife for any reason at all? "
19.4: And He answered and said, " Have you not read, that He who created I themfrom the beginning MADE THEM MALE AND FEMALE,
19.5: " and said, 'FOR THIS CAUSE A MAN SHALL LEAVE HIS FATHER AND MOTHER, AND SHALL BE UNITED TO HIS WIFE, AND THE TWO SHALL BECOME ONE FLESH'?
19.6: " Consequently they are no longer two, but one flesh. What therefore God has joined together, let no man separate. "
19.7: They said to Him, " Why then did Moshe command one to give her A CERTIFICATE OF DIVORCE and send I heraway? "
19.8: He said to them, " Because of your hardness of heart, Moshe allowed you to divorce your wives; but from the beginning it has not been so.
19.9: " And I say to you, whoever divorces his wife, except for fornication, and marries another I womancommits adultery. "
19.10: The disciples said to Him, " If the relationship with his wife is like this, it is advantageous not to marry. "
19.11: But He said to them, " Not all men I canmake room for this word, but I onlythose to whom it has been given.
19.12: " For there are eunuchs who were born so from their mother’s womb; and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by men; and there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the Kingdom of Heaven. He who has the power to make room I for this, let him make room I for it. "
19.13: Then children were brought to Him so that He might lay His hands on them and pray; and the disciples rebuked them.
19.14: But Yeshua said, " Let the children alone, and do not forbid them from coming to Me; for the Kingdom of Heaven belongs to such as these. "
19.15: And after laying His hands on them, He went away from there.
