19.16: And behold, one came to Him and said, " Teacher, what good thing shall I do that I might obtain eternal life? "
19.17: And He said to him, " Why are you asking Me about what is good? There is One Who is good; but if you wish to enter into life, keep the commandments. "
19.18: He said to Him, " Which ones? " And Yeshua said, " YOU SHALL NOT COMMIT MURDER. YOU SHALL NOT COMMIT ADULERTY. YOU SHALL NOT STEAL. YOU SHALL NOT BEAR FALSE WITNESS.
19.19: " HONOR YOUR FATHER AND MOTHER. And, YOU SHALL LOVE YOUR NEIGHBOR AS YOURSELF. "
19.20: The young man said to Him, " All these things I have kept, what am I still lacking? "
19.21: Yeshua said to him, " If you wish to reach the goal, go sell your possessions and give them to I thepoor, and you shall have treasure in Heaven; and come, follow Me. "
19.22: But when the young man heard this word, he went away distressed; for he was one who owned much property.
19.23: And Yeshua said to His disciples, " Truly I say to you, it is hard for a rich man to enter the Kingdom of Heaven.
19.24: " And again I say to you, it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich I manto enter into the Kingdom of God. "
19.25: And when the disciples heard I this, they were very much astonished, and said, " Then who can be saved? "
19.26: And looking upon I them, Yeshua said to them, " With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible. "
19.27: Then Petros answered and said to Him, " Behold, we have left everything and have followed You. What then will there be for us? "
19.28: And Yeshua said to them, " Truly I say to you, that you who have followed Me, in the regeneration when the Son of Man will sit on His glorious throne, you also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yisrael.
19.29: " And everyone who has left houses or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or fields for My name’s sake, shall receive many times as much, and shall inherit eternal life.
19.30: " But many first shall be last; and last, first.

20.1: " For the Kingdom of Heaven is like a housemaster who went out early in the morning to hire laborers for his vineyard.
20.2: " And when he had agreed with the laborers for a denarius for the day, he sent them into his vineyard.
20.3: " And he went out at about the third hour and saw others standing inactive in the market place;
20.4: " and to those he said, 'You too go in the vineyard, and whatever is correct I paymentI will give you. ' And they went.
20.5: " Again he went out about the sixth and ninth hour and did the same thing.
20.6: " And about the eleventh he went out and found others standing; and he said to them, 'Why have you been standing here inactive all day long? '
20.7: " They said to him, 'Because no one has hired us. ' He said to them, 'You too go in the vineyard. '
20.8: " And when evening had come, the owner of the vineyard said to his administrator, 'Call the laborers, and pay them their wages, beginning with the last up to the first. '
20.9: " And when those I hiredabout the eleventh hour came, each one received a denarius.
20.10: " And when those I hiredfirst came, they thought that they would receive more; but each one of them also received a denarius.
20.11: " And when they received it, they grumbled at the housemaster,
20.12: " saying, 'These last men have I onlyworked one hour, and you have made them equal to us who have borne the burden of the day and the scorching heat. '
20.13: " But he answered and said to one of them, 'Comrade, I am doing you no wrong; did you not agree with me for a denarius?
20.14: " 'Take what is yours and go, but I wish to give this last man the same as to you.
20.15: " 'Is it not permitted for me to do what I wish with what is my own? Or is your eye evil because I am generous? '
20.16: " Thus the last shall be first, and the first, last. "
20.17: And as Yeshua was about to go up to Yerushalayim, He took the twelve aside by themselves, and on the road He said to them,
20.18: " Behold, we are going up to Yerushalayim; and the Son of Man will be delivered up to the chief priests and scribes, and they will condemn Him to death,
20.19: " and will deliver Him to the nations to mock and scourge and crucify, and on the third day He will be raised up. "
20.20: Then the mother of the sons of Zavdai came to Him with her sons, bowing down and making a request of Him.
20.21: And He said to her, " What do you wish? " She said to Him, " Command that in Your Kingdom these two sons of mine may sit, one on Your right - hand and one on your left. "
20.22: But Yeshua answered and said, " You do not know what you are asking for. Do you have the power to drink the cup that I am about to drink? " They said to Him, " We have the power. "
20.23: He said to them, " My cup you shall drink; but to sit on My right - hand and on I Myleft, this is not Mine to give, but it is for those for whom it has been prepared by My Father. "
20.24: And hearing, the ten became indignant with the two brothers.
20.25: But Yeshua called them to Himself, and said, " You know that the rulers of the nations exercise lordship over them, and I theirgreat men exercise authority over them.
20.26: " It is not so among you, but whoever wishes to become great among you shall be your servant,
20.27: " and whoever wishes to be first among you shall be your slave;
20.28: " just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life a ransom for many. "
20.29: And as they were going out from Yericho, a great crowd followed Him.
20.30: And behold, two blind men sitting by the road, hearing that Yeshua was passing by, cried out, saying, " Lord, have mercy on us, Son of Daveed! "
20.31: And the crowd rebuked I andtold them to be quiet; but they cried out all the more, saying, " Lord, have mercy on us, Son of Daveed! "
20.32: And Yeshua stopped and called them, and said, " What do you want Me to do for you? "
20.33: They said to Him, " Lord, that our eyes may be opened. "
20.34: And moved with compassion, Yeshua touched their eyes; and immediately they recovered their sight and followed Him.

21.1: And when they approached Yerushalayim and had come to Beit - Pagey, to the Mount of Olives, then Yeshua sent two disciples,
21.2: saying to them, " Go into the village opposite you, and immediately you will find a donkey tied, and a colt with her; untie and bring I themto Me.
21.3: " And if anyone says something to you, you shall say, 'The Lord has need of them, ' and immediately he will send them. "
21.4: Now this took place I sothat what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying,
21.5: " Say to the daughter of Tziyon, 'BEHOLD, YOUR KING IS COMING TO YOU, GENTLE, AND MOUNTED ON A DONKEY, EVEN ON A COLT, THE FOAL OF A BEAST OF BURDEN. ' "
21.6: And the disciples went and did just as Yeshua had directed them,
21.7: and brought the donkey and the colt, and placed upon them their garments, upon which He had sat.
21.8: And most of the crowd spread their garments in the road, and others were cutting branches from the trees, and spreading them in the road.
21.9: And the crowds going before Him, and those who followed after, were crying out, saying, " Hoshia - na to the Son of Daveed! BLESSED IS HE WHO COMES IN THE NAME OF ADONAI! Hoshia - na in the highest!
21.10: And when He had entered Yerushalayim, all the city was stirred, saying, " Who is this? "
21.11: And the crowds were saying, " This is the prophet Yeshua, from Natzeret in Galil. "
21.12: And Yeshua entered the Temple and expelled all those who were buying and selling in the Temple, and overturned the tables of the moneychangers and the seats of those who were selling doves.
21.13: And He said to them, " It is written, 'MY HOUSE SHALL BE CALLED A HOUSE OF PRAYER'; but you are making it a CAVE OF ROBBERS. "
21.14: And blind and lame I peoplecame to Him in the Temple, and He healed them.
21.15: But when the chief priests and the scribes saw the wonderful things that He had done, and the children were crying out in the Temple and saying, " Hoshia - na to the Son of Daveed, " they became indignant,
21.16: and they said to Him, " Do you hear what these are saying? " And Yeshua said to them, " Yes. Have you ever read, 'OUT OF THE MOUTH OF INFANTS AND NURSING BABES YOU HAVE PREPARED PRAISE FOR YOURSELF? "
21.17: And He left them and went out of the city to Beit - Anyah, and lodged there.
21.18: Now in the morning, when He returned to the city, He became hungry.
21.19: And seeing a lone fig tree by the road, He came to it and found nothing on it except leaves only. And He said to it, " No longer shall there ever be fruit from you. " And instantly the fig tree wasted away.
21.20: And seeing, the disciples marveled, saying, " How did the fig tree waste away instantly? "
21.21: And Yeshua answered and said to them, " Truly I say to you, if you have faith and do not doubt, you shall not only do what was done to the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, 'Be taken up and cast into the sea, ' it shall happen.
21.22: " And all things you ask in prayer, having faith, you shall receive. "
21.23: And when He had come into the Temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came to Him while He was teaching, and said, " By what authority are you doing these things? And who gave you this authority? "
21.24: And Yeshua answered and said to them, " I will ask you also, a word, which if you tell Me, I will also tell you by what authority I do these things.
21.25: " The immersion of Yochanan was from what: from Heaven or from men? " And they reasoned among themselves, saying, " If we say, 'From Heaven, ' He will say to us, 'Then why did you not believe him? '
21.26: " But if we say, 'From men, ' we fear the mob; for they all hold Yochanan to be a prophet. "
21.27: And answering Yeshua, they said, " We do not know. " He also said to them, " Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.
21.28: " But what do you think? A man had two sons, and he came to the first and said, 'Son, go work today in the vineyard. '
21.29: " And he answered and said, 'I will, lord'; but he did not go.
21.30: " And he came to the second and said the same thing. But he answered and said, 'I will not'; I yethe afterward regretted and went.
21.31: " Which of the two did the will of his father? " They said, " The latter. " Yeshua said to them, " Truly I say to you that the tax - collectors and prostitutes will get into the Kingdom of God before you.
21.32: " For Yochanan came in the way of righteousness, and you did not believe him; but the tax - collectors and prostitutes did believe him. And you, seeing this, did not even feel regret afterward so as to believe him.
21.33: " Listen to another parable. There was a housemaster who planted a vineyard and put a wall around it and dug a wine press in it, and built a tower, and rented it out to vine - growers, and went on a journey I abroad.
21.34: " And when the harvest time approached, he sent his slaves to the vine - growers to receive his fruit.
21.35: " And the vine - growers took his slaves, and beat one, and killed another, and stoned a third.
21.36: " Again he sent another I groupof slaves larger than the first; and they did the same to them.
21.37: " But afterward he sent his son to them, saying, 'They will respect my son. '
21.38: " But when the vine - growers saw the son, they said among themselves, 'This is the heir; come, let us kill him and seize his inheritance. '
21.39: " And they took him, and threw him out of the vineyard, and killed him.
21.40: " Therefore, when the lord of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those vine - growers? "
21.41: They said to Him, " He will utterly ruin those evildoers, and will rent out the vineyard to other vine growers, who will pay him the fruits in their seasons. "
21.42: Yeshua said to them, " Did you never read in the Scriptures, 'THE STONE WHICH THE BUILDERS REJECTED, THIS BECAME THE CHIEF CORNER I stone; THIS CAME ABOUT FROM ADONAI, AND IT IS MARVELOUS IN OUR EYES'?
21.43: " Therefore I say to you, the Kingdom of God will be taken away from you, and be given to a nation producing the fruit of it.
21.44: " And he who falls on this stone will be crushed to pieces; but on whomever it falls, it will scatter him like dust. "
21.45: And when the chief priests and Pharisees heard His parables, they recognized that He was speaking about them.
21.46: And when they thought to seize Him, they feared the mob, because they held Him to be a prophet.

22.1: And Yeshua answered and spoke to them in parables, saying,
22.2: " The Kingdom of Heaven may be compared to a king, who gave a wedding feast for his son.
22.3: " And he sent out his slaves to call those who had been invited to the wedding feast, but they were unwilling to come.
22.4: " Again he sent out other slaves, saying, 'Tell those who have been invited, " Behold, I have prepared my dinner. My oxen and fattened livestock are butchered and everything is ready; come to the wedding feast. " '
22.5: " But they paid no attention and went their way, one to his own farm, another to his business,
22.6: " and the rest seized his slaves and insulted them and killed them.
22.7: " But the king was angered and sent his armies, and utterly ruined those murderers, and set their city on fire.
22.8: " Then he said to his slaves, 'The wedding is ready, but those who were invited were not ready.
22.9: " 'Go therefore to the main roads, and as many as you find, invite to the wedding feast. '
22.10: " And those slaves went out into the roads, and gathered together all they found, both evil and good; and the wedding hall was filled with dinner guests.
22.11: " But when the king came in to look upon the dinner guests, he saw there a man not dressed in wedding clothes,
22.12: " and he said to him, 'Comrade, how did you come in here without wedding clothes? And he was speechless.
22.13: " Then the king said to the servants, 'Bind him hand and foot, and cast him into the outer darkness; where there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth. '
22.14: " For many are called, but few I arechosen. "
22.15: Then the Pharisees went and counseled together how they might ensnare Him in what He said.
22.16: And they sent their disciples to Him, along with the Herodians, saying, " Teacher, we know that You are truthful, and teach the way of God in truth, and care for no one; for You do not look at the face of men.
22.17: " Tell us, therefore, what do You think? Is it permitted to give a poll - tax to Caesar, or not? "
22.18: But Yeshua was aware of their wickedness, and said, " Why are you testing me, you hypocrites?
22.19: " Show me the tribute - coin for the poll - tax. " And they brought Him a denarius.
22.20: And He said to them, " Whose image and inscription is this? "
22.21: They said to Him, " Caesar’s. " Then He said to them, " Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s. "
22.22: And hearing, they marveled, and leaving Him, they went away.
22.23: On that day Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to Him and questioned Him,
22.24: saying, " Teacher, Moshe said, 'IF A MAN DIES, HAVING NO CHILDREN, HIS BROTHER SHALL MARRY HIS WIFE, AND RAISE UP AN OFFSPRING TO HIS BROTHER. '
22.25: " Now there were seven brothers with us; and the first married, and died, and having no offspring left his wife to his brother.
22.26: " So also the second and the third, until to the seventh.
22.27: " And last of all, the woman died.
22.28: " In the resurrection, therefore, whose wife of the seven shall she be? For they all had her. "
22.29: But Yeshua answered and said to them, " You are misguided, neither understanding the Scriptures, nor the power of God.
22.30: " For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in Heaven.
22.31: " But as for the resurrection of the dead, have you not read that which was spoken to you by God, saying,
22.32: " 'I AM THE GOD OF AVRAHAM, AND THE GOD OF YITZCHAK, AND THE GOD OF YA'AKOV'? He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. "
22.33: And when the crowds heard, they were astonished at His teaching.
22.34: But when the Pharisees heard that He had put the Sadducees to silence, they gathered themselves together.
22.35: And one of them, a I personlearned in Torah, asked Him, testing Him,
22.36: " Teacher, what is the great commandment in the Torah? "
22.37: And He said to him, " 'YOU SHALL LOVE ADONAI YOUR GOD WITH ALL YOUR HEART, AND WITH ALL YOUR SOUL, AND WITH ALL YOUR MIND. '
22.38: " This is the great and foremost commandment.
22.39: " The second is like it: 'YOU SHALL LOVE YOUR NEIGHBOR AS YOURSELF. '
22.40: " On these two commandments depend the whole Torah and the Prophets. "
22.41: Now while the Pharisees were gathered together, Yeshua asked them a question,
22.42: saying, " What do you think about the Messiah, whose son is He? " They said to Him, " The sonof Daveed. "
22.43: He said to them, " Then how does Daveed in the Spirit call Him, 'Lord, ' saying,
22.44: " 'ADONAI SAID TO MY LORD, " SIT AT MY RIGHT HAND, UNTIL I PUT YOUR ENEMIES UNDERNEATH YOUR FEET' "?
22.45: " If Daveed thus calls Him 'Lord, ' how is He his son? "
22.46: And no one had the power to answer Him a word, nor did anyone dare from that day on question Him any more.

23.1: Then Yeshua spoke to the crowds and to His disciples,
23.2: saying, " The scribes and the Pharisees have seated themselves in the seat of Moshe;
23.3: " therefore all that they tell you, do and observe, but do not according to their works; for they say, and do not do.
23.4: " And they bind together heavy burdens, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves are unwilling to move them with I so much as theirfinger.
23.5: " But they do all their works to be noticed by men; for they make broad their tefillin, and lengthen the tzit - tziyot I of their garments.
23.6: " And they love the first place at banquets, and the first seats in the synagogues,
23.7: " and greetings in the market places, and being called by men, 'Rabbi. '
23.8: " But do not be called 'Rabbi'; for One is Your Teacher, and you are all brothers.
23.9: " And do not call I anyoneon Earth your father; for One is your Father, He Who is in Heaven.
23.10: " And do not be called leaders; for One is your Leader, the Messiah.
23.11: " But the greatest among you shall be your servant.
23.12: " And whoever exalts himself shall be humbled; and whoever humbles himself shall be exalted.
23.13: " But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you shut the Kingdom of Heaven from men; for you neither enter in yourselves, nor do you allow those who are entering to go in.
23.14: " Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, because you eat up widows’ houses, even while for a pretense you make long prayers; therefore you shall receive greater judgment.
23.15: " Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you traverse around to make one proselyte; and when he becomes one, you make him twice as much a son of Gey - Hinnom as yourselves.
23.16: " Woe to you, blind guides, who say, 'Whoever swears by the Temple, that is nothing; but whoever swears by the gold of the Temple, he is indebted. '
23.17: " You fools and blind I men! Which is greater, the gold, or the Temple that sanctified the gold?
23.18: " And, 'Whoever swears by the altar, I thatis nothing, but whoever swears by the offering upon it, he is indebted. '
23.19: " You blind I men! Which is greater, the offering or the altar that sanctifies the offering?
23.20: " Therefore he who swears by the altar, swears by the altar and everything on it.
23.21: " And he who swears by the Temple, swears by the Temple and by Him Who dwells in it.
23.22: " And he who swears by Heaven, swears by the Throne of God and by Him Who sits upon it.
23.23: " Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you tithe mint and dill and cummin, and have neglected the weightier I mattersof the Torah: justice and mercy and faith; but these things you should have done without neglecting the others.
23.24: " You blind guides, who strain out a gnat and swallow a camel!
23.25: " Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you cleanse the outside of the cup and of the dish, but inside they are full of plundering and incontinence.
23.26: " You blind Pharisee, first cleanse the inside of the cup and the dish, so that the outside of it may become cleansed too.
23.27: " Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like whitewashed tombs, which on the outside appear beautiful, but inside they are full of dead men’s bones and all uncleanness;
23.28: " even so you too outwardly appear righteous to men, but inwardly you are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness.
23.29: " Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you build the tombs of the prophets and decorate the monuments of the righteous,
23.30: " and say, 'If we had been I livingin the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets. '
23.31: " Thus you bear witness against yourselves, that you are the sons of those who murdered the prophets.
23.32: " Fill up, then, the measure I of the guiltof your fathers.
23.33: " You serpents, you offspring of vipers, how shall you escape the sentence of Gey - Hinnom?
23.34: " Therefore, behold, I am sending you prophets and wise men and scribes; some of them you will kill and crucify, and some of them you will scourge in your synagogues, and persecute from city to city,
23.35: " that upon you may come all the righteous blood shed on Earth, from the blood of righteous Hevel to the blood of Zekaryah, son of Berekhyah, whom you murdered between the Temple and the altar.
23.36: " Truly I say to you, all this shall come upon this race.
23.37: " O Yerushalayim, Yerushalayim, who kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to her! How often I wanted to gather your children together, the way a hen gathers together her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling.
23.38: " Behold, your house is being left to you desolate.
23.39: " For I say to you, from now on you shall not see Me until you say, 'BLESSED IS HE WHO COMES IN THE NAME OF ADONAI. ' "

24.1: And Yeshua came out from the Temple and was going away when His disciples came up to show the Temple buildings to Him.
24.2: And He answered and said to them, " Do you not see all these? Truly I say to you, not one stone here shall be left upon another, which will not be torn down. "
24.3: And as He was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to Him privately, saying, " Tell us, when will this be, and what I will bethe sign of your coming, and of the consummation of the age? "
24.4: And Yeshua answered and said to them, " See to it that no one misleads you.
24.5: " For many will come in My name, saying, 'I am the anointed one, ' and mislead many.
24.6: " And you will be hearing of wars and rumors of wars; see that you are not troubled, it is necessary for I these thingsto occur, but the end is not yet.
24.7: " For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and in various places there will be famines and earthquakes.
24.8: " But all these things are the beginning of birth pains.
24.9: " Then they will deliver you to tribulation, and will kill you, and you will be hated by all nations because of My name.
24.10: " And at that time many will be offended and will deliver up one another and hate one another.
24.11: " And many false prophets will arise, and will mislead many.
24.12: " And because lawlessness is multiplied, most people’s love will grow cold.
24.13: " But the one who endures to the end, he shall be saved.
24.14: " And this good news of the Kingdom shall be proclaimed in the whole world for a testimony to all the nations, and then the end shall come.
24.15: " Therefore when you see the ABOMINATION OF DESOLATION which was spoken of through Dani’el the prophet, standing in the Holy Place - - let the reader understand - -
24.16: " then let those who are in Yehudah escape to the mountains;
24.17: " let him who is on the housetop not go down to take things that are in his house;
24.18: " and let him who is in the field not turn back to get his garment.
24.19: " But woe to those who are with child and to those who nurse in those days!
24.20: " But pray that your flight may not be in the winter, neither on a Shabbat;
24.21: " for then there will be great tribulation, such as has not occurred since the beginning of the world until now, nor ever shall be.
24.22: " And unless those days had been shortened, no flesh would have been saved; but for the sake of the elect those days shall be shortened.
24.23: " Then if anyone says to you, 'Behold, here is the Messiah, ' or, 'There I He is, ' do not believe.
24.24: " For false messiahs and false prophets will arise and will show great signs and wonders, so as to mislead, if possible, even the elect.
24.25: " Behold, I have told you beforehand.
24.26: " If therefore they say to you, 'Behold, He is in the wilderness, ' do not go forth, or, 'Behold, He is in the inner chambers, ' do not believe I it.
24.27: " For just as the lightning comes from the east, and flashes even to the west, so shall the coming of the Son of Man be.
24.28: " Wherever the corpse is, there the vultures will gather together.
24.29: " But immediately after the tribulation of those days THE SUN WILL BE DARKENED, AND THE MOON WILL NOT GIVE ITS LIGHT, AND THE STARS WILL FALL FROM THE SKY, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken,
24.30: " and then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the heavens, and then all the tribes of the Earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of the sky with power and great glory.
24.31: " And He will send forth His angels with a great trumpet, and they will gather together His elect from the four winds, from one extreme of the heavens to the other extreme.
24.32: " Now learn the parable from the fig tree: when its branch has become tender and puts forth its leaves, you know that summer is near;
24.33: " even so, you, when you see all these things, recognize that He is near, at the doors.
24.34: " Truly I say to you, this race will not pass away until all these things occur.
24.35: " Heaven and Earth will pass away, but My words will not pass away.
24.36: " But of that day and hour, no one knows, not even the angels of Heaven, nor the Son, but the Father only.
24.37: " For the coming of the Son of Man will be just like the days of Noach.
24.38: " For just as in those days which were before the flood, they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noach entered the ark,
24.39: " and they did not understand until the flood came and took them all away by violence; so shall the coming of the Son of Man be.
24.40: " Then there shall be two men in the field; one will be taken alongside, and one will be left alone.
24.41: " Two women I will begrinding at the mill, one will be taken alongside, and one will be left alone.
24.42: " Therefore keep watch, for you do not know which day your Lord is coming.
24.43: " But know this, that if the housemaster had known in what watch of the night the thief was coming, he would have been on the watch and would not have allowed his house to have been broken into.
24.44: " Therefore you also must be ready; for the Son of Man is coming at an hour when you do not think I Hewill.
24.45: " Who then is the faithful and sensible slave whom his lord put in charge of his household to give them their nourishment at the proper time?
24.46: " Blessed is the slave whom his lord finds so doing when he comes.
24.47: " Truly I say to you, that he will put him in charge of all of his possessions.
24.48: " But if the evil slave says in his heart, 'My lord is not coming for a long time, '
24.49: " and shall begin to beat his fellow slaves, and eat and drink with drunkards,
24.50: " the lord of that slave will come on a day when he does not expect, and at an hour which he does not know,
24.51: " and shall cut him in pieces, and assign him a portion with the hypocrites; there shall be weeping and the gnashing of teeth.

25.1: " Then the Kingdom of Heaven will be comparable to ten virgins, who took their lamps, and went out to meet the bridegroom.
25.2: " And five of them were foolish, and five of them were prudent.
25.3: " For when the foolish took their lamps, they took no oil with them,
25.4: " but the prudent took oil in flasks with their lamps.
25.5: " Now while the bridegroom was tarrying, they all became drowsy and I beganto sleep.
25.6: " But in the middle of the night there was a shout, 'Behold, the bridegroom! Come out to meet I him.
25.7: " Then all those virgins rose, and trimmed their lamps.
25.8: " And the foolish said to the prudent, 'Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out. '
25.9: " But the prudent answered, saying, 'No, there will not be enough for us and for you; go instead to the dealers and buy for yourselves. '
25.10: " And while they were going away to make the purchase, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast; and the door was shut.
25.11: " And afterward the other virgins came, saying 'Lord, lord, open up for us! '
25.12: " But he answered and said, 'Truly I say to you, I do not know you. '
25.13: " Be on the alert then, for you do not know the day nor the hour.
25.14: " For I it isjust like a man going on a journey, who called his own slaves and entrusted his possessions to them.
25.15: " And to one he gave five talents, to another, two, and to another, one, each according to his own power; and he went on his journey.
25.16: " Immediately the one who had received the five talents went and traded with them, and gained five more talents.
25.17: " In the same manner the one who I hadthe two gained two more.
25.18: " But he who received the one went away, and dug in the ground, and hid his lord’s money.
25.19: " Now after a long time the lord of those slaves came and settled accounts with them.
25.20: " And the one who had received the five talents came forward, and brought five more talents, saying, 'Lord, you entrusted five talents to me; behold, I have gained five more talents. '
25.21: " His lord said to him, 'Well done, good and faithful slave; you were faithful with a few things, I will put you in charge of many things, enter into the joy of your lord. '
25.22: " The one who I hadthe two talents came forward and said, 'Lord, you entrusted to me two talents; behold, I have gained two more talents. '
25.23: " His lord said to him, 'Well done, good and faithful slave; you were faithful with a few things, enter into the joy of your lord. '
25.24: " And the one who had received the one talent came forward and said, 'Lord, I knew you to be a hard man, reaping where you did not sow, and gathering where you did not scatter.
25.25: " 'And I was afraid, and went away and hid your talent in the ground. Behold, you have what is yours. '
25.26: " But his lord answered and said to him, 'You evil, lazy slave, you knew that I reap where I did not sow, and gather where I did not scatter.
25.27: " 'Then you ought to have put my money in the bank, and on my arrival I would have received I what ismine back with interest.
25.28: " 'Therefore take away the talent from him, and give it to the one who has ten talents. '
25.29: " For to everyone who has shall I morebe given, and he shall have an abundance; but from the one who does not have, even what he does have shall be taken away.
25.30: " And cast out the useless slave into the outer darkness; where there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
25.31: " But when the Son of Man comes in His glory, and all the angels with Him, then He will sit on His glorious throne.
25.32: " And all the nations will be gathered before Him, and he will separate them from one another as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats,
25.33: " and He will put the sheep on His right I hand, and the goats on the left.
25.34: " Then the King will say to those on His right I hand, 'Come, you who are blessed of My Father, inherit the Kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the cosmos.
25.35: " 'For I was hungry, and you gave Me I somethingto eat; I was thirsty, and you gave Me drink; I was a stranger, and you invited Me in;
25.36: " 'naked, and you clothed Me; I was sick, and you visited Me; I was in prison, and you came to Me. '
25.37: " Then the righteous will answer Him, saying, 'Lord, when did we see You hungry, and feed You, or thirsty, and give You drink?
25.38: " 'And when did we see You a stranger, and invite You in, or naked, and clothed You?
25.39: " 'And when did we see You sick, or in prison, and come to You? '
25.40: " And the King will answer and say to them, 'Truly I say to you, to the extent that you did it to one of these brothers of Mine, I eventhe least, you did it to Me. '
25.41: " Then He will say to those on His left, 'Depart from Me, cursed I ones, into the eternal fire which has been prepared for the Devil and his angels;
25.42: " 'for I was hungry, and you gave Me I nothingto eat; I was thirsty, and you gave Me nothing to drink;
25.43: " 'I was a stranger, and you did not invite Me in; naked, and you did not clothe Me; sick, and in prison, and you did not visit Me. '
25.44: " Then they themselves will also answer, saying, 'Lord, when did we see you hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and did not minister to You? '
25.45: " Then He will answer them, saying, 'Truly I say to you, to the extent that you did not do it to one of the least of these, you did not do it to Me. '
25.46: " And they will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life. "

26.1: And it came about that when Yeshua had finished all these words, He said to His disciples,
26.2: " You know after two days the Pesach is coming, and the Son of Man I will bedelivered up for crucifixion. "
26.3: Then the chief priests and the elders of the people were gathered together in the courtyard of the high priest, named Kayafa;
26.4: and they counseled together to seize Yeshua by stealth, and kill I Him.
26.5: But they were saying, " Not during the festival, lest an uproar occur among the people. "
26.6: Now when Yeshua was in Beit - Anyah, at the home of Shimon the leper,
26.7: a woman came to him with an alabaster box of very expensive perfume, and she poured it down upon His head as He reclined.
26.8: But the disciples were indignant when they saw I this, and said, " Why this loss?
26.9: " For this might have been sold for a high price, and given to the poor. "
26.10: But Yeshua, aware of this, said to them, " Why do you trouble the woman? For she had done a good deed to Me.
26.11: " For the poor you have with you always; but you do not always have Me.
26.12: " For when she poured this perfume upon My body, she did it to prepare Me for burial.
26.13: " Truly I say to you, wherever this good news is proclaimed in the whole world, what this woman has done will also be spoken of in memory of her. "
26.14: Then one of the twelve, named Yehudah I fromK’riot, went to the chief priests,
26.15: and asked, " What are you willing to give me if I deliver Him up to you? " And they weighted out to him thirty pieces of silver.
26.16: And from then on he was looking for a fitting time to deliver Him up.
26.17: Now on the first I dayof Chag HaMatzah the disciples came to Yeshua, saying, " Where do You want us to prepare for You to eat the Pesach? "
26.18: And He said, " Go into the city to a certain man, and say to him, 'The Teacher says, My appointed time is near; I I am tokeep the Pesach at your house with My disciples. ' "
26.19: And the disciples did as Yeshua had directed them; and they prepared the Pesach.
26.20: Now when evening had come, He was reclining with the twelve disciples.
26.21: And as they were eating, He said, " Truly I say to you, that one of you will deliver Me up. "
26.22: And being deeply distressed, each one of them began to say to Him, " Surely not I, Lord? "
26.23: And He answered and said, " He who has dipped his hand with Me in the dish is the one who will deliver Me up.
26.24: " The Son of Man goes just as is written of Him; but woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is delivered up! It would have been better for that man if he had never been born. "
26.25: And Yehudah, who was delivering Him up, answered and said, " Surely it is not I, Rabbi? " He said to him, " You have said I ityourself. "
26.26: And while they were eating, Yeshua took bread, and after a blessing He broke and gave I itto the disciples, and said, " Receive, eat; this is My body. "
26.27: And when He had taken a cup and given thanks, He gave I itto them, saying, " Drink from it, all of you;
26.28: " for this is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for forgiveness of sins.
26.29: " But I say to you, I will not drink of the fruit of the vine from now on, until that day when I drink it anew with you in My Father’s Kingdom. "
26.30: And after singing a praise, they went forth to the Mount of Olives.
26.31: Then Yeshua said to them, " You will all be offended because of Me this night, for it is written, 'I WILL STRIKE DOWN THE SHEPHERD, AND THE SHEEP OF THE FLOCK SHALL BE SCATTERED. '
26.32: " But after I have been raised, I will go before you to Galil. "
26.33: But Petros answered and said to Him, " Though I theymay all be offended because of You, I will never be offended. "
26.34: Yeshua said to him, " Truly I say to you, that this night before a rooster crows, you will deny Me three times. "
26.35: Petros said to Him, " Even if it is necessary for me to die with You, I will not deny You. " And all the disciples said the same.
26.36: Then Yeshua came with them to a place called Gat’Sh’manim, and said to His disciples, " Sit here while I go over there and pray. "
26.37: And He took alongside with Him Petros and the two sons of Zavdai, and began to be distressed and troubled.
26.38: Then He said to them, " My soul is very sorrowful, even to death; remain here and keep watch with Me. "
26.39: And He proceeded a little further, and fell on His face and prayed, " My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from Me; yet, not as I will, but You will. "
26.40: And He came to His disciples and found them sleeping, and said to Petros, " So, you could not keep watch with Me for one hour?
26.41: " Keep watching and praying, that you may not enter into temptation; the spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak. "
26.42: He went away again and second time and prayed, saying, " My Father, if this I cupdoes not have the power to pass away lest I drink it, Your will be done. "
26.43: And again He came and found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy.
26.44: And He left them again, and went away and prayed a third time, saying the same words once more.
26.45: Then He came to His disciples and said to them, " Are you still sleeping and resting? Behold, the hour is nearing, and the Son of Man is being delivered up into the hands of sinners.
26.46: " Arise, let us go. Behold, the one who delivers Me up is nearing. "
26.47: And while He was still speaking, behold, Yehudah, one of the twelve, came up, accompanied by a great crowd with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and elders of the people.
26.48: Now he who was delivering Him up gave them a sign, saying, " The One I shall kiss, He is the One; seize Him. "
26.49: And immediately He went to Yeshua and said, " Greetings, Rabbi! " and kissed Him.
26.50: And Yeshua said to him, " Comrade, I dowhat you have come for. " Then they came near and laid hands on Yeshua and seized Him.
26.51: And behold, one of those who were with Yeshua extended I his handand drew out his sword, and struck the slave of the high priest, and took off his ear.
26.52: Then Yeshua said to him, " Put your sword back into its place; for all those who take up the sword will perish by the sword.
26.53: " Or do you think that I do not have the power to call upon My Father, and He will at once put at My disposal more than twelve legions of angels?
26.54: " How then shall the Scriptures be fulfilled, that it must occur in this way? "
26.55: At that time Yeshua said to the crowds, " Have you come out with swords and clubs to capture Me as against a robber? Every day I used to sit in the Temple teaching and you did not seize Me.
26.56: " But all this has occurred so that the Scriptures of the Prophets may be fulfilled. " Then all the disciples left Him and fled.
26.57: And those who had seized Yeshua led Him away to Kayafa, the high priest, where the scribes and the elders had gathered together,
26.58: But Petros also was following them at a distance I up tothe courtyard of the high priest, and entered in, and sat down with the officers to see the conclusion.
26.59: Now the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin sought false witness against Yeshua, in order that they might put Him to death;
26.60: but they found none, even though many false witnesses came forward. But later two came forward,
26.61: and said, " This Man stated, 'I have the power to tear down the Temple of God and to rebuild it in three days. ' "
26.62: And the high priest stood up and said to him, " Do you not answer? What is it that these men testify against You? "
26.63: But Yeshua kept silent. And the high priest said to Him, " I adjure You by the Living God, that You tell us whether You are the Messiah, the Son of God. "
26.64: Yeshua said to him, " You have said so. Nevertheless, I tell you, hereafter you shall see THE SON OF MAN SITTING AT THE RIGHT HAND OF POWER, and COMING ON THE CLOUDS OF HEAVEN. "
26.65: Then the high priest tore his robes, saying, " He has blasphemed! What further need do we have of witnesses? Behold, you have now heard the blasphemy.
26.66: " What is your opinion? " They answered and said, " He is deserving of death! "
26.67: Then they spit in His face and struck Him with their fists; and others slapped Him,
26.68: and said, " Prophecy to us, You Messiah; who is the one who hit you? "
26.69: Now Petros was sitting outside in the courtyard, and a certain maidservant came to him and said, " You also were with Yeshua the Galilean. "
26.70: But he denied I itbefore them all, saying, " I do not know what you are talking about. "
26.71: And when he had gone out to the gateway, another saw him and said to those who were bystanders, " This man was with Yeshua of Natzeret. "
26.72: And again he denied I itwith an oath, " I do not know the Man. "
26.73: And a little later the bystanders came up and said to Petros, " Surely you too are I oneof them; for the way you talk makes it evident. "
26.74: Then he began to curse and swear, " I do not know the Man! " And immediately a rooster crowed.
26.75: And Petros remembered the word which Yeshua had said, " Before a rooster crows, you will deny Me three times. " And he went out and wept bitterly.

27.1: Now when morning had come, all the chief priests and elders of the people took council against Yeshua to put Him to death;
27.2: and they bound Him and led Him away, and handed Him over to Pilatos the governor.
27.3: Then when Yehudah, who had delivered Him up, saw that He had been condemned, he felt remorse and turned back the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders,
27.4: saying, " I have sinned by delivering up innocent blood. " But they said, " What is that to us? See to it yourself. "
27.5: And he threw off the pieces of silver into the Temple and withdrew; and he went away and hanged himself.
27.6: And the chief priests took the pieces of silver and said, " It is not permitted to put them in the treasury, since it is the price of blood. "
27.7: And they counseled together and with the money bought the Potter’s Field as a burial place for foreigners.
27.8: For this reason that field has been called the Field of Blood to this day.
27.9: Then that which was spoken through Yirmayahu the prophet was fulfilled, saying, " AND THEY TOOK THE THIRTY PIECES OF SILVER, THE PRICE OF THE ONE WHOSE PRICE HAD BEEN SET BY THE SONS OF YISRAEL;
27.10: " AND THEY GAVE THEM FOR THE POTTER'S FIELD, AS ADONAI DIRECTED ME. "
27.11: Now Yeshua stood before the governor, and the governor questioned Him, saying, " Are You the King of the Yehudim? " And Yeshua said to him, " You have said so. "
27.12: And while He was being accused by the chief priests and elders, He made no answer.
27.13: Then Pilatos said to Him, " Do You not hear how many things they testify against You? "
27.14: And He did not answer him with regard to even a spoken word, so that the governor was quite amazed.
27.15: Now at the festival the governor was accustomed to release for the crowd I anyone prisoner whom they wished.
27.16: And they were holding then a notorious prisoner called Bar - Abba.
27.17: When therefore they were gathered together, Pilatos said to them, " Whom do you want me to release for you? Bar - Abba, or Yeshua Who is called Messiah? "
27.18: For he knew that because of envy they had handed Him over I to him.
27.19: And while he was sitting on the bema, his wife sent to him, saying, " Have nothing to do with that righteous I Man, for I have suffered much over him today in a dream. "
27.20: But the chief priests and the elders persuaded the crowds to ask for Bar - Abba, and utterly ruin Yeshua.
27.21: The governor answered and said to them, " Which of the two do you want me to release for you? " And they said, " Bar - Abba. "
27.22: Pilatos said to them, " Then what shall I do with Yeshua, Who is called Messiah? " They all said, " Let Him be crucified. "
27.23: And he said, " Why? What evil has He done? " But they kept shouting all the more, saying, " Let Him be crucified! "
27.24: And when Pilatos saw that he was accomplishing nothing, but rather that a riot was beginning, he took water and washed his hands in front of the crowds, saying, " I am innocent of this Man’s blood, see I to ityourselves. "
27.25: And all the people answered and said, " His blood I beupon us and on our children! "
27.26: Then he released Bar - Abba for them; and after having Yeshua scourged, he handed Him over to be crucified.
27.27: Then the soldiers of the governor took Yeshua alongside into the Praetorium and gathered the whole battalion around Him.
27.28: And they stripped Him and put a scarlet robe upon Him.
27.29: And after weaving a crown of thorns, they put it on His head, and a reed in His right hand; and they kneeled down before Him and mocked Him, saying, " Hail, King of the Yehudim! "
27.30: And they spit on Him, and took the reed and were beating Him on the head.
27.31: And when they had mocked Him, they stripped His robe off and put His garments on Him, and led Him away to crucify I Him.
27.32: And as they were coming out, they found a man of Kureinei name Shimon, whom they impressed I into serviceto bear His cross.
27.33: And when they came to a place called Gulgolta - - which means Place of a Skull - -
27.34: they gave Him wine to drink mixed with gall; and after tasting, He was unwilling to drink.
27.35: And having crucified Him, they divided up His garments among themselves by casting lots;
27.36: and sitting down, they I beganto keep watch over Him there.
27.37: And they put up above His head the accusation against Him, which read, " THIS IS YESHUA, THE KING OF THE YEHUDIM. "
27.38: Then two robbers were crucified with Him, one on the right, and one on the left.
27.39: And those passing beside were blaspheming Him, shaking their heads,
27.40: and saying, " You Who I wouldtear down the Temple and rebuild it in three days, save Yourself! If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross. "
27.41: In the same manner the chief priests also, along with the scribes and elders, were mocking and saying,
27.42: " He saved others; He cannot save Himself. He is the King of Yisrael; let Him come down now from the cross, and we will believe in Him.
27.43: " HE TRUSTS IN GOD; LET HIM DELIVER I Himnow IF HE WANTS HIM; for He said 'I am the Son of God. ' "
27.44: And the robbers also who had been crucified together with Him were reproaching Him the same.
27.45: Now from the sixth hour darkness fell upon all the land until the ninth hour,
27.46: And about the ninth hour Yeshua cried out with a great voice, saying, " ELI, ELI, LAMA SABACHTHANI? " That is, " My God, My God, why have you abandoned Me? "
27.47: And some of those who were standing there, when they heard this, said, " This man is calling for Eliyahu. "
27.48: And immediately one of them ran and took a sponge, filled it with wine vinegar, and put it on a reed, and gave Him a drink.
27.49: But the rest said, " Let us see whether Eliyahu will come to save Him. "
27.50: And Yeshua cried out again with a great voice, and yielded up I Hisspirit.
27.51: And behold, the curtain of the Temple was split in two from top to bottom, and the Earth shook; and the rocks were split,
27.52: and the tombs I alsowere opened; and many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep were raised;
27.53: and coming out of the tombs after His resurrection they entered the holy city and appeared to many.
27.54: Now the centurion and those who were with Him, keeping watch over Yeshua, when they saw the earthquake and what was happening, became very frightened and said, " Truly, this was the Son of God! "
27.55: And many women were there looking on Him from afar, who had followed Yeshua from Galil, ministering to Him,
27.56: among whom were Miriam of Magdala, and Miriam the mother of Ya’akov and Yosef, and the mother of the sons of Zavdai.
27.57: When it was evening, there came a rich man from Ramatayim, named Yosef, who himself had also become a disciple of Yeshua.
27.58: He went to Pilatos and asked for the body of Yeshua. Then Pilatos ordered for I itto be given over I tohim.
27.59: And Yosef took the body and wrapped it in a clean, fine linen shroud,
27.60: and laid it in his own freshly I madetomb, which he had hewn out of the rock; and he rolled a great stone to the door of the tomb and went away.
27.61: And Miriam of Magdala was there, and the other Miriam, sitting opposite the grave.
27.62: Now on the next day, which is after the preparation, the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered before Pilatos,
27.63: and said, " Lord, we remember that when He was still alive, I thisdeceiver said, 'After three days I I willrise again. '
27.64: " Therefore, give orders for the grave to be secured until the third day, lest His disciples go and steal Him away and say to the people, 'He has risen from the dead, ' and the last deception will be worse than the first. "
27.65: Pilatos said to them, " You have a guard. Go, secure it as you know how. "
27.66: So they went and made the grave secure, and along with the guard they sealed the stone.

28.1: Now late on the Shabbat, as it began to draw toward the first of the week, Miriam of Magdala and the other Miriam went to look at the grave.
28.2: And behold, a great earthquake had occurred, for an angel of the Lord came down from Heaven and approached and rolled away the stone and sat upon it.
28.3: And his appearance was as lightning, and his clothing as white as snow;
28.4: and the guards shook for fear of him, and became like dead men.
28.5: And the angel answered and said to the women, " Do not be afraid; for I know that you are seeking Yeshua Who has been crucified.
28.6: " He is not here, for He has risen just as He said. Come, see the place where He was lying.
28.7: " Then go quickly and tell His disciples that He has risen from the dead. And behold, He is going before you into Galil; there you will see Him. Behold, I have told you. "
28.8: So they departed quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy and ran to report it to His disciples.
28.9: And behold, Yeshua met them and spoke to them. And they approached and took hold of His feet and worshipped Him.
28.10: Then Yeshua said to them, " Do not be afraid. Go and announce to My brethren to leave for Galil, and there they will see Me. "
28.11: Now while they were going, behold, some of the guard came into the city and reported to the chief priests all that had happened.
28.12: And when they had gathered together with the elders and counseled together, they gave a sufficient sum of money to the soldiers,
28.13: and said, " You are to say, 'His disciples came by night and stole Him away while we were asleep. '
28.14: " And if this should be heard by the governor, we will persuade him and keep you out of trouble. "
28.15: And they took the money and did as they had been instructed; and this story was spread among the Yehudim until today.
28.16: Now the eleven disciples went to Galil, to the mountain which Yeshua had directed them.
28.17: And when they saw Him, they worshipped I Him; but some doubted.
28.18: And Yeshua came up and spoke to them, saying, " All authority has been given to Me in Heaven and on Earth,
28.19: " Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, immersing them in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
28.20: " teaching them to observe all that I commanded you; and behold, I am with you always, even to the consummation of the age. "

1.1: The beginning of the good news of Yeshua the Messiah, the Son of God.
1.2: As it is written in Yeshayahu the prophet, " BEHOLD, I SEND MY MESSENGER BEFORE YOUR FACE, WHO WILL PREPARE YOUR WAY;
1.3: " THE VOICE OF ONE CRYING IN THE WILDERNESS: 'PREPARE THE WAY OF ADONAI, MAKE HIS PATHS STRAIGHT. ' "
1.4: Yochanan the Immerser appeared in the wilderness proclaiming an immersion of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
1.5: And all the country of Yehudah was going out to him, and all the people of Yerushalayim; and they were immersed by him the Yarden River, confessing their sins.
1.6: Now Yochanan was clothed with camel’s hair and a leather belt around his waist, and he ate locusts and wild honey.
1.7: And he proclaimed, saying, " After me One is coming Who is mightier than I, and I am not fit to stoop down and loosen the straps of His sandals.
1.8: " I immerse you with water; but He will immerse you with the Holy Spirit. "
1.9: And it came to pass in those days that Yeshua came from Natzeret in Galil, and was immersed by Yochanan in the Yarden.
1.10: And immediately coming up out of the water, He saw Heaven dividing, and the Spirit as a dove coming down upon Him;
1.11: and a voice came out of the Heavens: " You are My beloved Son, in Whom I am well - pleased. "
1.12: And immediately the Spirit put Him forth I to goout into the wilderness.
1.13: And He was in the wilderness for forty days, being tempted by HaSatan; and He was with the wild beasts, and the angels were ministering to Him.
1.14: And after Yochanan had been delivered up I into custody, Yeshua came into Galil, proclaiming the good news of God,
1.15: and saying, " The season is fulfilled, and the Kingdom of God is at hand; repent and believe in the good news. "
1.16: And passing along by the Sea of Galil, He saw Shimon, and Andreas, the brother of Shimon, casting a net into the sea; for they were fishermen.
1.17: And Yeshua said to them, " Follow Me, and I will make you become fishers of men. "
1.18: And immediately they left their nets and followed Him.
1.19: And going on a little farther, He saw Ya’akov the I sonof Zavdai, and Yochanan his brother, who were also in the boat preparing the nets.
1.20: And immediately He called them; and they left their father Zavdai in the boat with the hired servants and went away to follow Him.
1.21: And they went into K’far - Nachum; and immediately on the Shabbat He entered the synagogue and was teaching.
1.22: And they were astonished at His teaching; for He was teaching them as I OneWho had authority, and not as the scribes.
1.23: And immediately there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit; and he cried out,
1.24: saying, " What have You to do with us, Yeshua of Natzeret? Have You come to ruin us? I know Who You are - - the Holy One of God! "
1.25: But Yeshua rebuked him, saying, " Be silenced, and come out of him! "
1.26: And throwing him into convulsions, the unclean spirit screamed out with a great voice, I andcame out of him.
1.27: And they were all astonished, so that they questioned among themselves, saying, " What is this? A fresh teaching? With authority He commands even the unclean spirits - - and they obey Him! "
1.28: And immediately the news of Him went out everywhere into the whole surrounding region of Galil.
1.29: And immediately after they had come out of the synagogue, I theyentered into the house of Shimon and Andreas, with Ya’akov and Yochanan.
1.30: Now Shimon’s mother - in - law was lying sick with a fever; and immediately they told Him about her.
1.31: And He approached her and raised her up, taking hold of her hand, and the fever left her and she served them.
1.32: And when evening had come, when the sun had set, they brought to Him all who were ill and those who were demon - possessed.
1.33: And the whole city was gathered together near the door.
1.34: And He healed many who were ill with various diseases, and cast out many demons; and He would not permit the demons to speak, because they knew Who He was.
1.35: And very early, while it was still night, He arose and went out and departed to a solitary place, and was praying there.
1.36: And Shimon and those who were with him pursued Him,
1.37: and they found Him and said to Him, " Everyone is seeking You. "
1.38: And He said to them, " Let us go elsewhere into the neighboring towns, in order that I might proclaim there also; for that is why I came out. "
1.39: And He went into their synagogues throughout all Galil, proclaiming and casting out demons.
1.40: And a leper came to Him, calling out for Him and falling on his knees before Him, and saying to Him, " If You will, You can cleanse me. "
1.41: And moved with compassion, He stretched out His hand and touched him, and said to him, " I am willing; be cleansed! "
1.42: And immediately the leprosy left him and he was cleansed.
1.43: And He strictly warned him and immediately sent him away,
1.44: and He said to him, " See that you say nothing to anyone; but go show yourself to the priest and offer for your cleansing what Moshe commanded for a testimony to them. "
1.45: But he went out and began to proclaim it much and to spread the word about, so I much thatYeshua could no longer openly enter into a city, but was outside in solitary places; and they were coming to Him from every quarter.

2.1: And when He had entered again into K’far - Nachum after some days, it was heard that He was at home.
2.2: And many were gathered together, so that there was no longer room I for them, and He was speaking the word to them.
2.3: And they came, bringing to Him a paralytic, raised up by four men.
2.4: And not having the power to come near to Him because of the crowd, they removed the roof above Him; and when they had dug an opening, they lowered the pallet on which the paralytic was lying.
2.5: And Yeshua, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic, " My child, your sins are forgiven. "
2.6: Now some of the scribes were sitting there, questioning in their hearts,
2.7: " Why does this Man speak in this way? He is blaspheming! Who has the power to forgive sins but God alone? "
2.8: And immediately Yeshua, recognizing in His spirit that they were questioning that way within themselves, said to them, " Why are you questioning about these things in your hearts?
2.9: " Which is easier, to say to the paralytic, 'Your sins are forgiven'; or to say, 'Arise, and take up your pallet and walk'?
2.10: " But in order that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on Earth to forgive sins " - - He said to the paralytic - -
2.11: " I say to you, arise, take up your pallet, and go home. "
2.12: And he arose and immediately took up the pallet and went out before them all; so that they were all beside themselves and were glorifying God, saying, " We have never seen anything like this! "
2.13: And He went out again by the seashore; and all the crowd was coming to Him, and He was teaching them.
2.14: And as He passed by, He saw Levee the I sonof Chalfai sitting in the tax office, and He said to him, " Follow Me! " And he rose and followed Him.
2.15: And it happened that as He was reclining in his house, and many tax - collectors and sinners were dining with Yeshua and His disciples; for there were many of them, and they were following Him.
2.16: And the scribes and the Pharisees, when they saw that He was eating with sinners and tax - collectors, said to His disciples, " Why is He eating and drinking with tax - collectors and sinners? "
2.17: And hearing this, Yeshua said to them, " Those who are strong have no need of a physician, but those who are ill; I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners. "
2.18: And Yochanan’s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting; and they came and said to Him, " Why do Yochanan’s disciples and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but Your disciples do not fast? "
2.19: And Yeshua said to them, " While the Bridegroom is with them, the attendants of the bridegroom do not fast, do they? So long as they have the Bridegroom with them, they do not have the power to fast.
2.20: " But the days will come when the Bridegroom is lifted off from them, and then they will fast in that day.
2.21: " No one sews a piece of unshrunk cloth on an old garment; otherwise the patch pulls away from it, the fresh from the old, and a worse tear results.
2.22: " And no one puts new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the wine will break apart the skins, and the wine is ruined, and the skins I are as well; but I one putsnew wine into fresh wineskins. "
2.23: And it came about that He was passing through the grainfields on the Shabbat, and His disciples began to make their way, picking the heads I of grain.
2.24: And the Pharisees were saying to Him, " Behold, why are they doing what is not permitted on the Shabbat? "
2.25: And He said to them, " Have you never read what Daveed did when he was in need and was hungry, he and those with him?
2.26: " How he entered the House of God I in the timeof Evyatar I thehigh priest, and ate the consecrated bread, which is not permitted for I anyoneto eat except the priests, and also gave I itto those who were with him? "
2.27: And He said to them, " The Shabbat was made for mankind, and not mankind for the Shabbat.
2.28: " So then, the Son of Man is Lord, even of the Shabbat. "

3.1: And He entered again into a synagogue; and a man was there who had a withered hand.
3.2: And they were watching Him, I to seewhether He would heal him on the Shabbat, in order that they might make accusation I againstHim.
3.3: And He said to the man who had the withered hand, " Arise, and I comeforth! "
3.4: And He said to them, " Is it permitted on the Shabbat to do good or to do evil, to save a life or to kill? " But they stayed silent.
3.5: And after looking around at them with wrath, grieved at their hardness of heart, He said to the man, " Stretch out your hand. " And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored.
3.6: And the Pharisees went out and immediately counseled together with the Herodians against Him, I as tohow they might utterly ruin Him.
3.7: And Yeshua withdrew to the sea with His disciples; and a great crowd from Galil followed, and from Yehudah,
3.8: and from Yerushalayim, and from Idumea, and I fromthe other side of the Yarden, and I fromaround Tzor and Tzidon, a great crowd heard of all that He was doing and came to Him.
3.9: And He told His disciples to have a boat stand ready for Him because of the crowd, in order that they not afflict Him I by crowding;
3.10: for He had healed many, so that all who had scourgings fell on Him in order to touch Him.
3.11: And whenever the unclean spirits beheld Him, they would prostrate before Him and cry out, saying, " You are the Son of God! "
3.12: And He strictly warned them not to make Him known.
3.13: And He went up to the mountain, and called to those whom He Himself wanted; and they came to Him.
3.14: And He made twelve, that they might be with Him, and that He might send them forth to proclaim,
3.15: and to have authority to cast out the demons.
3.16: And He made the twelve: Shimon - - to whom He placed the name Petros,
3.17: and Ya’akov, the I sonof Zavdai, and Yochanan the brother of Zavdai - - to then he placed the name B’nei - Regesh, which means " Sons of Thunder ";
3.18: and Andreas, and Philippos, and Bar - Tolmai, and Mattityahu, and Toma, and Ya’akov I the sonof Chalfai, and Taddai, and Shimon the Zealot;
3.19: and Yehudah I fromK’riot, who also delivered Him up.
3.20: And He came home, and the crowed came together again, to such an extent that they could not even eat bread.
3.21: And when His own people heard it, they went out to take custody of Him; for they were saying, " He is displaced. "
3.22: And the scribes who came down from Yerushalayim were saying, " He is possessed by Ba’al - zibbul. And by the ruler of the demons He casts out the demons. "
3.23: And He called them to Himself, and began speaking to them in parables, " How can HaSatan cast out HaSatan?
3.24: " And if a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom will not have the power to stand.
3.25: " And if a house is divided against itself, that house will not have the power to stand.
3.26: " And if HaSatan has risen up against himself and is divided, he does not have the power to stand; his end has come.
3.27: " But no one can enter the strong man’s house and plunder his goods, unless he first binds the strong man, and then he may plunder his house.
3.28: " Truly I say to you, all sins shall be forgiven I ofthe sons of men, and I themany blasphemies they blaspheme.
3.29: " But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit never has forgiveness, but is guilty of an eternal sin " - -
3.30: because they were saying, " He has an unclean spirit. "
3.31: And His mother and brothers came; and standing outside they sent to Him, and called Him.
3.32: And a crowd was sitting around Him, and they said to Him, " Behold, Your mother and your brothers are outside, looking for You. "
3.33: And answering them, He said, " Who are My mother and My brothers? "
3.34: And looking around on those who were sitting around Him, He said, " Behold, My mother and My brothers!
3.35: " For whoever does the will of God, he is my brother, and sister, and mother. "

4.1: And He began again to teach by the sea. And such a very great crowd gathered to Him that He got into a boat on the sea and sat down; and all the crowd was by the sea on the land.
4.2: And He was teaching them many things in parables, and in His teaching He said to them:
4.3: " Listen! Behold, the sower went out to sow;
4.4: " and it happened that as he was sowing, some I seedfell beside the road, and the birds came and devoured it.
4.5: " And other I seedfell on the rocky I ground, where it did not have much soil; and immediately it sprang up, because it had no depth of soil.
4.6: " But when the sun had risen, it was scorched; and because it had no root, it withered away.
4.7: " And another fell among the thorns, and the thorns came up and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.
4.8: " And another fell into the good soil and came up I out of the groundand increased, yielding a fruit thirty, sixty, and a hundredfold. "
4.9: And He said, " He who has ears, let him hear. "
4.10: And when He was alone, His followers along with the twelve, asked Him I aboutthe parables.
4.11: And He was saying to them, " To you has been given the mystery of the Kingdom of God; but those who are outside get everything in parables,
4.12: " in order that while seeing they may see and not perceive; and while hearing they may hear and not understand, lest they return and be forgiven. "
4.13: And He said to them, " Do you not understand this parable? And how, then, will you understand all the parables?
4.15: " And these are the ones who are beside the road where the word is sown; and when they hear, immediately HaSatan comes and takes away the word which has been sown in them.
4.16: " And in a similar manner these are the ones on whom seed was sown on the rocky I ground, who, when they hear the word, immediately receive it with joy;
4.17: " and they have no root in themselves, but I endurefor a season; then, when tribulation or persecution arises because of the word, immediately they stumble.
4.18: " And others are the ones on whom seed was sown among the thorns; these are the ones who have heard the word,
4.19: " and the anxieties of this age, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the desires for other things enter in and choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
4.20: " But those are the ones on whom seed was sown on the good soil; and they hear the word and accept it, and bear fruit, thirty, sixty, and a hundredfold. "
4.21: And He said to them, " A lamp is not brought to be put under a peck - measure, is it, or under a bed? Is it not I broughtto be put on the lampstand?
4.22: " For nothing is hidden, except to be made visible; nor has I anythingbeen secret, except to come to light.
4.23: " If any man has ears to hear, let him hear. "
4.24: And He was saying to them, " Take heed what you listen to. By your standard of measure it will be measured to you; and more shall be given you besides.
4.25: " For whoever has, to him I morewill be given; and whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him. "
4.26: And He said, " The Kingdom of God is like a man who casts spores upon the soil;
4.27: " and goes to sleep at night and wakes up by day, and the spore sprouts up and lengthens - - how, he himself does not know.
4.28: " The soil produces fruit by itself; first the stalk, then the head, then the full grain on the head.
4.29: " But when the fruit delivers, he immediately puts in the sickle, because the harvest has come. "
4.30: And He said, " To what may we compare the Kingdom of God, or by what parable shall we present it?
4.31: " It islike a mustard grain, which, when sown upon the soil, though it is smaller than all the seeds that are upon the Earth;
4.32: " yet when it is sown, it grows up and becomes larger than all the shrubs and forms large branches, so that the birds of the air can nest in its shade. "
4.33: And with many such parables He was speaking the word to them, as they had the power to hear it.
4.34: He did not speak to them without a parable; but He was explaining everything alone to His own disciples.
4.35: And on that day when evening had come, He said to them, " Let us go across to the other side. "
4.36: And leaving the crowd, they took Him alongside with them, just as He was, in the boat; and other boats were with Him.
4.37: And there came a fierce gale of wind, and the waves beat into the boat, so much that the boat was already filling up.
4.38: And He Himself was at the stern, asleep on the pillow; and they woke Him and said to Him, " Teacher, do You not care if we are perishing? "
4.39: And being aroused, He rebuked the wind and said to the sea, " Silence! Be still! " And the wind grew weary, and there was a great calm.
4.40: And He said to them, " Why are you so cowardly? How is it that you have no faith? "
4.41: And they became very afraid and said to one another, " Who then is this, that even the wind and sea obey Him? "

5.1: And they came to the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gerasenes.
5.2: And when He had come out of the boat, immediately a man from out of the tombs with an unclean spirit met Him,
5.3: who had been living in the tombs. And no one had the power to bind him any more, even with a chain;
5.4: because he had often been bound with shackles and chains, and the chains had been torn apart by him, and the shackles broken to pieces, and no one was strong I enoughto tame him.
5.5: And on account of all this, night and day, in the tombs and in the mountains, he was screaming out and cutting himself up with stones.
5.6: And seeing Yeshua from afar, he ran up and bowed down before Him;
5.7: and screaming out with a great voice, he said, " What have You to do with me, Yeshua, Son of the Most High God? I implore You by God, do not torment me! "
5.8: For He said to him, " Come out of the man, you unclean spirit! "
5.9: And He was questioning him, " What is your name? " And he said to Him, " My name is Legion; for we are many. "
5.10: And he begged Him much, that I Henot send them out of the country.
5.11: Now there was a great herd of pigs feeding there on the mountain.
5.12: And I the demonsbegged Him, saying, " Send us into the pigs so that we may enter them. "
5.13: And He granted them permission. And coming out, the unclean spirits entered the pigs; and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea, I numberingabout two thousand; and they were drowned in the sea.
5.14: And their herdsmen fled and reported it in the city and in the country. And I peoplecame to see what it was that had occurred.
5.15: And they came to Yeshua and saw the demoniac sitting down, clothed and of sound mind, the man who had the legion; and they became frightened.
5.16: And those who had seen it gave an account to them about what had happened to the demoniac, and about the pigs.
5.17: And they began to beg Him to depart from their region.
5.18: And as He was getting into the boat, the man who had been possessed by demons begged Him that he might accompany Him.
5.19: And He did not let him, but He said to him, " Go home to your people and report to them how much the Lord has done for you, and I howHe had mercy on you. "
5.20: And he went away and began to proclaim in Dekapolis how much Yeshua had done for him; and everyone marveled.
5.21: And when Yeshua had crossed over again to the other side, a great crowd gathered around Him; and He stayed by the seashore.
5.22: And one of the synagogue leaders, named Yair, came up, and upon seeing Him fell down at His feet,
5.23: and besought Him much, saying, " My little daughter is at the point of death. Come and lay Your hands on her that she may be saved and live. "
5.24: And He went with him. And a great crowd was following Him and pressing in on Him.
5.25: And a woman who had a hemorrhage for twelve years,
5.26: and had suffered much under many physicians, and had spent all that she had and was not helped at all, but rather had become worse,
5.27: after hearing about Yeshua, came up behind I Himin the crowd, and touched His garment.
5.28: For she thought, " If I just touch His garments, I shall be saved. "
5.29: And immediately the flow of her blood was dried up; and she felt in her body that she was healed of her affliction.
5.30: And immediately, Yeshua, recognizing in Himself that power from Him had gone forth, turned around in the crowd and said, " Who touched My garments? "
5.31: And His disciples said to Him, " You see the crowd pressing in on You, and You say, 'Who touched Me? ' "
5.32: And He looked around to see who had done this.
5.33: But the woman, fearing and trembling, aware of what had been done to her, came and prostrated before Him, and told Him the whole truth.
5.34: And He said to her, " Daughter, your faith has saved you; go in peace, and be healed of your affliction. "
5.35: While He was still speaking, they came from the I house ofthe synagogue leader, saying, " Your daughter has died. Why trouble the Teacher any more? "
5.36: But Yeshua, overhearing what was being said, told the synagogue leader, " Do not be afraid, only believe. "
5.37: And He allowed no one to follow Him, except Petros and Ya’akov and Yochanan the brother of Ya’akov.
5.38: And they came to the house of the synagogue leader; and He beheld an uproar, and much weeping and wailing.
5.39: And entering in, He said to them, " Why make an uproar and weep? The child has not died, but is sleeping. "
5.40: And they I werelaughing at Him. But putting them all out, He took alongside the child’s father and mother and His own I companions, and entered where the child was.
5.41: And taking the child by the hand, He said to her, " Talitha kumi! " - - which translated means, " Little girl, I say to you, arise! "
5.42: And immediately the girl arose and was walking; for she was twelve years old. And immediately they were overcome with amazement.
5.43: And He strictly ordered them that no one should know about this; and He said that I somethingshould be given to her to eat.

6.1: And He went out from there and came into His own country; and His disciples followed Him.
6.2: And when the Shabbat came, He began to teach in the synagogue; and the many hearers were astonished, saying, " Where did this Man I getall this, and what is the wisdom given to Him, and such miracles as these performed by His hands?
6.3: " Is this not the craftsman, the son of Miriam, and brother of Ya’akov, and Yosi, and Yehudah, and Shimon? And are not his sisters here with us? " And they took offense at Him.
6.4: And Yeshua said to them, " A Prophet is not dishonored, except in his own country and among His kindred and in His house. "
6.5: And He could do no miracle there, except that He laid His hands upon a few sick people and healed them.
6.6: And He marveled because of their unbelief. And He was going around the villages teaching.
6.7: And He called the twelve and began to send them out two - by - two; and He was giving them power over the unclean spirits;
6.8: and He charged them that they should take nothing for I theirway, except a staff; no bread, no bag, no money in their belt;
6.9: but to wear sandals and not put on two tunics.
6.10: And He said to them, " Wherever you enter a house, stay there until you leave there.
6.11: " And if any place that does not receive you or listen to you, as you go out from there shake the dust from below your feet for a testimony against them. "
6.12: And they went out and proclaimed that I menshould repent.
6.13: And they were casting out many demons, and were anointing with oil many sick, and were healing them.
6.14: And King Herodes heard, for His name had become manifest, and I somewere saying, " Yochanan the Immerser has risen from the dead; that is why these powers are at work in Him. "
6.15: Others said, " It is Eliyahu, " I andothers said, " It is a Prophet, like one of the prophets I of old. "
6.16: But when Herodes heard, he said, " Yochanan, whom I beheaded, has risen! "
6.17: For Herodes himself had sent and had Yochanan seized and bound in prison on account of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philippos, because he had married her.
6.18: For Yochanan had been saying to Herodes, " It is not permitted for you to have your brother’s wife. "
6.19: And Herodias had a grudge against him and wanted to put him to death. But she could not,
6.20: for Herodes feared Yochanan, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and kept him close. And when he heard him, he was very perplexed; and yet he heard him gladly.
6.21: And a seasonable day came when Herodes on his birthday gave a banquet for his chiefs and his commanders and the leading men of Galil,
6.22: and when the daughter of Herodias herself came in and danced, she pleased Herodes and his dinner guests; and the king said to the girl, " Ask me for whatever you wish, and I shall grant it. "
6.23: And he swore to her, " Whatever you ask of me, I will give you; up to half of my kingdom. "
6.24: And she went out and said to her mother, " Forwhat shall I ask? " And she said, " The head of Yochanan the Immerser. "
6.25: And she came in immediately with haste before the king, and asked, saying, " I want you to give me, at once, the head of Yochanan the Immerser on a platter. "
6.26: And although the king was deeply saddened, because of his oaths and because of his dinner guests, he was unwilling to refuse her.
