6.27: And immediately the king sent an executioner and commanded I himto bring his head. He went and had him beheaded in the prison,
6.28: and brought his head on a platter, and gave it to the girl; and the girl gave it to her mother.
6.29: And when his disciples heard, they came and took away his body, and laid it in a tomb.
6.30: And the apostles gathered together with Yeshua; and they reported to Him all that they had done and taught.
6.31: And He said to them, " Come away by yourselves to a solitary place, and rest a little " - - for many were coming and going, and they did not even have the opportunity to eat.
6.32: And they went away in a boat to a solitary place by themselves.
6.33: And I manysaw them going, and many recognized I them, and they ran there together on foot from all the cities, and got there ahead of them.
6.34: And when He went ashore He saw a great crowd; and He had compassion on them because they were like sheep without a shepherd. And He began to teach them many things.
6.35: And when it was already a late hour, His disciples came up to Him and said, " This place is solitary and it is already a late hour;
6.36: " send them away so that they might go into the surrounding country and villages and buy themselves something to eat. "
6.37: But He answered and said to them, " You give them I somethingto eat. " And they said to Him, " Shall we go and spend two hundred denarii I worthof bread, and give it to them to eat? "
6.38: And He said to them, " How many I loaves ofbread do you have? Go see. " And when they had been I made aware, they said, " Five, and two fish. "
6.39: And He commanded them all to sit down by groups on the green grass.
6.40: And they sat down in groups of hundreds and of fifties.
6.41: And He took the five I loaves ofbread and the two fish, and He looked up toward Heaven. He blessed I itand broke the I loaves ofbread and He was giving I themto His disciples to set before them; and He divided up the two fish among them all.
6.42: And they all ate and were satisfied.
6.43: And they took up twelve full baskets of the broken pieces, and also of the fish.
6.44: And those who ate the I loaves ofbread were five thousand men.
6.45: And immediately He made His disciples get into the boat, and go before I Himto the other side to Beit - Tzaidah, while He Himself was sending the crowd away.
6.46: And after He had taken leave of them, He departed to the mountain to pray.
6.47: And when it was evening, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and He I wasalone on the land.
6.48: And seeing them tortured at the oars, for the wind was against them; at about the forth watch of the night He came to them, walking on the sea, and He meant to pass by them.
6.49: But when they saw Him walking on the sea, they supposed that it was a phantasm, and cried out;
6.50: for they all saw Him and were frightened. But immediately He spoke to them and said to them, " Take courage; it is I, do not be afraid. "
6.51: And He got into the boat with them, and the wind grew weary. And they were utterly beside themselves,
6.52: for they did not understand about the I loaves ofbread, but their heart was hardened.
6.53: And when they had crossed over they came to land at Ginosar, and moored to the shore.
6.54: And when they had gotten out of the boat, immediately I the peoplerecognized Him,
6.55: and ran about the whole neighborhood and began to carry about on their pallets those who were sick, to the place where they heard He was.
6.56: And wherever He came, to villages, or cities, or I thecountry, they were laying the sick in the market places, and begging Him that they might just touch the tzit - tzit of His garment; and as many as touched it were saved.

7.1: And the Pharisees and certain ones of the scribes gathered together toward Him when they had come from Yerushalayim,
7.2: and had seen that some of His disciples were eating their bread with common hands, that is, unwashed.
7.3: For the Pharisees and all the Yehudim do not eat unless they wash the hands to the wrist, holding to the traditions of the elders;
7.4: and I when they comefrom the marketplace, they do not eat unless they sprinkle themselves; and there are many other things which they have taken alongside in order to hold, such as the immersion of cups and pitchers and copper pots.
7.5: And the Pharisees and the scribes asked Him, " Why do your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat their bread with common hands? "
7.6: And He said to them, " Rightly did Yeshayahu prophecy of you hypocrites, as it is written, 'THIS PEOPLE HONORS ME WITH THEIR LIPS, BUT THEIR HEART IS FAR FROM ME;
7.7: " 'IN VAIN DO THEY WORSHIP ME, TEACHING AS DOCTRINES THE INJUNCTIONS OF MEN. '
7.8: " Forsaking the commandment of God, you hold fast to the tradition of men. "
7.9: And He also said to them, " You nicely do away with the commandment of God, in order to keep your tradition.
7.10: " For Moshe said, 'HONOR YOUR FATHER AND YOUR MOTHER'; and, 'HE WHO SPEAKS EVIL OF FATHER OR MOTHER, LET HIM BE PUT TO DEATH';
7.11: " but you say, 'If a man says to I hisfather or mother, " Anything of mine you might have benefited from is korban " ' - - that is, a gift I to God - -
7.12: " you no longer permit him to do anything for I hisfather or mother;
7.13: " revoking the Word of God by your tradition which you have handed down; and you do many things much like that. "
7.14: And after He called the crowd to Him again, He said to them, " Hear Me, all of you, and understand:
7.15: " there is nothing outside the man which entering into him has the power to make him common; but the things which go forth out of the man are what make the man common.
7.16: " If any man has ears to hear, let him hear. "
7.17: And when leaving the crowd, He had entered the house, His disciples questioned Him about the parable.
7.18: And He said to them, " Are you also without understanding? Do you not understand that whatever enters into the man from outside cannot make him common?
7.19: " This isbecause it does not go into his heart, but into his stomach, and goes out into the latrine, purging all the foods. "
7.20: And He said, " That which goes forth out of the man, that is what makes him common.
7.21: " For from within, out of the heart of men, go forth the evil reasonings, fornications, thefts, murders, adulteries,
7.22: " covetousness, wickedness, deceit, licentiousness, an evil eye, pride, foolishness.
7.23: " All these evil things go fourth I fromwithin and make the man common. "
7.24: And from there He arose and went away to the borders of Tzor. And when He had entered a house, He wanted no one to know I of it, yet He could not escape notice.
7.25: But after hearing about Him, a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit, immediately came and fell down at His feet.
7.26: Now the woman was a Greek, of the Syrophoenician race. And she kept asking Him to cast the demon out of her daughter.
7.27: And He said to her, " Let the children be satisfied first, for it is not good to take the children’s bread, and cast it to the dogs. "
7.28: But she answered and said to Him, " Yes. Lord. I Buteven the dogs underneath the table eat on the children’s crumbs. "
7.29: And He said to her, " Because of this word, go on; the demon has come out of your daughter. "
7.30: And going away to her home, she found the child lying on the bed, the demon having come out.
7.31: And again He went out from the borders of Tzor, and came through Tzidon to the Sea of Galil, within the borders of Dekapolis.
7.32: And they brought to Him one who was deaf and spoke with impediment, and they begged Him to lay His hand upon him.
7.33: And He took him aside from the crowd by himself, I andput His fingers into his ears, and after spitting, He touched his tongue;
7.34: and looking up to Heaven with a deep groan, He said to Him, " Ephphatha! " That is, " Be opened! "
7.35: And His ears were opened, and the bond of his tongue was released, and he was speaking correctly.
7.36: And He charged them not to tell anyone; but the more He charged them, the more abundantly they proclaimed it.
7.37: And they were exceedingly astonished, saying, " He has done all things well; both the deaf He makes to hear, and the dumb to speak. "

8.1: In those days again, when there was a great crowd, and they had nothing to eat, He called to His disciples, and said to them,
8.2: " I feel compassion for the crowd because they have continued with Me now three days, and have nothing to eat;
8.3: " and if I send them away hungry to their houses, they will grow weary on the road; and some of them have come from afar. "
8.4: And His disciples answered Him, " Fromwhere will anyone be able to satisfy these men with bread here in a wilderness? "
8.5: And He was asking them, " How many loaves do you have? " And they said, " Seven. "
8.6: And He commanded the crowd to sit down on the ground; and taking the seven loaves, He gave thanks and broke them, and gave them to His disciples to set before them, and they set them before the crowd.
8.7: And they also had a few small fish; and having blessed them, He said I forthese to be set before I themalso.
8.8: And they ate and were satisfied; and they picked up seven large baskets full of the broken pieces.
8.9: And about four thousand were I there; and He sent them away.
8.10: And immediately He stepped onto the boat with His disciples, and came to the district of Dalmanuta.
8.11: And the Pharisees came out and began to dispute with Him, seeking from Him a sign from Heaven, to test Him.
8.12: And having sighed deeply in His spirit, He said, " Why does this generation seek after a sign? Truly, I say to you, no sign shall be given to this generation. "
8.13: And He left them, and again stepped onto I the boatand went away to the other side.
8.14: And they had forgotten to take bread; and did not have more than one loaf with them in the boat.

9.46: " where their worm does not die, and the fire is not extinguished.

9.48: " where their worm does not die, and the fire is not extinguished.

13.15: " let him who is on the housetop not go down or enter in, to take anything out of his house;

13.17: " But woe to those who are with child and to those who nurse in those days!
13.18: " But pray that this will not take place in the winter.
13.19: " For those days shall be tribulation, such as has not occurred since the beginning of the creation which God created until now, and never shall I be.
13.20: " And unless the Lord had shortened the days, no flesh would have been saved; but for the sake of the elect whom He chose, He shortened the days.
13.21: " And then if anyone says to you, 'Behold, here is the Messiah! '; or, 'Behold, there I He is! '; do not believe;
13.22: " for false messiahs and false prophets will arise, and will show signs and wonders, in order, if possible, to lead the elect astray.
13.23: " But take heed. Behold, I have told you everything beforehand.

13.25: " AND THE STARS WILL BE FALLING FROM HEAVEN, and the powers that are in the heavens will be shaken.

13.32: " But of that day and hour, no one knows, not even the angels in Heaven, nor the Son, but I onlythe Father.
13.33: " Take heed, keep awake; for you do not know when the right time is.
13.34: " It islike a man, away on a journey I abroad, having left his house and giving his slaves the authority, and I assigningto each one his work, also commanded the doorkeeper to keep watch.
13.35: " Therefore you also must be ready too; for the Son of Man is coming at an hour when you do not think I He will,
13.36: " lest He comes suddenly and finds you sleeping.
13.37: " And what I say to you, I say to all: 'Watch! ' "

14.22: And while they were eating, He took bread, and after a blessing He broke I it; and gave I itto them and said, " Receive; this is My body. "
14.23: And having taken a cup, I andgiven thanks, He gave I itto them; and they all drank of it.
14.24: And He said to them, " This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many.

14.26: And after singing a praise, they went forth to the Mount of Olives.

14.31: But he said insistently, " If it is necessary to die with You, I will not deny You! " And they were all saying the same in like manner.
14.32: And they came to a spot called Gat’Sh’manim; and He said to His disciples, " Sit here, while I pray. "

14.66: And as Petros was below in the courtyard, one of the maidservants of the high priest came,

14.68: But he denied I it, saying, " I neither know nor understand what you are speaking I of. " And he went out to the gateway.

15.30: " save Yourself, and come down from the cross! "

16.1: And when the Shabbat had elapsed, Miriam of Magdala and Miriam the I motherof Ya’akov, and Shlomit, brought spices so they might come and anoint Him.
16.2: And very early on the first of the week, they came to the tomb, when the sun had risen.
16.3: And they were saying to themselves, " Who will roll away the stone for us from the entrance of the tomb? "
16.4: And looking up, they saw that the stone had been rolled back, for it was very great.
16.5: And entering the tomb, they saw a young man sitting at the right; and they were amazed.
16.6: And he said to them, " Do not be amazed; you seek Yeshua the Naztrati, the crucified. He is risen! He is not here; behold, I here isthe place where they laid Him.
16.7: " But go, tell His disciples and Petros, 'He is going ahead of you into Galil; there you will see Him, just as He told you. "
16.8: And they went out and fled from the tomb, for trembling and astonishment had seized them; and they said nothing to anyone, for they were afraid.
16.9: Now after He had risen early on the first of the week, He first appeared to Miriam of Magdala, from whom He had cast out seven demons.
16.10: She went and reported to those who had been with Him, as they mourned and wept.

16.15: And He said to them, " Go into all the world and proclaim the good news to all creation.
16.16: " He who has believed and has been immersed will be saved; but he who has disbelieved will be condemned.

16.18: " they will pick up serpents, and if they drink any deadly I poison, it will not hurt them; they will lay hands on the sick, and they will recover. "

1.1: Inasmuch as many have attempted to arrange a narrative of the things brought to full measure among us,
1.2: just as they were handed down to us by those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and ministers of the word,
1.3: it seemed fitting for me as well, having investigated all with exactness from the beginning, to write I itout for you in successive order, most noble Theophilos;
1.4: so that you might know the certainty about the words you have been taught.
1.5: In the days of Herodes, king of Yehudah, there was a certain priest by the name of Zekaryah, of the division of Aviyah; and he had a wife from the daughters of Aharon, and her name was Elisheva.
1.6: And they were both righteous before God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord.
1.7: But they had no child, because Elisheva was barren, and both were advanced in their days.
1.8: Now it came about, while he was performing his priestly service before God in the order of his division,
1.9: according to the ethic of the priesthood, he was chosen by lot to enter the Temple of the Lord and burn incense.
1.10: And the whole number of the people were praying outside at the hour of the incense I offering.
1.11: And there appeared to him an angel of the Lord, standing to the right of the altar of incense.
1.12: And Zekaryah was troubled when he saw I him, and fear fell upon him.
1.13: But the angel said to him, " Do not be afraid, Zekaryah, for your supplication has been heard, and your wife Elisheva will bear you a son, and you will call his name Yochanan.
1.14: " And you will have joy and gladness, and many will rejoice at his birth.
1.15: " For he will be great in the sight of the Lord, and he will drink no wine or liquor, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit, even from his mother’s womb.
1.16: " And he will return many of the sons of Yisrael to the Lord their God.
1.17: " And he will go before Him in the spirit and power of Eliyahu, TO RETURN THE HEARTS OF THE FATHERS BACK TO THE CHILDREN, and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous; to make ready for the Lord a people prepared. "
1.18: And Zekaryah said to the angel, " How shall I know this? For I am an old man, and my wife is advanced in her days. "
1.19: And the angel answered and said to him, " I am Gavriel, who stands in the sight of God; and I was sent to speak to you, and to bring you this good news.
1.20: " And behold, you will be silent and unable to speak until the day when these things occur, because you did not believe my words, which shall be fulfilled in their right time. "
1.21: And the people were waiting for Zekaryah, and were wondering at his delay in the Temple.
1.22: When he came out, he could not talk to them; and they realized that he had seen a vision in the Temple; and he was making signs to them, but remained mute.
1.23: And it came about, when the days of his ministry were ended, that he went back home.
1.24: And after these days Elisheva his wife conceived; and she kept herself in seclusion for five months, saying,
1.25: " This is the way the Lord has dealt with me when He looked on I me, to take away my disgrace among men. "
1.26: In the sixth month the angel Gavriel was sent from God to a city in Galil, named Natzeret,
1.27: to a virgin betrothed to a man whose name was Yosef, of the House of Daveed; and the virgin’s name was Miriam.
1.28: And coming in, he said to her, " Hail, O favored one! The Lord is with you. "
1.29: But she was greatly troubled at his word, and considered what kind of greeting this might be.
1.30: And the angel said to her, " Do not be afraid, Miriam, for you have found grace with God.
1.31: " And behold, you will conceive in your womb and bear a son, and you shall call His name Yeshua.
1.32: " He will be great, and will be called the Son of the Most High; and the Lord God will give Him the throne of His father Daveed;
1.33: " and He will reign over the House of Ya’akov forever; and His Kingdom will have no end. "
1.34: And Miriam said to the angel, " How can this be, since I have no husband? "
1.35: And the angel answered and said to her, " The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; and for that reason the Holy - begotten shall be called the Son of God.
1.36: " And behold, even your kinswoman Elisheva has also conceived a son in her old age; and this is the sixth month to her who was called barren.
1.37: " For nothing is impossible with God. "
1.38: And Miriam said, " Behold, the slave of the Lord; let it be to me according to your spoken word. " And the angel departed from her.
1.39: In those days Miriam arose and went with haste to the hill country, to a city of Yehudah,
1.40: and entered into the house of Zekaryah and greeted Elisheva.
1.41: And it came about that when Elisheva heard the greeting of Miriam, the unborn baby leaped in her womb; and Elisheva was filled full of the Holy Spirit.
1.42: And she exclaimed with a great cry, and said, " Blessed I areyou among women, and blessed I isthe fruit of your womb!
1.43: " And how has it I happenedto me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
1.44: " For behold, when the voice of your greeting came to my ears, the unborn baby in my womb leaped for joy.
1.45: " And blessed I isshe who believed that there would be a completion of what had been spoken to her by her Lord. "
1.46: And Miriam said, " MY SOUL EXALTS the Lord,
1.47: " AND my spirit HAS REJOICED IN GOD MY SAVIOR.
1.48: " FOR HE HAS LOOKED ON THE LOW ESTATE OF HIS SLAVE. For behold, from now onward all generations will count me blessed.
1.49: " For the Mighty One has done great things for me; and holy is His name.
1.50: " AND HIS MERCY I isTO GENERATIONS OF GENERATIONS TOWARD THOSE WHO FEAR HIM.
1.51: " He has shown His strength with His arm; He has dispersed the proud in the thoughts of their heart.
1.52: " He has brought down rulers from I theirthrones, and has raised up those who were humble.
1.53: " HE HAS FILLED THE HUNGRY WITH GOOD THINGS; and the rich He has sent away empty.
1.54: " He has received again Yisrael His servant, in remembrance of His mercy,
1.55: " as He spoke to our fathers, to Avraham and his sperm forever. "
1.56: And Miriam stayed with her about three months, and I thenreturned to her home.
1.57: Now the time was fulfilled for Elisheva to give birth, and she brought forth a son.
1.58: And her neighbors and her relatives heard that the Lord had shown great mercy to her; and they were rejoicing with her.
1.59: And it came about that on the eighth day they came to circumcise the child, and they were going to call him Zekaryah, after his father.
1.60: But his mother answered and said, " Not so; he shall be called Yochanan. "
1.61: And they said to her, " There is no one among your relatives who is called by that name. "
1.62: And they nodded to his father, as to what he wanted him called.
1.63: And he asked for a writing tablet, and wrote, saying, " His name is Yochanan. " And they all marveled.
1.64: And instantly his mouth was opened and his tongue I loosed, and he was speaking, praising God.
1.65: And fear came on all those dwelling around them; and all these spoken words were being talked about in the hill country of Yehudah.
1.66: And all who heard them laid them up in their hearts, saying, " What then will this child be? For the hand of the Lord was certainly with him. "
1.67: And his father Zekaryah was filled full of the Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying:
1.68: " Blessed I bethe Lord God of Yisrael, for He has visited us and made redemption for His people,
1.69: " and has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the House of Daveed, His servant - -
1.70: " as He spoke by the mouth of His holy prophets from of old - -
1.71: " SALVATION FROM OUR ENEMIES, AND OUT OF THE HAND OF ALL WHO HATE US;
1.72: " to perform mercy toward our fathers, and to remember His holy covenant,
1.73: " the oath which He swore to Avraham our father,
1.74: " to grant us that we, being delivered out of the hand of our enemies, might serve Him without fear,
1.75: " in holiness and righteousness before Him all our days.
1.76: " And you, child, will be called the prophet of the Most High; for you will go on before the Lord to prepare His ways;
1.77: " to give knowledge of salvation to His people in forgiveness of their sins,
1.78: " because of the tender mercy of our God, in which the rising from on High did look upon us,
1.79: " to shine upon those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death, to make straight our feet into the way of peace. "
1.80: And the child grew and became strong in spirit, and he lived in the deserts until the day of his public appearance in Yisrael.

2.1: Now it came about in those days that a decree went out from Caesar Augustus, that a census be taken of all the inhabited Earth.
2.2: This was the first census that took place while Kurenios was governor of Suria.
2.3: And all were going to be enrolled, each to his own city.
2.4: And Yosef also went up from Galil, from the city of Natzeret, to Yehudah, to the city of Daveed, which is called Beit - Lechem, because he was of the house and lineage of Daveed,
2.5: to be enrolled together with Miriam, his betrothed, who was pregnant.
2.6: And it came to pass, in their being there, the days were completed for her to give birth.
2.7: And she brought fourth her first - born Son; and she wrapped Him in swaddling cloths, and laid Him in a feeding trough, because there was no place for them in the inn.
2.8: And in the same region there were shepherds staying out in the fields, and guarding their flock by night.
2.9: And an angel of the Lord stood over them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them; and they were greatly frightened.
2.10: And the angel said to them, " Do not be afraid; for behold, I announce to you good news of a great joy which will come to all the people;
2.11: " for to you is born today in the city of Daveed a Savior, Who is Messiah the Lord.
2.12: " And this I will bea sign for you: you will find a baby wrapped in swaddling cloths, and lying in a feeding trough. "
2.13: And suddenly there came with the angel a multitude of the Heavenly host, praising God and saying,
2.14: " Glory to God in the highest, and on Earth peace among men with whom He is pleased! "
2.15: And it came about when the angels had gone away from them into Heaven, that the shepherds said to one another, " Let us go over to Beit - Lechem, then, and see this spoken word that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us. "
2.16: And they went with haste and found Miriam and Yosef and the Baby lying in the feeding trough.
2.17: And when they had seen this, they made known the spoken word which had been told to them concerning this Child;
2.18: and all who heard it wondered at what the shepherds told them.
2.19: But Miriam preserved all these spoken words, pondering them in her heart.
2.20: And the shepherds went back, glorifying and praising God for all that they had heard and seen, as it had been told them.
2.21: And when eight days were completed to circumcise I the Child, His name was called Yeshua, having been so called by the angel before He was conceived in the womb.
2.22: And when the days for their cleansing according to the Torah of Moshe were completed, they brought Him up to Yerushalayim to present Him to the Lord
2.23: as it is written in the Torah of the Lord, " EVERY I first - bornMALE THAT OPENS THE WOMB SHALL BE CALLED HOLY TO ADONAI, "
2.24: and to offer a sacrifice according to what is said in the Torah of the Lord, " A PAIR OF TURTLEDOVES, OR TWO YOUNG PIGEONS. "
2.25: And behold, there was a man in Yerushalayim whose name was Shimon; and this man was righteous and devout, waiting anxiously for the consolation of Yisrael; and the Holy Spirit was upon him.
2.26: And it had been divinely told to him by the Holy Spirit that he would not see death before he had seen the Messiah of the Lord.
2.27: And he came in the Spirit into the Temple; and when the parents brought in the Child Yeshua, to do for Him the ethic of the Torah,
2.28: then he received Him into his arms, and blessed God, and said,
2.29: " Now Lord, You will let Your slave depart in peace according to Your word;
2.30: " because my eyes have seen Your salvation,
2.31: " which You have prepared in the presence of all peoples,
2.32: " A LIGHT OF REVELATION TO THE NATIONS, and the glory of Your people, Yisrael. "
2.33: And His father and mother were amazed at what was said about Him;
2.34: and Shimon blessed them, and said to Miriam His mother, " Behold, this I Childis set for the fall and rise of many in Yisrael, and for a sign that is spoken against - -
2.35: " and a sword will pierce even your own soul, that the thoughts out of many hearts may be revealed. "
2.36: And there was a prophetess, Channah, the daughter of Peneu’el, of the tribe of Asher. She was advanced in years, having lived with a husband seven years after her marriage,
2.37: and then as a widow to the age of eighty - four. And she never left the Temple, serving night and day with fastings and prayers.
2.38: And at that very hour she stood up and was acknowledging fully to God, and was speaking of Him to all those who were waiting anxiously for the redemption of Yerushalayim.
2.39: And when they had performed everything according to the Torah of the Lord, they returned to Galil, to their own city of Natzeret.
2.40: And the Child grew and became strong, being filled in wisdom; and the grace of God was upon Him.
2.41: And His parents were going yearly to Yerushalayim, at the festival of the Pesach.
2.42: And when He became twelve, they went up according to the ethic of the festival;
2.43: and having finished the days, in their going back the Child Yeshua stayed behind in Yerushalayim, but Yosef and His mother did not know,
2.44: but supposing Him to be in the caravan they went a day’s journey; and they were looking carefully for Him among their relatives and acquaintances.
2.45: And when they did not find Him, they turned back toward Yerushalayim, looking carefully for Him.
2.46: And it came about that after three days they found Him in the Temple, sitting in the middle of the teachers, both listening to them and asking them questions.
2.47: And all who heard Him were amazed at His insight and His answers.
2.48: And when they saw Him they were astonished; and His mother said to Him, " Child, why did You do so to us? "
2.49: And He said to them, " Why is it that you were seeking Me? Did you not know that it is necessary for Me to be in My Father’s I house? "
2.50: And they did not understand the spoken word which He spoke to them.

2.52: And Yeshua kept advancing in wisdom and maturity, and in favor with God and men.

3.4: as it is written in the scroll of the words of Yeshayahu the prophet, " THE VOICE OF ONE CRYING IN THE WILDERNESS, 'MAKE READY THE WAY OF ADONAI, MAKE HIS PATHS STRAIGHT.
3.5: " EVERY VALLEY SHALL BE FILLED, AND EVERY MOUNTAIN AND HILL SHALL BE MADE LOW; AND THE CROOKED SHALL BECOME STRAIGHT, AND THE ROUGH WAYS SMOOTH;
3.6: " AND ALL FLESH SHALL SEE THE SALVATION OF GOD. "

3.8: " Therefore bear fruits worthy of repentance, and do not begin to say to yourselves, 'We have Avraham our father, ' for I say to you that God has the power from these stones to raise up children to Avraham.

4.1: And Yeshua, full of the Holy Spirit, turned back from the Yarden and was led by the Spirit in the wilderness
4.2: forty days, being tempted by the Devil. And He ate nothing in those days; and when they had ended, He hungered.
4.3: The Devil said to Him, " If You are the Son of God, speak to this stone I for itto become bread. "
4.4: And Yeshua answered Him, " It is written, 'MAN SHALL NOT LIVE BY BREAD ALONE. ' "
4.5: And he brought Him up and showed Him all the kingdoms of the inhabited Earth in a moment of time.
4.6: And the Devil said to Him, " I will give you all this authority and its glory; for it has been delivered to me, and I give it to whomever I wish.
4.7: " Therefore, if You worship before me, it will all be Yours. "
4.8: And Yeshua answered and said to him, " It is written, 'YOU SHALL WORSHIP ADONAI YOUR GOD, AND HIM ONLY SHALL YOU SERVE. ' "
4.9: And he led Him to Yerushalayim and had Him stand on the pinnacle of the Temple, and said to Him, " If You are the Son of God, throw Yourself down from here;
4.10: " for it is written, 'HE WILL GIVE HIS ANGELS CHARGE CONCERNING YOU, TO GUARD YOU, '
4.11: " and, 'ON I theirHANDS THEY WILL RAISE YOU UP, LEST YOU STRIKE YOUR FOOT AGAINST A STONE. ' "
4.12: And Yeshua answered and said to him, " It is said, 'YOU SHALL NOT PUT ADONAI YOUR GOD TO THE TEST. ' "
4.13: And when the Devil had finished every temptation, he departed from Him until an opportune season.
4.14: And Yeshua turned back to Galil in the power of the Spirit; and news about Him went throughout all the surrounding region.
4.15: And He was teaching in their synagogues, being glorified by all.
4.16: And He came to Natzeret, where He had been brought up; and He entered in, as was His custom on the Shabbat, to the synagogue, and stood up and read.
4.17: And the scroll of the prophet Yeshayahu was handed to Him. And He unrolled the scroll, and found the place where it was written,
4.18: " THE SPIRIT OF ADONAI IS UPON ME, BECAUSE HE ANOINTED ME TO ANNOUNCE THE GOOD NEWS TO THE POOR. HE HAS SENT ME TO PROCLAIM FORGIVENESS TO THE CAPTIVES, AND RECOVERY OF SIGHT TO THE BLIND, TO SET FREE THOSE WHO ARE OPPRESSED,
4.19: " TO PROCLAIM THE ACCEPTABLE YEAR OF ADONAI. "
4.20: And He rolled I backthe scroll, and gave it back to the attendant, and sat down; and the eyes of all in the synagogue were fixed in a gaze upon Him.
4.21: And He began to say to them, " Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your ears. "
4.22: And all were bearing testimony of Him, and were wondering at the gracious words which were going forth from His mouth; and they said, " Is this not Yosef’s son? "
4.23: And He said to them, " Doubtless you will say this proverb to Me, 'Physician, heal yourself! Whatever we heard was done at K’far - Nachum, do here in your home town also. ' "
4.24: And He said, " Truly I say to you, no prophet is accepted in his home town.
4.25: " But I say to you in truth, there were many widows in Yisrael in the days of Eliyahu, when the sky was shut up for three years and six months, when a great famine came upon all the land;
4.26: " and Eliyahu was sent to none of them, but only to Tzarfat I in the landof Tzidon, to a woman who was a widow.
4.27: " And there were many lepers in Yisrael in I the timeof Elisha the prophet; and none of them was cleansed, but only Na’aman the Syrian. "
4.28: And all in the synagogue were filled with anger as they heard these things;
4.29: and they rose up and cast Him out of the city, and led Him to the brow of the hill on which their city was built, in order to cast Him over the precipice.
4.30: But passing through the middle of them, He went away.
4.31: And He went down to K’far - Nachum, a city of Galil. And He was teaching them on the Shabbat;
4.32: and they were astonished at His teaching, for His word was with authority.
4.33: And in the synagogue was a man possessed by the spirit of an unclean demon, and he cried out with a great voice,
4.34: " Ha! What have You to do with us, Yeshua of Natzeret? Have You come to ruin us? I know Who You are - - the Holy One of God! "
4.35: But Yeshua rebuked him, saying, " Be silenced and come out of him! " And when the demon had thrown him down in the middle I of them, he came out of him, not harming him.
4.36: And amazement came upon them all, and they were speaking with one another, saying, " What is this word? For with authority and power He commands the unclean spirits, and they come out. "
4.37: And the report about Him was going forth into every place in the surrounding district.
4.38: And He arose out of the synagogue and entered Shimon’s house. Now Shimon’s mother - in - law was pressed with a great fever, and they asked Him about her,
4.39: And He stood over her and rebuked the fever, and it left her; and immediately she arose and served them.
4.40: Now while the sun was setting, all those who had any that were sick with various diseases brought them to Him; and laying His hands on each one of them, He healed them.
4.41: And demons also were coming out of many, crying out and saying, " You are the Son of God! " But He rebuked them, and would not allow them to speak, because they knew that He was the Messiah.
4.42: And when day came, He departed and went to a solitary place; and the crowds were searching for Him, and came to Him, and tried to keep Him from going away from them.
4.43: But He said to them, " I must proclaim the Kingdom of God to the other cities also, for I was sent for this I mission. "
4.44: And He kept on proclaiming in the synagogues of Yehudah.

5.1: Now it came about that while the crowd was pressing on Him to hear the word of God, He was standing by the lake of Ginosar;
5.2: and He saw two boats standing beside the lake; but the fisherman had disembarked from them, and were washing their nets.
5.3: Stepping onto one of the boats, which was Shimon’s, He asked him to put out to sea a little from the land. And He sat down and was teaching the crowds from the boat.
5.4: And when He had ceased speaking, He said to Shimon, " Put out I to seainto the deep I waterand lower your nets for a catch. "
5.5: And Shimon answered and said, " Commander, we toiled all night and took nothing! But at Your spoken word I will lower the nets. "
5.6: And when they had done this, they netted a large number of fish; and their nets were breaking;
5.7: and they signaled to their companions in the other boat to come and help them. And they came, and filled both of the boats, so that they began to sink.
5.8: But when Shimon Petros saw I it, he prostrated at Yeshua’s knees, saying, " Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, O Lord! "
5.9: For amazement had surrounded him and all those with him, at the catch of fish which they had collected;
5.10: and so also Ya’akov and Yochanan, sons of Zavdai, who were partakers with Shimon. And Yeshua said to Shimon, " Do not fear, from now on you will be catching men alive. "
5.11: And when they had brought their boats to land, they left everything and followed Him.
5.12: And it happened that while He was in one of the cities, behold, I there wasa man full of leprosy; and when he saw Yeshua he fell on his face and begged him, saying, " Lord, if You are willing, You can cleanse me. "
5.13: And He stretched out His hand and touched him, saying, " I am willing, be cleansed. " And immediately the leprosy left him.
5.14: And He ordered him to tell no one, " But go and show yourself to the priest and offer for your cleansing, just as Moshe commanded, as a testimony to them. "
5.15: But the word about Him was spreading all the more, and many crowds were gathering to hear and to be healed of their infirmities.
5.16: But He was withdrawing to the wilderness and was praying.
5.17: And it came about one day that He was teaching; and there were Pharisees and teachers of the Torah sitting, who had come from every village of Galil and Yehudah and I fromYerushalayim; and the power of the Lord was with Him to heal.
5.18: And behold, men I werecarrying on a bed a man who was paralyzed; and they were trying to bring him in, and to lay him before Him.
5.19: But not finding any I wayto bring him in because of the crowd, they went up on the roof and let him down through the tiles with his stretcher, into the middle I of them, before Yeshua.
5.20: And seeing their faith, He said, " Man, your sins are forgiven. "
5.21: And the scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying, " Who is this that speaks blasphemies? Who has the power to forgive sins, but God alone? "
5.22: But Yeshua, aware of their reasonings, answered and said to them, " Why are you reasoning in your hearts?
5.23: " Which is easier, to say, 'Your sins are forgiven, ' or to say 'Rise and walk'?
5.24: " But in order that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on Earth to forgive sins, " - - He said to the one who was paralyzed - - " I say to you, rise, take up your stretcher, and go home. "
5.25: And immediately he arose before them, and took up what he had been lying on, and went away to his house, glorifying God.
5.26: And astonishment took them all, and they were glorifying God and were filled with fear, saying, " We have seen remarkable things today. "
5.27: And after this He went out, and looked upon a tax - collector named Levee, sitting at the tax - office; and He said to him, " Follow Me. "
5.28: And he left everything behind, and rose and followed Him.
5.29: And Levee made a great reception for Him in his house; and there was a great crowd of tax - collectors and others who were reclining with them.
5.30: And the Pharisees and their scribes were murmuring at His disciples, saying, " Why do you eat and drink with tax - collectors and sinners? "
5.31: And Yeshua answered and said to them, " Those who are healthy have no need of a physician, but those who are sick.
5.32: " I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance. "
5.33: And they said to Him, " The disciples of Yochanan fast often and offer prayers, those of the Pharisees also do the same; but Yours eat and drink. "
5.34: And Yeshua said to them, " Do you have the power to make the attendants of the bridegroom fast while the bridegroom is with them?
5.35: " But days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them; then they will fast in those days. "
5.36: And He also spoke a parable to them, " No one tears a piece from a fresh garment and puts it on an old garment; otherwise he will both tear the fresh, and the piece from the fresh will not match the old.
5.37: " And no one puts new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the new wine will burst the wineskins, and it will be spilled out, and the skins will be ruined.
5.38: " But new wine must be put into fresh wineskins.
5.39: " And no one after drinking old I winewishes for new; for he says, ‘The old is better. ' "

6.4: " how he entered the House of God, and took and ate the consecrated bread, which is not permitted for any to eat except the priests alone, and gave it to those with him? "
6.5: And He said to them, " The Son of Man is Lord of the Shabbat. "
6.6: And it came about on another Shabbat, that He entered into the synagogue and was teaching; and a man was there whose right hand was withered.
6.7: And the scribes and the Pharisees were observing Him scrupulously, I ifHe would heal on the Shabbat, in order that they might find I reasonto accuse Him.
6.8: But He knew their thoughts and said to the man who had the withered hand, " Arise and stand up in the middle! " And he arose and stood.
6.9: Then Yeshua said to him, " I ask you, is it permitted on the Shabbat to do good or to do evil, to save a life or to utterly ruin it? "
6.10: And having looked around at them all, He said to them, " Stretch out your hand. " And he did I so; and his hand was restored.
6.11: But they were filled with madness, and discussed toward what they might do to Yeshua.
6.12: And it was in these days that He went out to the mountain to pray; and He passed the night in prayer to God.
6.13: And when it became day, He called His disciples to Him; and chose twelve of them, whom He also named apostles:
6.14: Shimon, whom he also named Petros, and Andreas his brother, and Ya’akov and Yochanan, and Philippos and Bar - Tolmai;
6.15: and Mattityahu and Toma, Ya’akov I the sonof Chalfai, and Shimon who was called the Zealot;
6.16: Yehudah I the sonof Ya’akov, and Yehuda I fromK’riot, who became a traitor.
6.17: And He went down with them and stood on a level place. And I there wasa large crowd of His disciples, and a large number of people from all Yehudah and Yerushalayim and the coastal region of Tzor and Tzidon, who had come to hear Him and to be healed of their diseases,
6.18: and those who were troubled with unclean spirits were being cured.
6.19: And all the crowd was seeking to touch Him, for power was coming out of Him, and healing all.
6.20: And lifting up His eyes on His disciples, He said, " Blessed I areyou I who arepoor, for yours is the Kingdom of God.
6.21: " Blessed I areyou who hunger now, for you shall be satisfied. Blessed I areyou who weep now, for you shall laugh.
6.22: " Blessed are you when men hate you, and when they exclude you, and reproach you, and expel your name as evil, for the sake of the Son of Man.
6.23: " Rejoice in that day and leap, for behold, your reward is great in Heaven; for according to these things their fathers used to do to the prophets.
6.24: " But woe to you who are wealthy, for you have your comfort in full.
6.25: " Woe to you who are well - fed now, for you shall hunger. Woe I to youwho laugh now, for you shall mourn and weep.
6.26: " Woe I to youwhen all men speak well of you, for according to these things their fathers used to do to the false prophets.
6.27: " But I say to you who hear, love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,
6.28: " bless those who curse you, pray for those who revile you.
6.29: " To him who strikes you on the cheek, offer him the other also; and whoever takes away your coat, do not hinder even your shirt.
6.30: " Give to everyone who requests of you, and whoever takes away your I goods, do not ask it back.
6.31: " And just as you want people to do to you, do to them in the same manner.
6.32: " And if you love those who love you, what grace is I thatto you? For even sinners love those who love them.
6.33: " And if you do good to those who do good to you, what grace is I thatto you? For even sinners do the same.
6.34: " And if you lend from those from whom you expect to receive, what grace is I thatto you? Even sinners lend to sinners, in order to receive back I as duethe equal I amount.
6.35: " But love your enemies, and do good and lend, expecting nothing in return; and your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High, for He is kind to ungrateful and evil I men.
6.36: " Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.
6.37: " And judge not, and you will not be judged; and condemn not, and you will not be condemned; forgive, and you will be forgiven.
6.38: " Give, and it will be given to you; good measure, pressed down, shaken together, overflowing, they will be given into your lap. For by your standard of measure, it will be measured to you in return. "
6.39: And He also spoke a parable to them, " Can a blind man lead a blind man? Will they not both fall into a pit?
6.40: " A disciple is not above his teacher; but everyone, after he has been prepared, will be like his teacher.
6.41: " Why do you look at the twig that is in your brother’s eye, but do not pay attention to the log that is in your own eye?
6.42: " Or how can you say to your brother, 'Brother, allow me to cast out the twig that is in your own eye, ’ when you yourself do not see the log that is in your own eye? You hypocrite, first cast out the log that is in your own eye, and then you will see clearly to cast out the twig that is in your brother’s eye.
6.43: " For there is no good tree that bears rotten fruit; nor, again, a rotten tree which bears good fruit.
6.44: " For each tree is known by its own fruit. For men do not gather figs from thorns, nor are grapes picked from a briar bush.
6.45: " The good man out of the good treasure of his heart brings forth good; and the evil I manout of the evil I treasurebrings forth what is evil; for out of the overflow of his heart his mouth speaks.
6.46: " Why do you call Me 'Lord, Lord, ' and not do what I tell you?
6.47: " Everyone who comes to Me, and hears My words and does them, I will show you whom he is like:
6.48: " he is like a man building a house, who dug deep and laid a foundation upon the rock; and when a flood came, the river broke against that house and could not shake it, because it had been well built.
6.49: " But the one who has heard and does not do them is like a man who built his house upon the ground without a foundation; and the river broke against it and immediately it collapsed, and the fracture of that house was great. "

7.1: When He had fulfilled all His spoken words in the hearing of the people, He entered K’far - Nachum.
7.2: And a certain centurion’s slave, who was highly valued by him, was sick and about to die.
7.3: When he heard about Yeshua, he sent to Him elders of the Yehudim asking Him to come and bring through safely his slave.
7.4: And when they came to Yeshua, they diligently entreated Him, saying, " He is worthy to have You furnish this for him;
7.5: " for he loves our nation, and he built us our synagogue. "
7.6: Now Yeshua went with them, and when He was already not far from the house, the centurion sent friends, saying to Him, " Lord, do not trouble yourself, for I am not sufficient for You to come under my roof;
7.7: " therefore I did not consider myself worthy to come to You. But say the word, and my servant will be healed.
7.8: " For I, also, am a man under authority, with soldiers under me, and I say to this one, 'Go! ' and he goes; and to another, 'Come! ' and he comes; and to my slave, 'Do this! ' and he does it. "
7.9: Now when Yeshua heard this, He marveled at him, and turned and said to the crowd that was following Him, " I say to you, not even in Yisrael have I found such great faith. "
7.10: And when those who had been sent turned back to the house, they found the slave healthy.
7.11: And it came about next when He went to a city called Na’im; and His disciples were journeying along with them, accompanied by a large crowd.
7.12: Now as He was nearing the gate of the city, behold, a man who had died was being carried out I for burial, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow; and a considerable crowd from the city was with her.
7.13: And when the Lord saw her, He was moved with compassion for her, and said to her, " Do not weep. "
7.14: And He approached and touched the coffin; and those bearing I itstood still. And He said, " Young man, I say to you, arise! "
7.15: And the dead man sat up, and began to speak. And I Hegave him to his mother.
7.16: And fear took them all, and they were glorifying God, saying, " A great prophet has arisen among us! " and, " God has visited His people! "
7.17: And this word about Him went out all over Yehudah, and in all the surrounding region.
7.18: And the disciples of Yochanan reported to him about all these things.
7.19: And Yochanan, calling to him two of his disciples, sent them to the Lord, saying, " Are You He Who is to come, or do we look for another? "
7.20: And when the men had come to Him, they said, " Yochanan the Immerser has sent us to You, saying, 'Are You the One Who is to come, or do we look for another? ' "
7.21: In that hour He cured many of diseases and afflictions and evil spirits; and to many blind He granted sight.
7.22: And He answered and said to them, " Go and report to Yochanan what you have seen and heard: I theBLIND RECOVER SIGHT, I thelame walk, I thelepers are cleansed, and I thedeaf hear, I thedead are raised up, I thePOOR HAVE THE GOOD NEWS PROCLAIMED to them.
7.23: " And blessed is he who shall not be offended in Me. "
7.24: And when the messengers of Yochanan had gone away, He began to speak to the crowds about Yochanan, " What did you go out into the wilderness to look upon? A reed shaken by the wind?
7.25: " But what did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft clothing? Behold, those who are splendidly clothed and live in luxury are in royal palaces.
7.26: " But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and one who is more than a prophet.
7.27: " This is the one concerning whom it is written, 'BEHOLD, I SENT MY MESSENGER BEFORE YOUR FACE, WHO SHALL PREPARE YOUR WAY BEFORE YOU. '
7.28: " I tell you, among those born of women, there is none greater than Yochanan; yet he who is least in the Kingdom of God is greater than he. "
7.29: And when all the people and the tax - collectors heard, they declared God righteous, having been immersed with the immersion of Yochanan.
7.30: But the Pharisees and those learned in Torah rejected God’s counsel for themselves, not having been immersed by him.
7.31: " To what then shall I compare the men of this generation, and what are they like?
7.32: " They are like children sitting in the market place and calling out to one another; and they say, 'We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we lamented, and you did not weep. '
7.33: " For Yochanan the Immerser came eating no bread and drinking no wine; and you say, 'He has a demon! '
7.34: " The Son of Man came eating and drinking; and you say, 'Behold, a gluttonous man and a drunkard, a friend of tax - collectors and sinners! '
7.35: " But wisdom is justified by all her children. "
7.36: Now one of the Pharisees was asking Him to eat with him. And He entered into the Pharisee’s house, and reclined.
7.37: And behold, a woman of the city, who was a sinner, when she knew that He was reclining in the Pharisee’s house, she brought an alabaster box of perfume,
7.38: and standing behind I Himat His feet, weeping, she began to wet His feet with her tears, and wiped them with the hair of her head, and was kissing His feet and anointing them with the perfume.
7.39: Now when the Pharisee who had invited Him saw this, he said to himself, " If this Man were a prophet, He would know who and what kind of person this woman is who is touching Him, that she is a sinner. "
7.40: And Yeshua answering, said to him, " Shimon, I have something to tell you. " And he replied, " Say it, Teacher. "
7.41: " A certain creditor had two debtors: one owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.
7.42: " When they could not repay, he graciously forgave them both. Which of them therefore will love him more? "
7.43: Shimon answered and said, " I suppose the one whom he forgave more. " And He said to him, " You have judged correctly. "
7.44: And turning toward the woman, He said to Shimon, " Do you see this woman? I entered into your house; you gave Me no water for My feet, but she has wet My feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.
7.45: " You gave Me no kiss; but from the time I entered she has not ceased to kiss My feet.
7.46: " You did not anoint My head with oil, but she anointed My feet with perfume.
7.47: " Therefore I say to you, her sins, which are many, have been forgiven, for she loved much; but he who is forgiven little, loves little. "
7.48: And He said to her, " Your sins have been forgiven. "
7.49: And those who were reclining with Him began to say among themselves, " Who is this, Who even forgives sins? "
7.50: And He said to the woman, " Your faith has saved you; go in peace. "

8.1: And it came about soon afterwards, that He was traveling through from one city and village to another, proclaiming and announcing good news about the Kingdom of God; and the twelve were with Him,
8.2: and certain women who had been healed of evil spirits and sicknesses: Miriam who was called " fromMagdala, " from whom seven demons had come out,
8.3: and Yochanah the wife of Kuza, Herodes’ administrator, and Shoshanah, and many others who were ministering out of their means.
8.4: And when a great crowd came together, and those from the various cities were traveling to Him, He spoke by way of a parable:
8.5: " The sower went out to sow his spores, and as he sowed, some fell beside the road; and it was trodden under foot, and the birds of the air devoured it.
8.6: " And other I sporesfell on rocky I ground, and as soon as it sprang up, it wasted away, because it had no moisture.
8.7: " And another fell among the thorns, and the thorns grew up together with it and choked it.
8.8: " And another fell into the good soil, and grew up and yielded a fruit a hundredfold. " As He said this, He was calling out, " He who has ears to hear, let him hear. "
8.9: And His disciples were questioning Him as to what this parable might be.
8.10: And He said, " To you has been granted to know the mysteries of the Kingdom of God, but to the rest I it isin parables, so that SEEING THEY MAY NOT SEE, AND HEARING THEY MAY NOT UNDERSTAND.
8.11: " Now the parable is this: the spore is the Word of God.
8.12: " And those beside the road are those who have heard; then the Devil comes and takes away the word from their heart, that they may not believe and be saved.
8.13: " And those on the rocky I ground arethose who, when they hear, receive the word with joy; but these have no root, they believe for a season, and in a season of temptation fall away.
8.14: " And the I sporeswhich fell among the thorns, these are the ones who have heard, and as they go forth they are choked with anxieties and riches and pleasures of I thislife, and bring no fruit to perfection.
8.15: " And the I sporesin the good soil, these are the ones who have heard the word in a beautiful and good heart, and hold it fast, and bear fruit with patient endurance.
8.16: " Now no one after lighting a lamp covers it with a vessel, or puts it under a bed; but he puts it on a lampstand, so that those who enter may see its light.
8.17: " For nothing is hidden that shall not be made visible, nor I anythingsecret that shall not be known and made visible.
8.18: " Therefore, take heed how you listen; for whoever has, to him shall I morebe given; and whoever does not have, even what he thinks he has shall be taken away from him. "
8.19: Then His mother and brothers came to Him, but they could not reach Him because of the crowd.
8.20: And it was reported to Him, " Your mother and Your brothers are standing outside, wishing to see You. "
8.21: But He answered and said to them, " My mother and My brothers are those who hear the Word of God and do it. "
8.22: Now it came about on one of I thosedays, that He and His disciples got into a boat, and He said to them, " Let us go across to the other side of the lake. " And so they set out,
8.23: but as they were sailing He fell asleep; and a fierce gale of wind descended upon the lake, and they were being swamped and were in danger.
8.24: And they approached Him and woke Him, saying, " Commander, Commander, we are perishing! " And being aroused He rebuked the wind and the raging waves; and they ceased and there was a calm.
8.25: And He said to them, " Where is your faith? " And they were fearful and amazed, saying to one another, " Who then is this, that He commands even the winds and the water, and they obey Him? "
8.26: And they sailed to the country of the Gerasenes, which is opposite Galil.
8.27: And when He had come out onto the land, He was met by a certain man from the city who was possessed by demons; for a long time he had worn no clothes, and was not living in a house, but in the tombs.
8.28: When he saw Yeshua, he cried out and bowed down before Him, and said in a great voice, " What have You to do with me, Yeshua, Son of the Most High God? I beg You, do not torment me. "
8.29: For He had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. For it had seized him many times; and he was bound with chains and shackles and kept under guard; but he would tear his bonds and be driven by the demon into the desert.
8.30: Yeshua then asked him, " What is your name? " And he said, " Legion "; for many demons had entered into him.
8.31: And they begged Him not to command them to go away into the abyss.
8.32: Now there was a herd of many pigs feeding there on the mountain; and I theybegged Him to allow them to enter these. And He allowed them.
8.33: Then the demons came out of the man and entered into the pigs; and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and were drowned.
8.34: When the herdsmen saw what had happened, they ran away and reported it in the city and in the country.
8.35: Then I peoplewent out to see what had happened; and they came to Yeshua and found the man from whom the demons had come out, sitting at the feet of Yeshua, clothed and in his sound mind; and they were afraid.
8.36: And those who had seen it reported to them how the man who was demon - possessed was saved.
8.37: And all the people of the surrounding country of the Gerasenes and the surrounding district asked Him to depart from them; for they were seized with great fear; and He got onto a boat, and turned back.
8.38: But the man from whom the demons had come out was begging Him that he might accompany them; but He sent him away, saying,
8.39: " Turn back to your house and describe how much God has done for you. " And he went away, proclaiming throughout the whole city how much Yeshua had done for him.
8.40: As Yeshua turned back, the crowd welcomed Him, for they had all been expecting Him.
8.41: And behold, there came a man named Yair, and he was a leader of the synagogue; and he fell at Yeshua’s feet, and besought Him to come to his house;
8.42: for he had an only daughter, about twelve years old, and she was dying. But as He went, the crowds were pressing against Him.
8.43: And a woman who had a hemorrhage for twelve years, and could not be healed by anyone,
8.44: came up behind him, and touched the tzit - tzit of His garment; and immediately her flow of blood stood.
8.45: And Yeshua said, " Who was it that touched Me? " And while they were all denying it, Petros said, " Commander, the crowds surround You and press upon You! "
8.46: But Yeshua said, " Someone did touch Me, for I know that power has gone forth from Me. "
8.47: And when the woman saw that she had not escaped notice, she came trembling and prostrated before Him, and declared in the sight of all the people the reason why she had touched Him, and how she had been immediately healed.
8.48: And He said to her, " Daughter, your faith has saved you; go in peace. "
8.49: While He was still speaking, someone came from I the house ofthe synagogue leader, saying, " Your daughter has died; do not trouble the Teacher any more. "
8.50: But when Yeshua heard, He answered him, " Do not be afraid; only believe, and she shall be saved. "
8.51: And when He came to the house, He did not allow anyone to enter in with Him, except Petros and Yochanan and Ya’akov, and the father and mother of the child.
8.52: Now they were all weeping and wailing for her; but He said, " Stop weeping, for she has not died, but is sleeping. "
8.53: And they were deriding Him, knowing that she had died.
8.54: But taking her by the hand, He called, saying, " Child, arise! "
8.55: And her spirit returned, and she arose instantly; and He gave orders that I somethingshould be given to her to eat.
8.56: And her parents were amazed; but He charged them to tell no one what had happened.

9.1: And He called the twelve together, and gave them power and authority over all the demons, and to cure diseases.
9.2: And He sent them out to proclaim the Kingdom of God and to heal.
9.3: And He said to them, " Take nothing for I yourjourney, neither a staff, nor a bag, nor bread, nor silver; neither have two tunics each.
9.4: " And whatever house you enter, stay there, and from there come out.
9.5: " And as for those who do not receive you, when you go out from that city, shake off the dust from your feet as a testimony against them. "
9.6: And they departed and were going through the villages, proclaiming the good news, and healing everywhere.
9.7: Now Herodes the tetrarch heard of all that was happening; and he was greatly perplexed, because it was said by some that Yochanan had been raised from the dead,
9.8: and by some that Eliyahu had appeared, and by others that one of the prophets of old had risen.
9.9: And Herodes said, " I myself had Yochanan beheaded; but Who is this about Whom I hear such things? " And he sought to see Him.
9.10: And when the apostles had turned back, they related fully to Him how much that they had done. And taking them alongside with Him, He withdrew Himself to a city called Beit - Tzaidah.
9.11: But the crowds were aware of this and followed Him; and having welcomed them, He was speaking to them about the Kingdom of God and curing those who had need of healing.
9.12: And the day began to wear away, and the twelve came and said to Him, " Send the crowd away, that they may go into the villages and surrounding country to lodge and get provisions; for here we are in a desolate place. "
9.13: But He said to them, " You give them I somethingto eat! " And they said, " We have no more than five loaves and two fish - - unless we are to go and buy food for all these people, "
9.14: for there were about five thousand men. And He said to His disciples, " Make them recline in groups of about fifty each. "
9.15: And they did so, and made them all recline.
9.16: And He took the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up to Heaven, He blessed and broke them, and was giving I themto the disciples to place before the crowd.
9.17: And they all ate and were satisfied; and the broken pieces which they had left over were taken up, twelve baskets.
9.18: And it happened that while He was praying alone the disciples were with Him, and He questioned them, saying, " Who do the crowds say that I am? "
9.19: And they answered and said, " Yochanan the Immerser, but others I sayEliyahu, and others that one of the prophets of old has risen. "
9.20: And He said to them, " But Who do you say that I am? " And Petros answered and said, " The Messiah of God. "
9.21: But He charged them and commanded I themto say this to no one,
9.22: saying, " The Son of Man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and on the third day be raised. "
9.23: And He said to all, " If anyone wishes to come after Me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily and follow Me.
9.24: " For whoever wishes to save his life shall lose it; but whoever loses his life for My sake, he shall save it.
9.25: " For what is a man profited if he gains the whole world, and loses or forfeits himself?
9.26: " For whoever is ashamed of Me and of My words, of him will the Son of Man be ashamed when He comes in His glory, and I the gloryof the Father and of the holy angels.
9.27: " But I tell you truthfully, there are certain ones standing here who shall not taste death until they see the Kingdom of God. "
9.28: And about eight days after these words, it came about that He took alongside Petros and Yochanan and Ya’akov, and ascended the mountain to pray.
9.29: And while He was praying, the sight of His face was altered, and His clothing I becamewhite I andradiant.
9.30: And behold, two men were talking with Him, who were Moshe and Eliyahu,
9.31: who appeared in glory, were speaking of His exodus, which He was to fulfill in Yerushalayim.
9.32: Now Petros and those who were with him were heavy with sleep; but when they were fully awake, they saw His glory and the two men standing with Him.
9.33: And it came about, as these were separating from Him, Petros said to Yeshua, " Commander, it is good for us to be here; and let us make three tabernacles: one for You, and one for Moshe, and one for Eliyahu " - - not knowing what he said.
9.34: And as he was saying this, a cloud formed and overshadowed them; and they were afraid as they entered into the cloud.
9.35: And a voice came out of the cloud, saying, " This is My Son, My Chosen, listen to Him! "
9.36: And when the voice had spoken, Yeshua was found alone. And they kept silent and reported to no one in those days anything of what they had seen.
9.37: And it came about on the next day, when they had come down from the mountain, a great crowd met Him.
9.38: And behold, a man from the crowd shouted out, saying, " Teacher, I beg You to look at my son, for he is my only begotten,
9.39: " and behold, a spirit seizes him, and he suddenly cries out; and it throws him into a convulsion, foaming I at the mouth, and as it shatters him, it scarcely leaves him.
9.40: " And I begged Your disciples to cast it out, but they could not. "
9.41: And Yeshua answered and said, " O faithless and perverted generation, how long shall I be with you and bear with you? Bring your son here. "
9.42: And while he was yet drawing near, the demon dashed I him to the ground, and threw him into a convulsion. But Yeshua rebuked the unclean spirit, and healed the boy, and gave him back to his father.
9.43: And they were all astonished at the magnificence of God. But while they were all marveling at everything He did, He said to His disciples,
9.44: " Let these words sink into your ears; for the Son of Man is about to be delivered up into the hands of men. "
9.45: But they did not understand this spoken word, and it was concealed from them, so that they might not perceive it; and they were afraid to ask Him about this spoken word.
9.46: And an argument arose among them as to which one of them was the greatest.
9.47: But Yeshua, perceiving the reasoning of their hearts, took a child and stood him by His side,
9.48: and said to them, " Whoever receives this child in My name receives Me; and whoever receives Me receives Him Who sent Me; for he who is least among you, this is the one who is great. "
9.49: And Yochanan answered and said, " Commander, we saw someone casting out demons in Your name; and we tried to hinder him because he does not follow with us. "
9.50: But Yeshua said to him, " Do not hinder I him; for he who is not against you is for you. "
9.51: And it came about, when the days were approaching for His ascension, that He fixed His face to go to Yerushalayim;
9.52: and He sent messengers on ahead of Him. And they went, and entered a village of the Shomronim, to make preparations for Him.
9.53: And they did not receive Him, because He was going with His face toward Yerushalayim.
9.54: And when His disciples Ya’akov and Yochanan saw I this, they said, " Lord, do you want us to bid fire to come down from Heaven and consume them? "
9.55: But He turned and rebuked them, I and said, " You do not know what kind of spirit you are of;
9.56: " for the Son of Man did not come to utterly ruin men’s lives, but to save them. " And they went on to another village.
9.57: And as they were going along the road, someone said to Him, " I will follow You wherever You go. "
9.58: And Yeshua said to him, " The foxes have holes, and the birds of the air nests; but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay His head. "
9.59: And He said to another, " Follow Me. " But he said, " Allow me first to go and bury my father. "
9.60: But He said to him, " Leave the dead to bury their own dead; but as for you, go and publish abroad the Kingdom of God. "
9.61: And another also said, " I will follow You, Lord; but first allow me to take leave of those in my house. "
9.62: But Yeshua said to him, " No one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back is useful for the Kingdom of God. "

10.1: Now after this the Lord appointed seventy others, and sent them on before Him, two by two, to every city and place where He Himself was going to come.
10.2: And He said to them, " The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few; therefore beseech the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into His harvest.
10.3: " Go your way; behold, I send you out as lambs in the middle of wolves.
10.4: " Carry no purse, no bag, no sandals; and greet no one on the way.
10.5: " And whatever house you enter, first say, 'Peace to this house! '
10.6: " And if a son of peace is there, your peace will rest upon him; but if not, it shall be turned back to you.
10.7: " And stay in that house, eating and drinking what they I placebeside you; for the laborer is worthy of his wages. Do not move from house to house.
10.8: " And whatever city you enter into and they receive you, eat what is set before you;
10.9: " and heal the sick in it and say to them, 'The Kingdom of God has come near to you. '
10.10: " But whatever city you enter into and they do not receive you, go out into its streets and say,
10.11: " 'Even the dust of your city that clings to our feet, we wipe off against you; nevertheless, know this, that the Kingdom of God has come near. '
10.12: " I say to you, it shall be more tolerable on that day for S’dom than for that town.
10.13: " Woe to you, Korazin! Woe to you, Beit - Tzaidah! For if the miracles had been performed in Tzor and Tzidon which occurred in you, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
10.14: " But it shall be more tolerable in the judgment for Tzor and Tzidon than for you.
10.15: " And you, K’far - Nachum, will you be exalted to Heaven? You will be brought down to Sheol!
10.16: " He who hears you hears Me, and he who rejects you rejects Me; and he who rejects Me rejects the One Who sent Me. "
10.17: And the seventy turned back with joy, saying, " Lord, even the demons are subject to us in Your name! "
10.18: And He said to them, " I was beholding HaSatan fall from Heaven like lightning.
10.19: " Behold, I have given you authority to tread upon serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy; and nothing shall act wickedly against you.
10.20: " Nevertheless do not rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you; but rejoice that your names are inscribed in Heaven. "
10.21: In that same hour He rejoiced greatly in the Holy Spirit and said, " I praise You, O Father, Lord of Heaven and Earth, that You have hidden these things from I thewise and intelligent and revealed them to babes. Yes, Father, for thus it was well - pleasing before You.
10.22: " All things have been delivered to Me by My Father; and no one knows Who the Son is except the Father, and Who the Father is except the Son, and anyone to whom the Son wills to reveal I Him. "
10.23: And turning to the disciples, He said privately, " Blessed I arethe eyes which see what you see,
10.24: " for I tell you that many prophets and kings wished to see the things that you see, and did not see I them, and to hear the things that you hear, and did not hear I them. "
10.25: And behold, a certain I personlearned in the Torah stood up and put Him to the test, saying, " Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life? "
10.26: And He said to him, " What is written in the Torah? How do you read? "
10.27: And he answered and said, " YOU SHALL LOVE ADONAI YOUR GOD WITH ALL YOUR HEART, AND WITH ALL YOUR SOUL, AND WITH ALL YOUR STRENGTH, AND WITH ALL YOUR MIND; AND YOUR NEIGHBOR AS YOURSELF. "
10.28: And He said to him, " You have answered correctly; do this, and you will live. "
10.29: But wishing to justify himself, he said to Yeshua, " And who is my neighbor? "
10.30: Yeshua replied and said, " A certain man was going down from Yerushalayim to Yericho, and he fell among robbers, and they stripped him and beat him, and they went away leaving him half dead.
10.31: " Now by chance a certain priest was going down that road; and when he saw him, he passed by on the opposite side.
10.32: " And likewise a Levite also, when he came to the place and saw him, passed by on the opposite side.
10.33: " But a certain Shomroni, as he journeyed, came upon him; and when he saw him, he felt compassion,
10.34: " and approached him, and bound up his wounds, pouring oil and wine on I them; and he put him on his own beast and brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
10.35: " And the next day he took out two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper, and said, 'Take care of him; and whatever more you spend, I will repay you when I come back. '
10.36: " Which of these three, do you think, proved to be a neighbor to the man who fell among the robbers? "
10.37: And he said, " The one who showed mercy toward him. " And Yeshua said to him, " Go and do likewise. "
10.38: Now as they were going along, He entered a certain village; and a woman named Marta received Him into her house.
10.39: And she had a sister called Miriam, who sat at the Lord’s feet I andwas listening to His word.
10.40: But Marta was distracted with much serving; and she came up I to Him, and said, " Lord, do You not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Then tell her to help me. "
10.41: But the Lord answered and said to her, " Marta, Marta, you are anxious and disturbed about many things;
10.42: " but I onlyone thing is needed, really I onlyone, for Miriam has chosen the good portion, which shall not be taken away from her. "

11.1: And it came to pass that while He was praying in a certain place, as He ceased, one of His disciples said to Him, " Lord, teach us to pray, just as Yochanan also taught his disciples. "
11.2: And He said to them, " When you pray, say: Father, hallowed be Your name. Your Kingdom come.
11.3: " Give us each day our daily bread;
11.4: " and forgive us our sins, for we ourselves also forgive everyone who is indebted to us. And lead us not into temptation. "
11.5: And He said to them, " Which of you shall have a friend and go to him at midnight and say to him, 'Friend, lend me three loaves I of bread;
11.6: " for a friend of mine has arrived on a journey, and I have nothing to set before him';
11.7: " and he will answer from inside I his houseand say, 'Do not bother me; the door has already been shut, and my children with me are in bed; I cannot arise and give you I anything. '
11.8: " I tell you, though he will not arise up and give him I anythingbecause he is his friend, yet because of his persistence he will arise and give him as much as he needs.
11.9: " And I say to you: ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
11.10: " For everyone who asks, receives; and he who seeks, finds; and to him who knocks, it will be opened.
11.11: " Now which father among you, if his son asks for a fish; he will not give him a snake instead of a fish, will he?
11.12: " Or I ifhe asks for an egg, he will not give him a scorpion, will he?
11.13: " If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more shall your Father Who is in Heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him? "
11.14: And He was casting out a demon, and it was dumb; and it happened that when the demon had come out, the dumb man spoke; and the crowds marveled.
11.15: But certain ones of them said, " He casts out demons by Ba’al - zibbul, the ruler of the demons. "
11.16: And others, to test I Him, were seeking of Him a sign from Heaven.
11.17: But He, knowing their thoughts, said to them, " Any kingdom divided against itself is laid waste; and a house I dividedagainst itself falls.
11.18: " And if HaSatan also is divided against himself, how shall his kingdom stand? For you say that I cast out demons by Ba’al - zibbul.
11.19: " And if I cast out demons by Ba’al - zibbul, by whom do your sons cast them out? On account of this, they shall be your judges.
11.20: " But if it is by the finger of God that I cast out demons, then the Kingdom of God has come upon you.
11.21: " When a strong I man, fully armed, guards his own homestead, his possessions are undisturbed;
11.22: " but when one stronger than he comes upon him and prevails over him, he takes away from him all his armor on which he had relied, and distributes his plunder.
11.23: " He who is not with Me is against Me; and he who does not gather with Me, scatters.
11.24: " When an unclean spirit goes out of a man, it passes through waterless places, seeking rest; and finding none, it says, 'I will turn back to my house from which I came. '
11.25: " And when it comes, it finds it swept and put in order,
11.26: " then it goes and takes alongside itself seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they enter in and live there. And the last state of that man becomes worse than the first. "
11.27: And it came about that while He said these things, a certain woman in the crowd lifted up her voice, and said to Him, " Blessed is the womb that bore You, and the breasts at which You nursed! "
11.28: But He said, " Rather, blessed are those who hear the Word of God, and guard it. "
11.29: And as the crowds were increasing, He began to say, " This generation is an evil generation; it seeks a sign, but no sign shall be given to it except the sign of Yonah.
11.30: " For just as Yonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so will the Son of Man be to this generation.
11.31: " The Queen of the South will rise up at the judgment with the men of this generation and condemn them, because she came from the ends of the Earth to hear the wisdom of Shlomo; and behold, something greater than Shlomo is here.
11.32: " The men of Nineveh will arise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at the proclamation of Yonah; and behold, something greater than Yonah is here.
11.33: " No one after lighting a lamp puts it away in a cellar, nor under a peck - measure, but on a lampstand, in order that those who enter may see the light.
11.34: " The lamp of your body is your eye; when your eye is clear, your whole body also is full of light; but when it is bad, your whole body also is full of darkness.
11.35: " Therefore take heed, lest the light in you be darkness.
11.36: " If therefore your whole body is full of light, with no dark part in it, it will be wholly bright, as when the lamp gives light to you with its rays. "
11.37: Now while He was speaking, a Pharisee asked Him to dine with him; and He went in, and reclined.
11.38: And when the Pharisee saw it, he was astonished that He had not first immersed Himself before the dinner.
11.39: But the Lord said to him, " Now you Pharisees cleanse the outside of the cup and the dish; but inside of you, you are full of robbery and wickedness.
11.40: " You fools! Did not He Who made the outside make the inside also?
