11.41: " But give that which is within as alms; and behold, all things are clean for you.
11.42: " But woe to you Pharisees! For you tithe mint and rue and every garden herb, and disregard justice and the love of God; but these are the things it is necessary to have done without neglecting the others.
11.43: " Woe to you Pharisees! For you love the first seats in the synagogues, and the greetings in the market places.
11.44: " Woe to you! For you are like unseen tombs, and the men walk over I themnot I knowing it. "
11.45: And one of those learned in Torah, answering, said to Him, " Teacher, in saying this, You insult us also. "
11.46: But He said, " Woe to you learned in Torah also! For you load down men with burdens hard to bear, while you yourselves do not touch the burdens with one of your fingers.
11.47: " Woe to you! For you build the tombs of the prophets whom your fathers killed.
11.48: " Consequently, you are witnesses and join in approving the works of your fathers; because it was they who killed them, and you build I their tombs.
11.49: " Because of this also the wisdom of God said, 'I will send to them prophets and apostles, and I someof them they will kill and persecute,
11.50: " 'so that the blood of all the prophets, shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation,
11.51: " 'from the blood of Hevel to the blood of Zekaryah, who perished between the altar and the House I of God. Yes, I tell you, it shall be required of this generation. '
11.52: " Woe to you learned in Torah! For you have taken away the key of knowledge; you did not enter in yourselves, and those who were entering in, you hindered. "
11.53: And as He came out from there, the scribes and the Pharisees began to have a grudge against Him and to question Him closely on many things,
11.54: lying in wait for Him, to catch I Himin something He might say.

12.1: In the meantime, when so many thousands of the crowd had gathered together that they were all trampling on one another, He began to say to His disciples first, " Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
12.2: " Nothing is covered up that will not be revealed, or hidden that will not be known.
12.3: " Accordingly, whatever you have said in the dark shall be heard in the light, and what you have whispered in the inner rooms shall be proclaimed upon the housetops.
12.4: " I say to you, My friends, do not fear those who kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do.
12.5: " But I will warn you Whom to fear: fear Him Who, after He has killed has authority to cast into Gey - Hinnom; yes. I tell you, fear Him!
12.6: " Are not five sparrows sold for two assaria? And not one of them is forgotten before God.
12.7: " Indeed, even the hairs on your head are all numbered. Fear not; you are of more value than many sparrows.
12.8: " And I say to you, everyone who acknowledges Me before men, the Son of Man also shall acknowledge him before the angels of God;
12.9: " but he who denies Me before men shall be denied before the angels of God.
12.10: " And everyone who will speak a word against the Son of Man, it shall be forgiven him; but he who blasphemes against the Holy Spirit, it shall not be forgiven him.
12.11: " And when they bring you before the synagogues and the rulers and the authorities, do not be anxious how or what you are to say in your defense, or what you should say;
12.12: " for the Holy Spirit will teach you in that very hour what you ought to say. "
12.13: And a certain I personin the crowd said to Him, " Teacher, tell my brother to divide the I familyinheritance with me. "
12.14: But He said to him, " Man, who appointed Me a judge or arbiter over you? "
12.15: And He said to them, " Take heed, and be on your guard against every form of covetousness; for not I evenwhen one has an abundance does his life consist of his possessions. "
12.16: And He told them a parable, saying, " The land of a certain rich man brought forth I fruitwell.
12.17: " And he was reasoning within himself, saying, 'What shall I do, since I have nowhere to gather together my fruits? '
12.18: " And he said, 'This is what I will do: I will tear down my barns and build larger ones, and there I will gather together all my grain and my goods.
12.19: " 'And I will say to my soul, " Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years; take your rest, eat, drink, be merry. " '
12.20: " But God said to him, 'You fool! This night your soul is required of you; and the things you have prepared, whose will they be? '
12.21: " So is he who stores up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God. "
12.22: And He said to His disciples, " Thus I say to you, do not be anxious for your life, what you shall eat; not for your body, what you shall put on.
12.23: " For life is more than nourishment, and the body more than clothing.
12.24: " Consider the ravens, they neither sow nor reap; they have neither storehouse nor barn, and I yetGod feeds them. How much more valuable are you than the birds!
12.25: " And which of you by being anxious can add a cubit to his stature?
12.26: " If then you do not have the power to do a very little thing, why are you anxious about the rest?
12.27: " Consider the lilies, how they grow; they neither toil nor spin. But I tell you, even Shlomo in all his glory did not array himself like one of these.
12.28: " But if God so clothes the grass in the field, which is I alivetoday and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, how much more I will He clothe you, O you of little faith?
12.29: " And do not seek what you shall eat or what you shall drink, and do not be in suspense.
12.30: " For all these things the nations of the world inquire after; but your Father knows that you have need of these things.
12.31: " But, seek for His Kingdom, and these things shall be added to you.
12.32: " Fear not, little flock, because your Father has thought well of you to give you the Kingdom.
12.33: " Sell your possessions, and give alms; make yourselves purses which do not become old, an unfailing treasure in Heaven, where no thief comes near, nor moth decays.
12.34: " For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
12.35: " Let your loins be girded and your lamps burning.
12.36: " And be like men who are waiting for their lord when he returns from the wedding feast, so that they may immediately open I the doorto him when he comes and knocks.
12.37: " Blessed are those slaves whom the lord shall find awake when he comes; truly I say to you, he will gird himself and have them recline, and will come to and serve them.
12.38: " And if he comes in the second watch, or even in the third, and finds I themso, blessed are those I slaves!
12.39: " But know this, that if the housemaster had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would not have allowed his house to be broken into.
12.40: " You also must be ready; for the Son of Man is coming at an hour that you do not expect. "
12.41: And Petros said, " Lord, are you telling this parable to us, or to all also? "
12.42: And the Lord said, " Who then is the faithful and sensible administrator whom his lord will put in charge of his therapists, to give them their rations at the right time?
12.43: " Blessed is the slave whom his lord finds so doing when he comes.
12.44: " Truly I say to you, that he will put him in charge of all of his possessions.
12.45: " But if that slave says in his heart, 'My lord is delayed in coming, ' and begins to beat the menservants and the maidservants, and to eat and drink and get drunk;
12.46: " the lord of that slave will come on a day when he does not expect, and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him in pieces; and assign him a portion with the unbelievers.
12.47: " And that slave who knew his lord’s will and did not prepare or act toward his will, shall receive many lashes,
12.48: " but he who did not know, and did things worthy of a flogging, will receive a light beating. And from everyone who has been given much shall much be required; and to whom they committed much, of him they will ask all the more.
12.49: " I came to cast fire upon the Earth; and how I wish it were already kindled!
12.50: " But I have an immersion to be immersed with, and how distressed I am until it is completed!
12.51: " Do you think that I have come to give peace on Earth? I tell you, no, but rather division;
12.52: " for from now on five in one house will be divided; three against two, and two against three.
12.53: " They will be divided, father against son, and son against father, mother against daughter, and daughter against mother, mother - in - law against daughter - in - law, and daughter - in - law against mother - in - law. "
12.54: He also said to the crowds, " When you see a cloud rising in the west, immediately you say, 'A shower is coming, ' and so it happens.
12.55: " And when I you seea south wind blowing, you say, 'There will be scorching heat, ' and it happens.
12.56: " You hypocrites! You know how to examine the appearance of the Earth and the sky, but why do you not examine this season?
12.57: " And why do you not judge for yourselves what is right?
12.58: " For while you were leading your adversary before the magistrate, on the way make an effort to settle with him, lest he drag you before the judge, and the judge turn you over to the constable, and the constable throw you into prison.
12.59: " I say to you, you shall not get out of there until you have paid the very last mite. "

13.1: Now at that same season there were some present who reported to Him about the Galileans, whose blood Pilatos had mingled with their sacrifices.
13.2: And He answered and said to them, " Do you suppose that these Galileans were I worsesinners than all I otherGalileans, because they suffered this?
13.3: " I tell you, no; but unless you repent, you will all likewise perish.
13.4: " Or those eighteen, on whom the tower in Shiloach fell and killed them, were I worsedebtors then all the men who live in Yerushalayim?
13.5: " I tell you, no; but unless you repent, you will all likewise perish. "
13.6: And He told this parable: " A certain man had a fig tree which had been planted in his vineyard; and he came seeking fruit on it, but did not find any.
13.7: " And he said to the vinedresser, 'Behold, for three years I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree, but have not found any. Cut it down! Why should it render the ground useless? '
13.8: " And he answered and said to him, 'Let it alone, lord, for this year also until I dig around it and cast in manure;
13.9: " 'and if it indeed bears fruit, I fine; but if not, cut it down. ' "
13.10: And He was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Shabbat.
13.11: And behold, there was a woman who had a spirit of infirmity for eighteen years; she was bent over and could not straighten up at all.
13.12: And when Yeshua saw her, He called her over and said to her, " Woman you are free from your infirmity. "
13.13: And He laid His hands upon her; and immediately she was set upright again, and was glorifying God.
13.14: And the synagogue leader, indignant because Yeshua had healed on the Shabbat, said to the crowd, answering, " There are six days in which it is necessary for work to be done; therefore come during them and be healed, but not on the Shabbat day. "
13.15: But the Lord answered them and said, " You hypocrites! Does not each one of you on the Shabbat untie his ox or his donkey from the stall, and lead it away to water I it?
13.16: " And this woman, a daughter of Avraham whom HaSatan bound, behold, eighteen years, should she not have been released from this bond on the Shabbat day? "
13.17: And as He said this, all His adversaries were ashamed; and the entire crowd was rejoicing over all the glorious things that were done by Him.
13.18: Therefore He said, " What is the Kingdom of God like, and to what shall I compare it?
13.19: " It is like a mustard grain, which a man took and cast into his own garden; and it grew and became a tree; and THE BIRDS OF THE AIR NESTED IN ITS BRANCHES. "
13.20: And again He said, " To what shall I compare the Kingdom of God?
13.21: " It is like leaven which a woman took and hid in three pecks of meal, until it was all leavened. "
13.22: And as He was passing through from one city and village to another, teaching, and making progress toward Yerushalayim.
13.23: And a certain one said to Him, " Lord, are there I justa few who are being saved? " And He said to them,
13.24: " Strive to enter by the narrow door; for many, I tell you, will seek to enter and not be strong.
13.25: " From when the master of the house rises up and shuts the door, you will begin to stand outside and knock at the door, saying, 'Lord, open up to us! ' Then He will answer and say to you, 'I do not know where you are from. '
13.26: " Then you will begin to say, 'We ate and drank in Your sight, and You taught in our streets';
13.27: " but He will say, 'I tell you, I do not know where you are from; depart from me, you unrighteous! '
13.28: " There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth there when you see Avraham and Yitzchak and Ya’akov and all the prophets in the Kingdom of God, but you yourselves expelled.
13.29: " And they will be present from east and west, and from north and south, and will recline in the Kingdom of God.
13.30: " And behold, there are I thoselast who will be first, and I thosefirst who will be last. "
13.31: And at that very hour some Pharisees approached, saying to Him, " Go out and go away from here, for Herodes wants to kill You. "
13.32: And He said to them, " Go and tell that fox, 'Behold, I cast out demons and perform cures today and tomorrow, and the third I dayI reach My goal. '
13.33: " Nevertheless I must go on today and tomorrow and the I dayfollowing; for it is not possible that a prophet should perish outside of Yerushalayim.
13.34: " O Yerushalayim, Yerushalayim, killing the prophets and stoning those who are sent to you! How often I wanted to gather together your children, just as a hen I gathers togetherher brood under her wings, but you were unwilling!
13.35: " Behold, your house is left to you I desolate; and I say to you, you will not see Me until you say, 'BLESSED IS HE WHO COMES IN THE NAME OF ADONAI. ' "

14.1: And it came to pass when He went into the house of one of the leaders of the Pharisees on a Shabbat to eat bread, that they were observing Him scrupulously.
14.2: And behold, there was a certain man before Him who was suffering from dropsy.
14.3: And Yeshua answered and spoke to those learned in Torah and Pharisees, saying, " Is it permitted to heal on the Shabbat, or not? "
14.4: But they kept silent. And He took hold of him, and healed him, and released him.
14.5: And He said to them, " Which of you, having a son or an ox fall into a well, and will not immediately pull him out on a Shabbat day? "
14.6: And they were not strong enough to reply to this.
14.7: And He spoke a parable to those called when he noticed how they were selecting the places of honor; saying to them,
14.8: " When you are invited by someone to a wedding feast, do not recline at the place of honor, lest someone more valued than you may have been called by him,
14.9: " and he who called you both shall come and say to you, 'Give place to this man, ' and then in shame you proceed to occupy the last place.
14.10: " But when you are invited, go and fall back to the last place, so that when the one who has invited you comes, he may say to you, 'Friend, go up besides higher'; then you will have glory in the sight of all who are at the table with you.
14.11: " For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and he who humbles himself shall be exalted. "
14.12: And He also said to the one who had called Him, " When you give a dinner or a banquet, do not invite your friends or your brothers or your relatives or wealthy neighbors, lest they also invite you in return, and repayment come to you.
14.13: " But when you give a reception, call I thepoor, I thecrippled, I thelame, I theblind,
14.14: " and you will be blessed, because they cannot repay you; for you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous. "
14.15: And when one of those who were reclining I at the tablewith Him heard this, he said to Him, " Blessed is he who shall eat bread in the Kingdom of God! "
14.16: But He said to him, " A certain man was giving a big dinner, and he invited many;
14.17: " and he sent his slave at the dinner hour to say to those who had been invited, 'Come, for everything is prepared now. '
14.18: " But they all alike began to make excuses. The first said to him, 'I have bought a field and I need to go out and see it; please consider me excused. '
14.19: " And another said, 'I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to approve them, please consider me excused. '
14.20: " And another said, 'I have married a wife, and because of this I do not have the power to come. '
14.21: " And the slave came and reported this to his lord. Then the housemaster became angry and said to his slave, 'Go out hastily into the streets and lanes of the city and introduce in here the poor and crippled and blind and lame. '
14.22: " And the slave said, 'Lord, what you commanded has been done, and still there is a place. '
14.23: " And the lord said to the slave, 'Go out to the roads and fences, and compel I themto come in, that my house may be filled.
14.24: " 'For I say to you, none of those men who were invited shall taste of my dinner. ' "
14.25: Now great crowds were journeying along with Him; and He turned and said to them,
14.26: " If anyone comes to Me, and does not hate his own father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, yes, and even his own life, he does not have the power to be My disciple.
14.27: " Whoever does not take up his own cross and come after Me does not have the power to be My disciple.
14.28: " For which of you, when he wants to build a tower, does not first sit down and calculate the cost, whether he has enough to complete it?
14.29: " Otherwise, when he has laid a foundation, and is not strong enough to complete fully, all who behold it begin to mock him,
14.30: " saying, 'This man began to build and was not strong enough to complete fully. '
14.31: " Or what king, going to meet another king in battle, will not first sit down and take counsel whether he is powerful with ten thousand to encounter him who with twenty thousand is coming against him?
14.32: " Or otherwise, while the other is still far off, he sends a delegation and asks things for peace.
14.33: " So therefore, whoever of you who does not leave all of his possessions does not have the power to be My disciple.
14.34: " Therefore, salt is good; but if even salt has become tasteless, with what will it be made salty?
14.35: " It is useless neither for the soil nor for the manure pile; it is cast out. He who has ears to ear, let him hear. "

15.1: Now all the tax - collectors and the sinners were coming near to listen to Him.
15.2: And both the Pharisees and the scribes were murmuring I among themselves, saying, " This I Manreceives sinners to Himself and eats with them. "
15.3: And He told them this parable, saying,
15.4: " What man among you, having a hundred sheep and having lost one of them, does not leave behind the ninety - nine in the wilderness, and go after the one which is lost, until he finds it?
15.5: " And when he has found it, he lays it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
15.6: " And when he comes to I hishouse, he calls together his friends and his neighbors, saying to them, 'Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep which was lost! '
15.7: " I tell you in that same way, there will be I morejoy in Heaven over one sinner who repents, than over ninety - nine righteous persons who need no repentance.
15.8: " Or what woman, having ten drachmas, if she loses one coin, does not light a lamp and sweep the house and search carefully until she finds it?
15.9: " And when she has found it, she calls together her friends and neighbors, saying, 'Rejoice with me, for I have found the coin which I had lost! '
15.10: " In the same way, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner who repents. "
15.11: And He said, " A certain man had two sons;
15.12: " and the younger of them said to his father, 'Father, give me the portion of the estate that falls to me. ' And he divided his living between them.
15.13: " And not many days after, the younger son gathered everything together and went on a journey I abroadinto a far distant country, and there he squandered his estate, living wastefully.
15.14: " Now when he had spent everything, a mighty famine took place in that country, and he began to be in want.
15.15: " And he went and attached himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into his fields to feed pigs.
15.16: " And he was longing to fill his stomach with the pods that the pigs were eating, and no one was giving I anythingto him.
15.17: " But when he came to himself, he said, 'How many of my father’s hired servants have a superabundance of bread, but I am perishing here with hunger!
15.18: " 'I will arise and go to my father, and I will say to him, " Father, I have sinned against Heaven, and before you;
15.19: " ' " I am no longer worthy to be called your son; make me as one of your hired servants. " '
15.20: " And he arose and came to his father. But while he was yet at a distance, his father saw him and had compassion, and ran and embraced him and kissed him.
15.21: " And the son said to him, 'Father, I have sinned against Heaven and before you; I am no longer worthy to be called your son. '
15.22: " But the father said to his slaves, 'Bring quickly the best robe and put it on him, and give a ring for his hand and sandals for his feet;
15.23: " 'and bring the fattened calf, kill it, and let us eat and be merry;
15.24: " 'for this son of mine was dead, and has come to life again; he was lost, and is found. ' And they began to be merry.
15.25: " Now his elder son was in the field; and when he came and drew near to the house, he heard music and dancing.
15.26: " And he called one of the servants and was inquiring what these things might be.
15.27: " And he said to him, 'Your brother has come, and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has received him back in good health. '
15.28: " But he became angry, and was not willing to go in; and his father came out and was entreating him.
15.29: " But he answered and said to his father, 'Behold, these many years I have been serving you, and I never disregarded a commandment of yours; but you have never given me a kid, that I might be merry with my friends;
15.30: " 'but when this son of yours came, who has devoured your living with prostitutes, you killed the fattened calf for him. '
15.31: " And he said to him, 'Child, you have always been with me, and all that is mine is yours.
15.32: " 'But it is necessary to be merry and rejoice, for this brother of yours was dead, and is alive; he was lost, and is found. ' "

16.1: Now He also said to the disciples, " There was a certain rich man who had a steward, and charges were brought to him that he was squandering his possessions.
16.2: " And he called him and said to him, 'What is this I hear about you? Give I meword of your stewardship, for you can no longer be steward. '
16.3: " And the steward said to himself, 'What shall I do, because my lord is taking the stewardship away from me? I am not strong enough to dig; I am ashamed to beg.
16.4: " 'I know what I shall do, so that when I am removed from the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses. '
16.5: " And he summoned each one of his lord’s debtors, and he said to the first, 'How much do you owe my lord? '
16.6: " And he said, 'A hundred baths of oil. ' And he said to him, 'Take your bill, and sit down quickly and write fifty. '
16.7: " Then he said to another, 'And how much do you owe? ' And he said, 'A hundred kors of wheat. ' He said to him, 'Take your bill and write eighty. '
16.8: " And his lord praised the unrighteous steward because he had acted shrewdly; for the sons of this age are more shrewd in dealing with their own generation than the sons of light.
16.9: " And I say to you, make friends for yourselves by means of the mammon of unrighteousness; that when it fails, they may receive you into the eternal tabernacles.
16.10: " He who is faithful in the least, is faithful also in much; and he who in the least is unrighteous, is also unrighteous in much;
16.11: " If therefore you have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will entrust the true I richesto you?
16.12: " And if you have not been faithful in that which is another’s, who will give you that which is your own?
16.13: " No servant can serve two lords; for either he will hate the one and love the other, or else he will hold to one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon. "
16.14: Now the Pharisees, who were lovers of money, were listening to all of this, and they were scoffing at Him.
16.15: And He said to them, " You are those who justify yourselves in the sight of men, but God knows your hearts; for that which is high among men is an abomination in the sight of God.
16.16: " The Torah and the Prophets I areuntil Yochanan; since then the good news of the Kingdom of God is proclaimed, and everyone is forcing His way into it.
16.17: " But it is easier for Heaven and Earth to pass away, than for one stroke of a letter of the Torah to fall.
16.18: " Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery; and he who marries one who is divorced from her husband commits adultery.
16.19: " Now there was a certain rich man, and he dressed in purple and fine linen, making merry splendidly every day.
16.20: " And a certain poor man named El’azar was laid at his gate, covered with sores,
16.21: " and desiring to be fed with what fell from the rich man’s table; otherwise, even the dogs were coming and licking his sores.
16.22: " Now it came to pass that the poor man died and he was carried away by the angels to Avraham’s bosom; and the rich man also died and was buried.
16.23: " And in Sheol he lifted up his eyes, being in torment, and saw Avraham from afar, and El’azar in his bosom.
16.24: " And he called out and said, 'Father Avraham, have mercy upon me, and send El’azar that he may dip his finger in water and cool my tongue; for I am suffering pain in this flame. '
16.25: " But Avraham said, 'Child, remember that in your lifetime you received your good things, and El’azar likewise bad things; but now he is comforted here, and you are suffering pain.
16.26: " 'And besides all this, between us and you a great chasm is fixed, in order that those who wish to step across from here to you do not have the power, and none may cross over from there to us. '
16.27: " And he said, 'Then I beg you, father, that you send him to my father’s house,
16.28: " 'for I have five brothers, so that he may solemnly warn them, lest they also come to this place of torment. '
16.29: " But Avraham said, 'They have Moshe and the Prophets; let them hear them. '
16.30: " But he said, 'No, father Avraham! But if someone goes to them from the dead, they will repent. '
16.31: " But he said to him, 'If they do not listen to Moshe and the Prophets, neither will they be convinced if someone rises from the dead. ' "

17.1: And He said to His disciples, " It is impossible for the stumbling blocks not to come, but woe to him through whom they come!
17.2: " It would be more profitable for him if a I heavystone were hung around his neck and he were thrown down into the sea, than that he should cause one of these little ones to stumble.
17.3: " Take heed to yourselves! If your brother sins, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him.
17.4: " And if he sins against you seven times a day, and returns to you seven times, saying, 'I repent, ' forgive him. "
17.5: And the apostles said to the Lord, " Increase our faith! "
17.6: And the Lord said, " If you had faith like a mustard grain, you would say to this sycamine tree, 'Be uprooted and planted in the sea'; and it would obey you.
17.7: " But which of you, having a slave plowing or shepherding, will say to him when he has come in from the field, 'Come immediately and sit down to eat'?
17.8: " But will he not say to him, 'Prepare something for me to eat, and gird yourself and serve me, till I eat and drink; and afterward you will eat and drink'?
17.9: " He does not thank the slave because he did what he was commanded, does he?
17.10: " So you also, when you have done all that is commanded you, say, 'We are unworthy slaves; we have done I onlythat which we ought to have done. ' "
17.11: And it came about while He was going to Yerushalayim, that He was passing between Shomron and Galil.
17.12: And as He entered into a certain village, He was met by ten lepers, who stood at a distance;
17.13: and they raised their voices, saying, " Yeshua, Commander, have mercy on us! "
17.14: And when He saw them, He said to them, " Go and show yourselves to the priests. " And it came about that as they were going, they were cleansed.
17.15: Now one of them, when he saw that he had been healed, turned back, glorifying God with a great voice,
17.16: and he fell on his face at His feet, giving thanks to Him. And he was a Shomroni.
17.17: And Yeshua answered and said, " Were not ten cleansed? Where are the nine?
17.18: " Was no one found to turn back to give glory to God, except this foreigner? "
17.19: And He said to him, " Rise and go; your faith has saved you. "
17.20: Now having been asked by the Pharisees as to when the Kingdom of God was coming, He answered them and said, " The Kingdom of God is not coming with observation;
17.21: " nor will they say, 'Behold, here I it is! ' or, 'There I it is! ' For behold, the Kingdom of God is within you. "
17.22: And He said to the disciples, " The days are coming when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you will not see it.
17.23: " And they will say to you, 'Behold there! Behold here! ' Do not go away, and do not run after I them.
17.24: " For just as the lightning, when it flashes out of one part under the sky, shines to the other part of the sky, so will the Son of Man be in His day.
17.25: " But first He must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.
17.26: " And just as it happened in the days of Noach, so shall it be also in the days of the Son of Man:
17.27: " they were eating, they were drinking, they were marrying, they were being given in marriage, until the day that Noach entered into the ark, and the flood came and utterly ruined them all.
17.28: " Likewise as it was in the days of Lot: they were eating, they were drinking, they were buying, they were selling, they were planting, they were building;
17.29: " but on the day that Lot went out from S’dom, fire and brimstone rained from Heaven and utterly ruined them all.
17.30: " It will be just the same on the day that the Son of Man is revealed.
17.31: " On that day, let not the one who is on the housetop and whose goods are in the house do down to take them away; and likewise let not the one who is in the field return.
17.33: " Whoever seeks to keep his life shall lose it, and whoever loses I his lifeshall preserve it.
17.34: " I say to you, on that night there will be two in one bed; one will be taken alongside, and the other will be left alone.
17.35: " There will be two women grinding together; one will be taken alongside, and the other will be left alone.
17.36: I " Two men will be in the field; one will be taken alongside, and the other will be left alone. "
17.37: And answering they said to Him, " Where, Lord? " And He said to them, " Where the body I is, there also will the vultures be gathered together. "

18.1: Now He spoke a parable to them, to the effect that it is necessary to pray always and not to lose heart,
18.2: saying, " A certain judge was in a certain city, who neither feared God nor respected man.
18.3: " And a widow was in that city, and she was coming to him, saying, 'Vindicate me against my adversary. '
18.4: " And for a time he would not; but afterward he said to himself, 'Even if I do not fear God or respect man,
18.5: " 'yet because this widow causes me trouble, I will vindicate her, lest by continually coming she wear me down. ' "
18.6: And the Lord said, " Hear what the unrighteous judge says;
18.7: " now shall not God vindicate His elect, who call out to Him day and night, and will He delay long over them?
18.8: " I tell you that He will bring vindication for them speedily. Yet, when the Son of Man comes, will He find faith on the Earth? "
18.9: And He also spoke this parable to certain ones who trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and despised the rest:
18.10: " Two men went up into the Temple to pray, one a Pharisee, and the other a tax - collector.
18.11: " The Pharisee stood and thus prayed, 'God, I thank You that I am not like the rest of men: swindlers, unrighteous, adulterers, or even like this tax - collector.
18.12: " 'I fast twice a week; I pay a tenth of all that I get. '
18.13: " But the tax - collector, standing far off, would not even lift up his eyes to Heaven, but beat his breast, saying, 'God, make propitiation for me, the sinner! '
18.14: " I tell you, this one went down to his house justified rather than the other; for everyone who exalts himself shall be humbled, but he who humbles himself shall be exalted. "
18.15: And they brought infants to Him also, so that He might touch them; but when the disciples saw it, they rebuked them.
18.16: But Yeshua called to them, saying, " Permit the children to come to Me, and do not hinder them, for the Kingdom of God exists for such as these.
18.17: " Truly I say to you, whoever does not receive the Kingdom of God shall not enter into it. "
18.18: And a certain ruler questioned Him, saying, " Good Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life? "
18.19: And Yeshua said to him, " Why do you call Me good? No one is good except God alone.
18.20: " You know the commandments: 'DO NOT COMMIT ADULTERY. DO NOT MURDER. DO NOT STEAL. DO NOT BEAR FALSE WITNESS. HONOR YOUR FATHER AND MOTHER. ' "
18.21: And he said, " All these I have kept from I myyouth. "
18.22: And when Yeshua heard I this, He said to him, " One thing you still lack; sell all that you have and distribute it to the poor, and you shall have treasure in Heaven; and come, follow Me. "
18.23: But when he heard these things, he became very sad; for he was exceedingly rich.
18.24: And Yeshua saw him and said, " How hard it is for those who are wealthy to enter the Kingdom of God!
18.25: " For it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter the Kingdom of God. "
18.26: And those who heard it said, " Then who can be saved? "
18.27: But He said, " The things impossible with men are possible with God. "
18.28: And Petros said, " Behold, we have left our own and followed You. "
18.29: And He said to them, " Truly I say to you, there is no one who has left house or wife or brothers or parents or children, for the sake of the Kingdom of God,
18.30: " who will not receive many times as much in this season and in the age to come, eternal life. "
18.31: And He took the twelve alongside and said to them, " Behold, we are going up to Yerushalayim, and all things will be brought to the goal which have been written through the prophets about the Son of Man.
18.32: " For He will be delivered up to the nations, and will be mocked and insulted and spit upon,
18.33: " and having scourged Him, they will kill Him; and on the third day He will rise again. "
18.34: But they understood none of these things, and this spoken word was hidden from them, and they did not know the things being said.
18.35: And it came about that as He was nearing Yericho, a certain blind man was sitting beside the road, begging.
18.36: Now hearing a crowd going by, he was inquiring what this might be.
18.37: And they reported to him that Yeshua of Natzeret was passing by.
18.38: And He called out, saying, " Yeshua, Son of Daveed, have mercy on me! "
18.39: And those going before rebuked him, telling him to be quiet; but he kept crying out all the more, " Son of Daveed, have mercy on me! "
18.40: And Yeshua stood and commanded that he be brought to Him; and when he had come near, He questioned him,
18.41: " What do you want Me to do for you? " And he said, " Lord, I I wantto recover my sight. "
18.42: And Yeshua said to Him, " Recover your sight; your faith has saved you. "
18.43: And instantly he recovered his sight and was following Him, glorifying God; and when all the people saw it, they gave praise to God.

19.1: And He entered into and was passing through Yericho.
19.2: And behold, there was a man called by the name of Zakkai; and he was a chief tax - collector, and he was rich.
19.3: And he was seeking to see Who Yeshua was, and he was unable because of the crowd, for he was small in stature.
19.4: And running ahead, he went up into a sycamore tree so that he could see Him, for He was about to pass through that way.
19.5: And when Yeshua came to the place, He looked up and said to him, " Zakkai, make haste and come down; for today it is necessary that I stay at your house. "
19.6: And he made haste and came down, and received Him under his roof gladly.
19.7: And having seen I it, all murmured among themselves, saying, " He has gone to be the guest of a man who is a sinner. "
19.8: And Zakkai stood and said to the Lord, " Behold, Lord, half of my possessions I will give to the poor, and if in anything I took by false accusation, I I willrestore it fourfold. "
19.9: And Yeshua said to him, " Today salvation has come to this house, inasmuch as he also is a son of Avraham.
19.10: " For the Son of Man came to seek and save that which was lost. "
19.11: And while they were hearing these things, having added He spoke a parable, because He was near Yerushalayim, and they thought that the Kingdom of God was going to instantly appear.
19.12: He said therefore, " A certain nobleman went to a distant country to receive a kingdom for himself, and return.
19.13: " And calling ten of his slaves, he gave them ten minas, and said to them, 'Do business until I come. '
19.14: " But his citizens hated him and sent a delegation after him, saying, 'We do not want this one to reign over us. '
19.15: " And it happened as he returned, having received the kingdom, he said that these slaves, to whom he had given the money, be called to him so that he might know what they had gained by their business.
19.16: " And the first came before him, saying, 'Lord, your mina has gained ten minas more. '
19.17: " And he said to him, 'Well done, good slave! Because you were faithful in a least thing, be in authority over ten cities. '
19.18: " And the second came, saying, 'Your mina, lord, has made five minas. '
19.19: " And he said to him also, 'And you are to be over five cities. '
19.20: " And another came, saying, 'Lord, behold your mina, which I kept put away in a handkerchief;
19.21: " 'for I was afraid of you, because you are a severe man; you take up what you did not lay down, and reap what you did not sow. '
19.22: " He said to him, 'Out of your mouth I will judge you, wicked slave. You knew that I was a severe man, taking what I did not lay down, and reaping what I did not sow.
19.23: " 'And why did you not put my money in the bank; and having come, I might have exacted it with interest? '
19.24: " And he said to those who stood by, 'Take the mina from him, and give it to the one who has ten minas. '
19.25: " And they said to him, 'Lord, he has ten minas. '
19.26: " I say to you that to everyone who has will I morebe given, but from the one who does not have, even what he does have will be taken away.
19.27: " But as for these enemies of mine, who did not want me to reign over them, bring them here and slay them in front of me. "
19.28: And after He had said these things, He went on ahead, going up to Yerushalayim.
19.29: And it happened that as He was nearing Beit - Pagey and Beit - Anyah, toward the mount that is called Olivet, He sent two of the disciples,
19.30: saying, " Go into the village opposite, in which upon entering you will find a colt tied, on which no one has ever yet sat; untie it and bring it.
19.31: " And if anyone asks you, 'Why are you untying it? ' thus you will say, 'The Lord has need of it. ' "
19.32: And those who were sent, having gone away, found it just as He had told them.
19.33: And as they were untying the colt, its owners said to them, " Why are you untying the colt? "
19.34: And they said, " The Lord has need of it. "
19.35: And they brought it to Yeshua, and they threw their garments upon the colt, and put Yeshua I upon it.
19.36: And as He was going, they were spreading their garments on the road.
19.37: And as He was now drawing near, toward the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began rejoicing to praise God with a great voice for all the miracles which they had seen,
19.38: saying, " BLESSED IS THE KING WHO COMES IN THE NAME OF ADONAI! Peace in Heaven and glory in the highest! "
19.39: And certain of the Pharisees in the crowd said to Him, " Teacher, rebuke Your disciples. "
19.40: And He answered and said, " I tell you, if these should be silent, the stones will cry out. "
19.41: And when He drew near, He saw the city and wept over it,
19.42: saying, " If you had known in this day, even you, the things for your peace! But now they have been hidden from your eyes.
19.43: " For the days shall come upon you when your enemies will cast around you a rampart, and will hold you in on every side,
19.44: " and dash you to the ground, and your children within you, and they will not leave in you one stone upon another, because you did not know the season of your visitation. "
19.45: And He entered into the Temple and began to expel those who were selling,
19.46: saying to them, " It is written, 'MY HOUSE SHALL BE A HOUSE OF PRAYER'; but you have made it a CAVE OF ROBBERS. "
19.47: And He was teaching daily in the Temple; but the chief priests and the scribes and the principal men among the people were seeking to utterly ruin Him,
19.48: but they could not find anything they could do; for all the people hung on, hearing Him.

20.1: And it happened on one of those days, as He was teaching the people and announcing the good news in the Temple, that the chief priests and the elders came upon I Him,
20.2: and spoke to Him, saying, " Tell us by what authority You do these things, or Who is the One Who gave You this authority? "
20.3: And He answered and said to them, " I will also ask you a word, and you tell Me:
20.4: " Was the immersion of Yochanan from Heaven or from men? "
20.5: And they reasoned with themselves, saying, " If we say, 'From Heaven, ' He will say, 'Why did you not believe him? '
20.6: " But if we say, 'From men, ' all the people will stone us; for they are convinced that Yochanan was a prophet. "
20.7: And they answered that they did not know from where.
20.8: And Yeshua said to them, " Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things. "
20.9: And He began to tell the people this parable: " A man planted a vineyard and rented it out to vine - growers, and went on a journey I abroadfor a long time.
20.10: " And at the I harvestseason he sent a slave to the vine - growers, in order that they might give him of the fruit of the vineyard; but the vine - growers beat him and sent him away empty.
20.11: " And he again sent another slave; and they beat him also and treated him shamefully, and sent him away empty.
20.12: " And he again sent a third; and this one also they wounded and expelled.
20.13: " And the lord of the vineyard said, 'What shall I do? I will send my beloved son. Perhaps they will respect him. '
20.14: " But when the vine - growers saw him, they reasoned with one another, saying, 'This is the heir. Let us kill him that the inheritance may be ours. '
20.15: " And they expelled him out of the vineyard and killed him. What, therefore, will the lord of the vineyard do to them?
20.16: " He will come and utterly ruin these vine - growers and give the vineyard to others. " And hearing this, they said, " May it never be! "
20.17: But He looked at them and said, " When then is this that has been written: 'THE STONE WHICH THE BUILDERS REJECTED, THIS BECAME THE CHIEF CORNER I stone '?
20.18: " Everyone falling on that stone will be broken in pieces; but on whomever it falls, it will scatter him like dust. "
20.19: And the scribes and the chief priests sought to lay hands on Him that very hour, but they feared the people; for they perceived that He spoke this parable against them.
20.20: And they scrupulously observed Him, and sent spies who pretended to be righteous, so that they might seize upon a word of His, so as to deliver Him up to the rule and the authority of the governor.
20.21: And they questioned Him, saying, " Teacher, we know that You speak and teach rightly, and that you do not receive a face, but teach the way of God in truth.
20.22: " Is it permitted for us to pay taxes to Caesar, or not? "
20.23: But He noted their craftiness and said to them,
20.24: " Show Me a denarius. Whose image and inscription does it have? " And they said, " Caesar’s. "
20.25: And He said to them, " Then render to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s. "
20.26: And they were not strong enough to seize Him in a spoken word in the presence of the people; and marveling at His answer they were silent.
20.27: Now some of the Sadducees came to Him, who say there is no resurrection,
20.28: and they questioned Him, saying, " Teacher, Moshe wrote to us, 'IF ANYONE'S BROTHER DIES, HAVING A WIFE, AND HE IS CHILDLESS, HIS BROTHER SHOULD TAKE THE WIFE AND RAISE UP OFFSPRING TO HIS BROTHER. '
20.29: " Now there were seven brothers; and the first took a wife, and died childless;
20.31: " and the third took her; and in like manner also I allseven died, leaving no children.
20.32: " And last of all the woman died.
20.33: " In the resurrection, therefore, which one’s wife will she be? For the seven had her as wife. "
20.34: And Yeshua said to them, " The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage,
20.35: " but those who are accounted worthy to attain that age and the resurrection from the dead, neither marry, nor are given in marriage;
20.36: " for neither do they have the power to die anymore, for they are equal to angels, and are sons of God, being sons of the resurrection.
20.37: “But that the dead are raised, even Moshe pointed out at the I burningbush, where he calls the Lord 'THE GOD OF AVRAHAM, AND THE GOD OF YITZCHAK, AND THE GOD OF YA'AKOV. '
20.38: " Now He is not the God of the dead, but of the living; for all live to Him. "
20.39: And some of the scribes answered and said, " Teacher, You have spoken well. "
20.40: For they did not have the courage to question Him any more about anything.
20.41: And He said to them, " How I dothey say the Messiah is Daveed’s son?
20.42: " For Daveed himself says in the scroll of Tehellim, 'ADONAI SAID TO MY LORD, " SIT AT MY RIGHT HAND,
20.43: " ' " UNTIL I PUT YOUR ENEMEIS AS A FOOTSTOOL FOR YOUR FEET. ' "
20.44: " Daveed thus calls Him 'Lord, ' and how is He his son? "
20.45: And as all the people were listening, He said to His disciples,
20.46: " Beware of the scribes, those desiring to walk about in long robes, and love greetings in the market places, and first seats in the synagogues, and first places at banquets,
20.47: " who eat up widows’ houses, and for a pretense offer long prayers; these will receive abundant judgment. "

21.1: And He looked up and saw the rich putting their gifts into the treasury.
21.2: And He saw a certain poor widow putting in two mites.
21.3: And He said, " Truly I say to you, this poor widow has put in more than all I of them;
21.4: " for these out of their abundance put into the gifts; but she out of her poverty put in all the living that she had. "
21.5: And while some were speaking concerning the Temple, that it was adorned with beautiful stones and devoted things, He said,
21.6: " These things which you are looking at, the days will come when there will not be left one stone upon another which will not be torn down. "
21.7: And they questioned Him, saying, " Teacher, when therefore will these things be? And what I will bethe sign when these things are about to occur? "
21.8: And He said, " See to it that you are not misled; for many will come in My name, saying, 'I am I He, ' and, 'The season is nearing'; do not go after them.
21.9: " And when you hear of wars and instabilities, do not be terrified; for it is necessary for these things to occur first, but the end is not immediate. "
21.10: Then He said to them, " Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
21.11: " Also there will be great earthquakes, and in various places plagues and famines; and there will be terrors and great signs from Heaven.
21.12: " But before all these things, they will lay their hands on you, and will persecute you, delivering you up to the synagogues and prisons, being brought before kings and governors for My name’s sake.
21.13: " This will turn out for you a testimony.
21.14: " Settle, then, your hearts not to prepare beforehand how to defend yourselves;
21.15: " for I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which none of your adversaries will have the power to resist or speak against.
21.16: " You will be delivered up even by parents and brothers and relatives and friends, and they will put I someof you to death,
21.17: " and you will be hated by all on account of My name.
21.18: " But not a hair of your head will perish.
21.19: " But by your patient endurance you will gain your lives.
21.20: " But when you see Yerushalayim encircled by armies, then know that her desolation has come near.
21.21: " Then let those who are in Yehudah flee to the mountains, and let those who are in the middle of the city withdraw, and let not those who are in the country enter into the city;
21.22: " because these are the days of vindication, in order that all things which are written may be fulfilled.
21.23: " Woe to those who are with child and those who nurse babies in those days; for there will be great distress upon the land, and wrath to this people,
21.24: " and they will fall by the edge of the sword, and will be led captive into all the nations, and Yerushalayim will be tread on by the nations until the seasons of the nations be fulfilled.
21.25: " And there will be signs in sun and moon and stars, and upon the Earth dismay among nations, in perplexity at the roaring of the sea and the waves,
21.26: " men fainting from fear and the expectation of what is coming on the world; for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
21.27: " And then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
21.28: " But when these things begin to occur, straighten up and lift up your heads, because your redemption is drawing near. "
21.29: And He told them a parable: " Look at the fig tree, and all the trees;
21.30: " as soon as they put forth I leaves, seeing I it, you will know for yourselves that the summer is already near.
21.31: " In this way, also, when you see these things happening, recognize that the Kingdom of God is near.
21.32: " Truly I say to you, this race will not pass away, until all things have occurred.
21.33: " Heaven and Earth will pass away, but My words will not pass away.
21.34: " But take heed that your hearts not be weighed down with dissipation and drunkenness and the anxieties pertaining to I thislife, and that day come on you suddenly like a trap;
21.35: " for as a trap it will come upon all those who dwell upon the face of the Earth.
21.36: " But remain sleepless, praying so that you may have strength to flee all these things that are about to occur, and to stand before the Son of Man. "
21.37: Now He was, during the days, in the Temple teaching, but during the nights He would go out and spend the night on the mount that is called Olivet.
21.38: And all the people were coming early unto Him in the Temple to hear Him.

22.1: Now Chag HaMatzah, being called Pesach, was nearing.
22.2: And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how they might take Him up; for they feared the people.
22.3: And HaSatan entered into Yehudah who was called I the man fromK’riot, being of the number of the twelve.
22.4: And he went away and conferred with the chief priests and the officers how he might deliver Him up to them.
22.5: And they were rejoiced and agreed to give him money.
22.6: And he consented and was seeking a fitting time to deliver Him up to them, away from the crowd.
22.7: Then came the day of Chag HaMatzah on which it was necessary for the Pesach to be sacrificed.
22.8: And He sent Petros and Yochanan, saying, " Go and prepare the Pesach for us, that we may eat it. "
22.9: And they said to Him, " Where do you want us to prepare it? "
22.10: And He said to them, " Behold, when you have entered into the city, a man will meet you carrying a pitcher of water; follow him into the house which he enters.
22.11: " And tell the master of the house, 'The Teacher says to you, " Where is the guest room where I am to eat the Pesach with My disciples? " '
22.12: " And he will show you a large upper spread out; prepare it there. "
22.13: And having gone, they found I itjust as He had told them; and they prepared the Pesach.
22.14: And when the hour had come, He reclined, and the apostles with Him.
22.15: And He said to them, " I have earnestly desired to eat this Pesach with you before I suffer,
22.16: " for I say to you that I shall not eat it again until it is fulfilled in the Kingdom of God. "
22.17: And when He had taken a cup I andgiven thanks, " Take this and distribute it among yourselves;
22.18: " for I say to you, I will not drink of the fruit of the vine from now on until the Kingdom of God comes. "
22.19: And when He had taken bread I andgiven thanks, He broke and gave I itto them, saying, " This is My body which is given for you; do this in remembrance of Me. "
22.20: And in like manner I He tookthe cup after they had dined, saying, " This cup which is poured out for you is the renewed covenant in My blood.
22.21: " But behold, the hand of him delivering Me up is with Me on the table.
22.22: " For indeed the Son of Man goes as it has been appointed; but woe to that man by whom He is delivered up! "
22.23: And they began to examine themselves which one of them it might be who was about to do this.
22.24: And there occurred also a dispute among them, which one of them was regarded to be greatest.
22.25: And He said to them, " The kings of the nations exercise lordship over them; and those exercising authority over them are called benefactors.
22.26: " But not so with you, but let him who is the greatest among you become as the youngest, and who is leading as the servant.
22.27: " For who is greater, the one who reclines I at the tableor the one who serves? Is it not the one who reclines? But I am among you as the One Who serves.
22.28: " And you are those who have continued with Me in My trials;
22.29: " and I grant to you, just as My Father did grant to Me, a Kingdom,
22.30: " that you may eat and drink at My table in My Kingdom, and you will sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Yisrael.
22.31: " Shimon, Shimon, HaSatan has demanded to sift you like wheat;
22.32: " but I have prayed for you that your faith may not fail; and you, when you have returned, strengthen your brethren. "
22.33: And he said to Him, " Lord, with You I am ready to go both to prison and to death! "
22.34: And He said, " I tell you, Petros, the rooster will not crow today until you have denied knowing Me three times. "
22.35: And He said to them, " When I sent you without a purse or bag or sandals, did you lack anything? " And they said, " Nothing. "
22.36: And He said to them, " But now, let him who has a purse take it, and likewise a bag; and let him who does not have sell his garment and buy a sword.
22.37: " For I tell you that this which is written must accomplish its goal in Me, 'AND HE WAS RECKONED WITH TRANSGRESSORS'; for what is written about Me has I itspurpose. "
22.38: And they said, " Lord, behold, here are two swords. " And He said to them, " It is sufficient. "
22.39: And coming out, He went on, according to His ethic, to the Mount of Olives; and the disciples also followed Him.
22.40: And having come to the place, He said to them, " Pray that you may not enter into temptation. "
22.41: And He was withdrawn from them, about a stone’s throw I away, and fell on His knees and was praying,
22.42: saying, " Father, if You are willing, remove this cup from Me; nevertheless not My will, but Yours be done. "
22.43: Now an angel from Heaven appeared to Him, strengthening Him.
22.44: And being in anguish, He prayed more intently; and His sweat became like drops of blood, falling down upon the ground.
22.45: And when He rose from prayer, coming to the disciples, He found them sleeping from grief,
22.46: and He said to them, " Why do you sleep? Rise and pray that you may not enter into temptation. "
22.47: While He was still speaking, behold, a crowd I came, and the one called Yehudah, one of the twelve, was coming before them; and He drew near to Yeshua to kiss Him.
22.48: But Yeshua said to Him, " Yehudah, are you delivering up the Son of Man with a kiss? "
22.49: And when those who were around Him saw what was about to occur, they said, " Lord, shall we strike with the sword? "
22.50: And a certain one of them struck the slave of the high priest and took off his right ear.
22.51: But Yeshua answered and said, " Leave I italone! " And He touched His ear and healed him.
22.52: And Yeshua said to those coming upon Him, the chief priests and officers of the Temple and elders, " Have you come out with swords and clubs as against a robber?
22.53: " While I was with you daily in the Temple, you did not extend your hands against Me; but this hour and the authority of darkness are yours. "
22.54: And seizing Him, they led Him I away, and brought Him to the house of the high priest; but Petros was following at a distance.
22.55: And when they had kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down together, Petros sat among them.
22.56: And a certain maidservant, having seen him sitting in the light, and looking intently at him, said, " This man also was with Him. "
22.57: But he denied I it, saying, " Woman, I do not know Him. "
22.58: And after a little while, another saw him and said, " You also are I oneof them. " But Petros said, " Man, I am not! "
22.59: And after about an hour had intervened, a certain other was confidently affirming, saying, " Certainly this one also was with Him, for he is also a Galilean. "
22.60: But Petros said, " Man, I do not know what you are saying. " And immediately, while he was still speaking, a rooster crowed.
22.61: And the Lord turned and looked at Petros. And Petros remembered the word of the Lord, how He had said to Him, " Before the rooster crows today, you will deny Me three times. "
22.62: And he went out and wept bitterly.
22.63: And the men who were holding Yeshua were mocking Him and beating Him;
22.64: and they blindfolded Him and questioned Him, saying, " Prophesy! Who is it who struck You? "
22.65: And blaspheming, they were saying many other things against Him.
22.66: And when day came, the council of elders of the people gathered together, both chief priests and scribes; and they led Him away to their own Sanhedrin, saying,
22.67: " If You are the Messiah, tell us. " But He said to them, " If I tell you, you will not believe;
22.68: " and if I ask a question, you will not answer.
22.69: " But from now on THE SON OF MAN WILL BE SEATED AT THE RIGHT HAND of the power of God. "
22.70: And they all said, " Are You then the Son of God? " And He said to them, " I AM. "
22.71: And they said, " What need yet we have of testimony? For we ourselves have heard it from His own mouth. "

23.1: And rising up, the whole number of them led Him before Pilatos.

23.3: And Pilatos questioned Him, saying, " Are You the King of the Yehudim? " And He answered him and said, " You say I it. "
23.4: And Pilatos said to the chief priests and the crowd, " I find no fault in this Man. "
23.5: But they insisted, saying, " He stirs up the people, teaching throughout all Yehudah, having begun from Galil to here. "
23.6: But when Pilatos heard this, he asked whether the Man was a Galilean.
23.7: And having known that He was from Herodes’ jurisdiction, he sent Him to Herodes, who himself also was in Yerushalayim in those days.
23.8: Now when Herodes saw Yeshua, he rejoiced; for he had wanted to see Him for a long time, because of hearing many things about Him. And he hoped to see some sign done by Him.
23.9: And he questioned Him in sufficient words; but He answered him nothing.
23.10: And the chief priests and the scribes stood, vehemently accusing Him.
23.11: And Herodes with his soldiers, having treated Him with contempt and mocking Him, arrayed Him in an elegant robe and sent Him back to Pilatos.
23.12: Now Herodes and Pilatos became friends with each other that very day; for before they had been at enmity with each other.
23.13: And Pilatos called together the chief priests and the rulers of the people,
23.14: and said to them, " You brought me this Man as One Who incites the people, and behold, examining Him before you, I have found no fault in this Man I inwhat you charge against Him.
23.15: " No, nor has Herodes, for he sent Him back to us; and behold, nothing worthy of death has been done by Him.
23.16: " I will therefore chastise Him and release Him. "
23.17: I Now he had to release to them one at the festival.
23.18: But they cried out with the whole multitude, saying, " Away with this man, and release for us Bar - Abba! " - -
23.19: who had been, because of a certain insurrection that had occurred in the city, thrown into prison.
23.20: And Pilatos, wanting to release Yeshua, called to them again,
23.21: but they kept shouting, saying, " Crucify, crucify Him! "
23.22: And a third time he said to them, " Why? What evil has He done? I have found no cause I fordeath in Him; I will therefore chastise Him and release Him. "
23.23: But they were pressing with great voices, asking that He should be crucified. And their voices overpowered.
23.24: And Pilatos pronounced sentence that their request be done.
23.25: And he released I the onewho because of insurrection and murder had been thrown into prison. But Yeshua he delivered up to their will.
23.26: And as they led Him away, they laid hold of a certain Shimon of Kureinei, coming in from the country, and placed on him the cross to bear behind Yeshua.
23.27: And there followed Him a great number of the people and of women who bewailed and lamented Him.
23.28: But Yeshua, turning to them, said, " Daughters of Yerushalayim, do not weep over Me, but weep over yourselves and over your children.
23.29: " For behold, the days are coming when they will say, 'Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that did not bear, and the breast that did not nurse. '
23.30: " Then they will begin to SAY TO THE MOUNTAINS, 'FALL ON US'; AND TO THE HILLS, 'COVER US. '
23.31: " For if they do these things in the green tree, what will take place in the dry? "
23.32: And others also, two criminals, were led with Him to be put to death.
23.33: And when they came to the place that is called Skull, there they crucified Him, and the criminals, one on the right and one on the left.
23.34: And Yeshua said, " Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. " And they cast lots to divide His garments.
23.35: And the people stood by, watching; but the rulers scoffed at Him, saying, " He saved others; let Him save Himself. I That isif He is the Messiah of God, His Chosen One! "
23.36: The soldiers also mocked Him, approaching Him and offering Him wine vinegar,
23.37: and saying, " If You are the King of the Yehudim, save Yourself! "
23.38: Now there was also an inscription above Him, " THIS IS THE KING OF THE YEHUDIM. "
23.39: And one of the criminals who was hanged blasphemed Him, saying, " Are You not the Messiah? Save Yourself and us! "
23.40: 40 But the other answering, and rebuking him, said, " Do you not even fear God, because you are in the same judgment?
23.41: " And we indeed justly, for we are receiving things worthy of what we did; but this One did nothing wrong. "
23.42: And he said, " Yeshua, remember me when You come into Your Kingdom. "
23.43: And He said to him, " Truly I say to you, today you will be with Me in Paradise. "
23.44: And it was now about the sixth hour, and darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.
23.45: And the sun failed, and the curtain of the Temple was split in the middle.
23.46: And Yeshua, crying out with a great voice, said, " Father, into Your hands I commit My spirit. " And having said this, He expired.
23.47: Now when the centurion saw what had taken place, he glorified God, saying, " Certainly this Man was righteous. "
23.48: And all the crowd present together at this sight, when they saw what had taken place, turned back beating their breasts.
23.49: And all those known to Him stood at a distance, and the women who followed Him from Galil, beholding these things.
23.50: And behold, a man named Yosef, being a councilor, a good and righteous man
23.51: - - he had not consented to their counsel and deed - - from Ramatayim, a city of the Yehudim, who was expecting the Kingdom of God;
23.52: this man went to Pilatos and asked for the body of Yeshua.
23.53: And he took it down and wrapped it in a linen shroud, and placed Him in a rock - hewn tomb, where no one had ever yet been laid.
23.54: And it was the Preparation Day, and a Shabbat was dawning.
23.55: Now the women who had come with Him out of Galil followed after, and looked at the tomb, and how His body was placed.
23.56: And they turned back and prepared spices and ointments. And on the Shabbat they rested according to the commandment.

24.1: But on the first of the week, at daybreak, they went to the tomb, bearing the spices which they had prepared.
24.2: And they found the stone rolled away from the tomb,
24.3: but when they entered into I it, they did not find the body of the Lord Yeshua.
24.4: And it happened, while they were perplexed about this, that behold, two men stood by them in shining clothing;
24.5: and as they were frightened and bowed their faces to the ground, they said to them, " Why do you seek the living among the dead?
24.6: " He is not here, but He is risen! Remember how He told you, while He was still in Galil,
24.7: " saying that it was necessary for the Son of Man to be delivered up into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and on the third day rise again. "
24.8: And they remembered His spoken words,
24.9: and having turned back from the tomb they reported all these things to the eleven, and to all the rest.
24.10: Now it was Miriam of Magdala and Yochanah and Miriam the I motherof Ya’akov, and the other women with them, who told these things to the apostles;
24.11: And these words appeared to them as silly talk, and they would not believe them.
24.12: I But Petros arose and ran to the tomb; stooping down he saw the linen alone; and he went away to his own home, wondering at what had happened.
24.13: And behold, two of them were going that very day to a village named Amma’us, which was about sixty stadia from Yerushalayim.
24.14: And they conversed to each other about all these things taking place.
24.15: And it happened that while they conversed and reasoned together, Yeshua Himself neared, and was going on with them.
24.16: But their eyes were held so as not to recognize Him.
24.17: And He said to them, " What are these words that you exchange with each other as you walk? " And they stood, looking sad.
24.18: And one of them, whose name was Kleopas, answered and said to Him, " Are You the only One visiting Yerushalayim and unaware of what things have occurred in these days? "
24.19: And He said to them, " What things? " And they said to Him, " The things about Yeshua of Natzeret, Who was a prophet, powerful in word and work before God and all the people,
24.20: " and how the chief priests and our rulers delivered Him up to a judgment of death, and crucified Him.
24.21: " But we were hoping that it was He Who was about to redeem Yisrael. But then with all these things, it is I nowthe third day since these things happened.
24.22: " But also some women among us amazed us. When they were at the tomb early,
24.23: " and did not find His body, they came, saying also to have seen a vision of angels, who said that He was alive.
24.24: " And some of those who were with us went to the tomb, and found it just as in this way as the women also had said; but Him they did not see. "
24.25: And He said to them, " O foolish ones and slow of heart, to believe in all that the prophets have spoken!
24.26: " Was it not necessary that the Messiah should suffer these things and enter into His glory? "
24.27: And beginning with Moshe and all the Prophets, He thoroughly explained to them all the Scriptures concerning Himself.
24.28: And as they neared the village where they were going, He seemed to be going further.
24.29: And they constrained Him, saying, " Stay with us, for it is toward evening, and the day is now far spent. " And He went in to stay with them.
24.30: And it happened in His reclining with them, He took the bread and blessed I it, and breaking I itHe gave I itto them.
24.31: And their eyes were opened completely and they recognized Him, and He became unseen by them.
24.32: And they said to one another, " Did not our hearts burn within us while He talked to us on the road, while He was opening up the Scriptures to us? "
24.33: And they arose at that same hour and turned back to Yerushalayim, and found the eleven gathered together and those who were with them,
24.34: saying, " The Lord has risen indeed, and has appeared to Shimon. "
24.35: And they explained what had happened on the road and how He was recognized by them in the breaking of the bread.
24.36: And as they were saying this, He Himself stood in the middle of them.
24.37: But they were startled and frightened, and supposed that they were seeing a spirit.
24.38: And He said to them, " Why are you troubled, and why do questionings arise in your hearts?
24.39: " See My hands and My feet, that it is I Myself; handle Me and see, for a spirit has not flesh and bones as you see that I have. "
24.40: I And having said this, He showed them His hands and His feet.
24.41: But while they were not believing from the joy, and were marveling, He said to them, " Have you anything here to eat? "
24.42: And they gave Him a piece of broiled fish,
24.43: and He took it and ate before them.
24.44: Now He said to them, " These are My words which I spoke to you, while I was still with you, that everything written about Me in the Torah of Moshe and the Prophets and the Tehellim must be fulfilled. "
24.45: Then He completely opened their minds to understand the Scriptures,
24.46: and He said to them, " In this way it has been written, that the Messiah should suffer and rise again from the dead the third day;
24.47: " and that the repentance for forgiveness of sins should be proclaimed in His name to all the nations, beginning from Yerushalayim.
24.48: " You are witnesses of these things.
24.49: " And behold, I sent forth the promise of My Father upon you; but you are to sit in the city until you are clothed with power from on high. "
24.50: And He led them out until Beit - Anyah, and lifting up His hands, He blessed them.
24.51: And it happened that while He blessed them, He parted from them.
24.52: And they turned back to Yerushalayim with great joy.
24.53: and were continually in the Temple, praising God.

1.1: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
1.2: He was in the beginning with God.
1.3: All things came into being through Him, and separately from Him not even one I thingcame into being that has come into being.
1.4: In Him was life, and the life was the Light of men.
1.5: And the Light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome it.
1.6: There came a man sent from God, whose name was Yochanan.
1.7: He came for testimony, to bear witness concerning the Light, that all might believe through him.
1.8: He was not the Light, but he bore witness concerning the Light.
1.9: The true Light that enlightens every man was coming into the world.
1.10: He was in the world, and the world came into being through Him, and the world did not know Him.
1.11: He came to His own, and His own did not take Him alongside I them.
1.12: But as many took Him alongside, to them He gave authority to become children of God, to those believing in His name,
1.13: who were born not of blood nor of the will of the flesh nor of the will of man, but of God.
1.14: And the Word became flesh, and tabernacled among us, and we beheld His glory, glory as of the only begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth.
1.15: Yochanan testified concerning Him, and cried out, saying, " This was He of Whom I said, 'He Who comes after me has been before me, for He existed before me. ' "
1.16: And out of His fullness we have all received, and grace on top of grace.
1.17: For the Torah was given through Moshe; grace and truth came through Yeshua the Messiah.
1.18: No one has ever seen God; the only begotten God, Who is in the bosom of the Father, He has made Him known.
1.19: And this is the testimony of Yochanan, when the Yehudim sent to him priests and Levites to Yerushalayim to question him, " Who are you? "
1.20: And he confessed and did not deny, and confessed, " I am not the Messiah. "
1.21: And they questioned him, " What then? Are you Eliyahu? " And he said, " I am not. " " Are you the Prophet? " And he answered, " No. "
1.22: They said then to him, " Who are you, that we may give an answer to those sending us? What do you say about yourself? "
1.23: He said, " I am a voice of one crying in the wilderness, 'MAKE STRAIGHT THE WAY OF ADONAI, ' as Yeshayahu the prophet said. "
1.24: And those sent were of the Pharisees.
1.25: And they questioned him and said to him, " Why then are you immersing, if you are not the Messiah, nor Eliyahu, nor the Prophet? "
1.26: Yochanan answered them, saying, " I immerse in water, I butin the middle of you stands One Whom you do not know.
1.27: " This isHe Who comes after me, the strap of Whose sandal I am not worthy to loosen. "
1.28: These things occurred in Beit - Anyah beyond the Yarden, where Yochanan was immersing.
1.29: On the next day he saw Yeshua coming toward him, and said, " Behold, the Lamb of God Who takes away the sin of the world!
1.30: " This is He on behalf of Whom I said, 'After me comes a Man Who has been before me, for He existed first. '
1.31: " And I myself did not know Him, but in order that He might be manifested to Yisrael, I came immersing in water. "
1.32: And Yochanan testified, saying, " I beheld the Spirit descending as a dove out of Heaven, and He remained upon Him.
1.33: " And I myself did not recognize Him, but He Who sent me to immerse in water said to me, 'He upon Whom you see the Spirit descending and remaining upon Him, this is He Who immerses in the Holy Spirit. '
1.34: " And I have seen and testified that this is the Son of God. "
1.35: Again on the next day Yochanan was standing, and two of his disciples,
1.36: and having looked upon Yeshua as he walked, he said, " Behold, the Lamb of God! "
1.37: And the two disciples heard him speak, and they followed Yeshua.
1.38: Now Yeshua turning, and having noticed them following, said to them, " What do you seek? " And they said to Him, " Rabbi, " which translated means Teacher, " where are You staying? "
1.39: He said to them, " Come and see. " They came then and saw where He was staying; and they stayed with Him that day, for it was about the tenth hour.
1.40: Andreas, the brother of Shimon Petros, was one of the two who heard Yochanan, and followed Him.
1.41: He found first his brother Shimon, and said to him, " We have found the Mashiach, " which translated means Anointed One.
1.42: He brought him to Yeshua. Yeshua looked at him, and said, " You are Shimon the son of Yochanan. You shall be called Kefa, " which is translated Petros.
1.43: On the next day He wished to go out into Galil, and He found Philippos. And Yeshua said to him, " Follow Me. "
1.44: Now Philippos was from Beit - Tzaidah, of the city of Andreas and Petros.
1.45: Philippos found Natan’el and said to him, " We have found Him of Whom Moshe wrote in the Torah, and the Prophets, Yeshua of Natzeret, the son of Yosef. "
1.46: And Natan’el said to him, " Is there the power for anything good to come out of Natzeret? " Philippos said to him, " Come and see. "
1.47: Yeshua saw Natan’el coming to Him, and said of him, " Behold, a Yisraeli indeed, in whom there is no guile! "
1.48: Natan’el said to Him, " How do you know me? " Yeshua answered and said to him, " Before Philippos called you, you being under the fig tree, I saw you. "
1.49: Natan’el answered Him, " Rabbi, You are the Son of God. You are the King of Yisrael. "
1.50: Yeshua answered and said to him, " Because I said to you I saw you under the fig tree, do you believe? You shall see greater things than these. "
1.51: And He said to him, " Truly, truly, I say to you, you will see Heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man. "

2.1: And on the third day there was a wedding at Kanah of Galil, and the mother of Yeshua was there;
2.2: and Yeshua also was invited, and His disciples, to the wedding.
2.3: And being short of wine, the mother of Yeshua said to Him, " They have no wine. "
2.4: And Yeshua said to her, " What is that to Me and to you, woman? My hour has not yet come. "
2.5: His mother said to the servants, " Whatever He tells you, do. "
2.6: Now there were six stone waterpots set I there, according to the purification of the Yehudim, each containing two or three measures.
2.7: Yeshua said to them, " Fill the waterpots with water. " And they filled them to the top.
2.8: And He said to them, " Draw out, now, and carry it to the headwaiter. " And they carried it I to him.
2.9: And when the headwaiter tasted the water that had become wine, and did not know where it came from - - thought the servants who had drawn the water knew - - the headwaiter called the bridegroom,
2.10: and said to him, " Every man first serves the good wine, and when they have drunk freely, then the inferior; you have kept the good wine until now. "
2.11: This beginning of I Hissigns Yeshua did in Kanah of Galil, and manifested His glory. And His disciples believed in Him.
2.12: After this He went down to K’far - Nachum, He and His mother and His brothers and His disciples; and they stayed not many days.
2.13: And the Pesach of the Yehudim was nearing, and Yeshua went up to Yerushalayim.
2.14: And He found in the Temple those who were selling oxen and sheep and doves, and the moneychangers seated.
2.15: And He made a whip of ropes, and expelled I themall out of the Temple, with the sheep and the oxen; and He poured out the coins of the moneychangers, and overturned their tables;
2.16: and to those who were selling the doves, He said, " Take these things away; you shall not make My Father’s House a house of trade. "
2.17: His disciples remembered that it was written, " ZEAL FOR YOUR HOUSE WILL CONSUME ME. "
