2.18: The Yehudim then said to Him, " What sign do You show to us, seeing that You do these things? "
2.19: Yeshua answered and said to them, " Dissolve this Temple, and in three days I will raise it up. "
2.20: The Yehudim then said, " Inforty - six years was this Temple built, and will You raise it up in three days? "
2.21: But He was speaking of the Temple of His body.
2.22: When therefore He was raised from the dead, His disciples remembered that He had said this; and they believed the Scripture and the word which Yeshua had spoken.
2.23: Now when He was in Yerushalayim at the Pesach, during the festival, many believed in His name, beholding signs that He was doing.
2.24: But Yeshua Himself was not trusting Himself to them, because He knew all men,
2.25: and because He had no need that anyone should bear witness concerning man, for He Himself knew what was in man.

3.1: Now there was a man of the Pharisees, named Nakdimon, a ruler of the Yehudim;
3.2: this man came to Him by night, and said to Him, " Rabbi, we know that you have come from God, a Teacher; for no one has the power to do these signs that You do unless God is with him. "
3.3: Yeshua answered and said to him, " Truly, truly, I say to you, unless one is born again he does not have the power to see the Kingdom of God. "
3.4: Nakdimon said to Him, " How can a man be born when he is old? Can he enter a second time into his mother’s womb and be born? "
3.5: Yeshua answered, " Truly, truly, I say to you, unless one is born of water and the Spirit, he does not have the power to enter into the Kingdom of God.
3.6: " That which is born of the flesh is flesh, and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.
3.7: " Do not marvel that I said to you, 'You must be born again. '
3.8: " The Spirit blows where He wishes, and you hear His voice; but you do not know from where He comes and where He goes; so is everyone who is born of the Spirit. "
3.9: Nakdimon answered and said to Him, " How do these things have the power to occur? "
3.10: Yeshua answered and said to him, " Are you the teacher of Yisrael, and do not know these things?
3.11: " Truly, truly, I say to you, that which we know, we speak; and that which we have seen, we bear witness; and you do not receive our witness.
3.12: " If I have told you Earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe if I tell you Heavenly things?
3.13: " And no one has ascended into Heaven, but He Who descended from Heaven, the Son of Man.
3.14: " And as Moshe lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up;
3.15: " that whoever believes in Him may have eternal life.
3.16: " For God so loved the world, that He gave His only begotten Son, that whoever believes in Him should not perish, but have eternal life.
3.17: " For God did not send His Son into the world to judge the world, but that the world might be saved through Him.
3.18: " He who believes in Him is not judged; he who does not believe in Him has been judged already, because he has not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.
3.19: " And this is the judgment, that the light has come into the world, and men loved the darkness rather than the light; for their works were evil.
3.20: " For everyone who practices evil hates the light, and does not come to the light, so that his works should be exposed.
3.21: " But he who is doing the truth comes to the light, that his works may be manifested, having been worked in God. "
3.22: After these things Yeshua and His disciples came into the land of Yehudah, and there He tarried with them and immersed.
3.23: And Yochanan also was immersing in Einayim near Shalem, because there was much water there; and they were coming and being immersed.
3.24: For Yochanan had not yet been cast into prison.
3.25: There arose therefore questioning from the disciples of Yochanan with a Yehudi about purification.
3.26: And they came to Yochanan and said to him, " Rabbi, He Who was with you beyond the Yarden, to Whom you have testified, behold, He is immersing, and all are coming to Him. "
3.27: Yochanan answered and said, " A man has the power to receive nothing, if it has not been given I tohim from Heaven.
3.28: " You yourselves testify to Me that I said, 'I am not the Messiah, ' but, 'I have been sent before Him. '
3.29: " He who has the bride is the bridegroom; but the friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices with joy because of the bridegroom’s voice. Therefore, this my joy has been fulfilled.
3.30: " It is necessary for Him to increase, but me to decrease.
3.31: " He Who comes from above is above all; he who is of the Earth is from the Earth, and speaks of the Earth. He Who comes from Heaven is above all.
3.32: " What He has seen and heard, of that He testifies; and no one receives His testimony.
3.33: " He who receives His testimony has sealed that God is true.
3.34: " For He Whom God has sent speaks the spoken words of God, for not by measure does God give the Spirit.
3.35: " The Father loves the Son, and has given all things into His hand.
3.36: " He who believes in the Son has eternal life; but he who does not believe in the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God abides on him. "

4.1: When therefore the Lord knew that the Pharisees had heard that Yeshua was making and immersing more disciples than Yochanan - -
4.2: although Yeshua Himself was not immersing, but His disciples - -
4.3: He left Yehudah and departed again into Galil.
4.4: And it was necessary to go through Shomron.
4.5: So He came to a city of Shomron, called Suchar, near the property that Ya’akov gave to his son Yosef;
4.6: and Ya’akov’s well was there. Yeshua therefore, being wearied by the journey was sitting thus on the well. It was about the sixth hour.
4.7: There came a woman of Shomron to draw water. Yeshua said to her, " Give Me a drink. "
4.8: For His disciples had gone away into the city to buy nourishment in the marketplace.
4.9: The Shomroni woman therefore said to him, " How is it that You, being a Yehudi, as to drink from me, being a Shomroni woman? " For Yehudim have no associations with Shomronim.
4.10: Yeshua answered and said to her, " If you knew the gift of God, and Who is it Who says to you, 'Give Me a drink, ' you would have asked Him, and He would have given you living water. "
4.11: She said to Him, " Lord, You have nothing to draw with and the well is deep. From where then do You have living water?
4.12: " Are You greater than our father Ya’akov, who gave us the well, and drank out of it himself, and his sons, and his cattle? "
4.13: Yeshua answered and said to her, " Everyone who drinks of this water will thirst again;
4.14: " but whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never thirst; but the water that I will give him will become in him a spring of water leaping up into eternal life. "
4.15: The woman said to Him, " Lord, give me this water, in order that I may not thirst, nor come here to draw. "
4.16: He said to her, " Go, call your husband, and come here. "
4.17: The woman answered and said, " I have no husband. " Yeshua said to her, " You are right in saying, 'I have no husband';
4.18: " for you have had five husbands, and he who you have now is not your husband; this you have said truly. "
4.19: The woman said to Him, " Lord, I perceive that You are a prophet.
4.20: " Our fathers worshipped on this mountain; and you say that in Yerushalayim is the place where it is necessary to worship. "
4.21: Yeshua said to her, " Woman, believe Me, an hour is coming when neither on this mountain, nor in Yerushalayim, will you worship the Father.
4.22: " You worship what you do not know; we worship that which we know, for salvation is of the Yehudim.
4.23: " But an hour is coming, and now is, when the true worshippers will worship the Father in spirit and truth; for such the Father seeks to worship Him.
4.24: " God is Spirit, and it is necessary for those who worship Him to worship Him in spirit and truth. "
4.25: The woman said to Him, " I know that Mashiach is coming, " He Who is called Anointed One, " when He comes He will announce all things to us. "
4.26: Yeshua said to her, " I Who speak to you am I He. "
4.27: And upon this, His disciples came and marveled that He was talking with a woman; yet no one said, " What do You seek? " or " Why are You talking with her? "
4.28: So the woman left her waterpot, and went away into the city, and said to the men,
4.29: " Come, see a man Who told me all the things that I I everdid. Is this One not the Messiah? "
4.30: They went out of the city and were coming to Him.
4.31: In the meantime the disciples were questioning Him, saying, " Rabbi, eat. "
4.32: But He said to them, " I have found eating to eat which you do not know. "
4.33: The disciples therefore said to one another, " Did anyone bring Him I anythingto eat? "
4.34: Yeshua said to them, " My food is to do the will of Him Who sent Me, and to bring His work to its goal.
4.35: " Do you not say, 'There are yet four months, and the harvest comes'? Behold, I say to you, lift up your eyes and look upon the fields that they are bright for harvest.
4.36: " Already he who reaps receives wages, and gathers fruit for eternal life; that he who sows and he who reaps may rejoice together.
4.37: " For in this the word is true, 'One sows and another reaps. '
4.38: " I sent you to reap that for which you did not labor; others have labored, and you have entered into their labor. "
4.39: And out of that city many of the Shomronim believed in Him, because of the word of the woman who bore witness, " He told me all the things that I I everdid. "
4.40: So when the Shomronim came to Him, they were asking Him to stay with them; and He stayed there two days.
4.41: And many more believed because of His word;
4.42: and they said to the woman, " It is no longer because of your saying that we believe, for we have heard for ourselves, and know that this One is truly the Savior of the world. "
4.43: And after the two days He went out from there into Galil.
4.44: For Yeshua Himself testified that a prophet has no honor in his own country.
4.45: So when He came to Galil, the Galileans received Him, having seen all that He had done in Yerushalayim at the festival; for they themselves also went to the festival.
4.46: Then Yeshua came again to Kanah of Galil where He had made the water wine. And there was a certain royal official, whose son was sick at K’far - Nachum.
4.47: When he heard that Yeshua had come out of Yehudah into Galil, he went and requested Him to come down and heal his son; for he was about to die.
4.48: Yeshua therefore said to him, " Unless you see signs and wonders, you will not believe. "
4.49: The royal official said to Him, " Lord, come down before my child dies. "
4.50: Yeshua said to him, " Go; your son lives. " The man believed the word that Yeshua spoke to him, and went I away.
4.51: And as he was going down, I hisslaves met him, saying that his son was alive.
4.52: So he inquired of them the hour in which he became better. Then they said to him, " Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him. "
4.53: So the father knew that I it wasin that hour in which Yeshua said to him, " Your son lives. " And he himself believed, and his whole house.
4.54: This was again a second sign that Yeshua had done, when He had come out of Yehudah into Galil.

5.1: After these things there was a festival of the Yehudim, and Yeshua went up to Yerushalayim.
5.2: Now there is in Yerushalayim by the Sheep I Gatea pool, in Ivri called Beit - Zata, which has five porticos.
5.3: In these lay a great number of those who were sick, blind, lame, and withered, I waiting for the moving of the waters;
5.4: for an angel of the Lord descended at certain seasons into the pool and agitated the water. The first then walking in, after the agitation of the water, was made healthy from whatever disease he was held by.
5.5: And a certain man was there, being in infirmity thirty - eight years.
5.6: When Yeshua saw Him bedridden there, and knew that he had already been I therea long time, He said to him, " Do you want to get well? "
5.7: The sick man answered Him, " Lord, I have no man to put me into the pool when the water is stirred up, and while I am going, another goes down before me. "
5.8: Yeshua said to him, " Arise, lift up your pallet, and walk. "
5.9: And immediately the man became well, and lifted up his pallet and was walking. Now it was the Shabbat on that day.
5.10: Therefore the Yehudim said to the man who was cured, " It is the Shabbat, and it is not permitted for you to lift up your pallet. "
5.11: But he answered them, " He Who made me healthy was the One Who said to me, 'Lift up your pallet and walk. ' "
5.12: They asked him, " Who is the Man Who said to you, 'Lift up I your palletand walk'? "
5.13: Now the man who had been healed did not know Who it was; for Yeshua had withdrawn, as there was a crowd in the place.
5.14: Afterward, Yeshua found him in the Temple, and said to him, " Behold, you have become healthy. Sin no more, that nothing worse happen to you. "
5.15: The man went away and told the Yehudim that it was Yeshua Who had made him healthy.
5.16: And on account of this the Yehudim were persecuting Yeshua, because He was doing these things on the Shabbat.
5.17: But Yeshua answered them, " My Father works until now, and I Myself am working. "
5.18: Because of this, then, the Yehudim were seeking more to kill Him, because He was not only loosing the Shabbat, but also was calling God His Own Father, making Himself equal to God.
5.19: Yeshua therefore answered and said to them, " Truly, truly, I say to you, the Son can do nothing of Himself, except I it issomething He sees the Father doing; for whatever I Hedoes, these things the Son also does likewise.
5.20: " For the Father loves the Son, and shows Him all things that He Himself is doing; and greater works than these will He show Him, that you may marvel.
5.21: " For just as the Father raises the dead and makes them alive, even in this way the Son also makes alive whom He wishes.
5.22: " For the Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son,
5.23: " in order that all may honor the Son, just as they honor the Father. He who does not honor the Son does not honor the Father Who sent Him.
5.24: " Truly, truly, I say to you, he who hears My word and believes Him Who sent Me, has eternal life, and does not come into judgment, but has passed out of death into life.
5.25: " Truly, truly, I say to you, an hour is coming, and now is, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live.
5.26: " For just as the Father has life in Himself, so He gave also to the Son to have life in Himself;
5.27: " and authority He gave Him to perform judgment; because He is I theSon of Man.
5.28: " Do not marvel at this; for an hour is coming in which all who are in the tombs shall hear His voice,
5.29: " and shall come forth; those who did the good I thingsto a resurrection of life, those who did the evil I thingsto a resurrection of judgment.
5.30: " I do not have the power to do anything of Myself. As I hear, I judge; and My judgment is righteous, because I do not seek My Own will, but the will of Him Who sent Me.
5.31: " If I alone testify concerning Myself, My testimony is not true.
5.32: " There is another Who testifies concerning Me, and I know that the testimony which He testifies concerning Me is true.
5.33: " You have sent to Yochanan, and he has testified to the truth.
5.34: " But I do not receive testimony from man, but I say these things that you may be saved.
5.35: " He was the burning and shining lamp, and you were willing to rejoice, for an hour, in his light.
5.36: " But the testimony which I have is greater than Yochanan’s; for the works which the Father has given to Me to bring to the goal, the very works that I do, testify concerning Me, that the Father has sent Me.
5.37: " And the Father Who has sent Me has Himself testified concerning Me. You have neither heard His voice at any time, nor have you seen His form.
5.38: " And you do not have His word abiding in you, for you do not believe Him Who He sent.
5.39: " You search the Scriptures, because you think that in them you have eternal life; and it is these which testify concerning Me;
5.40: " and you will not come to Me, that you may have life.
5.41: " I do not receive glory from men.
5.42: " But I know that you do not have the love of God in yourselves.
5.43: " I have come in My Father’s name, and you do not receive Me; if another comes in his own name, you will receive him.
5.44: " How will you have the power to believe, who receive glory from one another, and do not seek the glory that is from the only God?
5.45: " Do not think that I will accuse you to the Father; it is Moshe who accuses you, in whom you have hoped.
5.46: " For if you believed Moshe, you would believe Me; for he wrote concerning Me.
5.47: " But if you do not believe his writings, how will you believe My spoken words? "

6.1: After these things Yeshua went away to the other side of the Sea of Galil, or Tiberias.
6.2: And a great crowd was following Him, because they were seeing the signs that He was doing on those who were sick.
6.3: And Yeshua went up on the mountain, and there He sat with His disciples.
6.4: Now the Pesach, the festival of the Yehudim, was nearing.
6.5: Then Yeshua, lifting up His eyes, and seeing that a great crowd was coming to Him, said to Philippos, " Where are we to buy bread at a marketplace, that these may eat? "
6.6: And this He said to test him; for He Himself knew what He was about to do.
6.7: Philippos answered Him, " Two hundred denarii worth of bread is not sufficient for them, for each of them to take a little. "
6.8: One of His disciples, Andreas, Shimon Petros’ brother, said to Him,
6.9: " There is a little boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish, but what are these for so many? "
6.10: Yeshua said, " Make the people sit down. " Now there was much grass in the place; therefore the men sat down, in number about five thousand.
6.11: Yeshua then took the loaves I of bread; and having given thanks He distributed to those who were reclining; likewise also of the fish as much as they wished.
6.12: And when they were satisfied, He said to His disciples, " Gather up the abounding broken pieces that nothing may be lost. "
6.13: So they gathered them together and filled twelve baskets with broken pieces from the twelve barley loaves, which were abounding by those who had eaten.
6.14: When therefore the people saw the sign that He had done, they said, " This is truly the Prophet Who is coming to the world! "
6.15: Yeshua therefore, knowing they were about to come and seize Him, to make Him king, withdrew again to the mountain by Himself alone.
6.16: Now when evening came, His disciples went down to the sea,
6.17: and having stepped onto a boat, they were crossing the sea to K’far - Nachum. And it had already become dark, and Yeshua had not yet come to them.
6.18: And the sea was aroused by a great wind blowing.
6.19: When therefore they had rowed about twenty - five or thirty stadia, they gazed at Yeshua walking on the sea and coming near to the boat; and they were frightened.
6.20: But He said to them, " It is I; do not be afraid. "
6.21: Then they wished to take Him into the boat, and the boat was immediately at the land to which they were going.
6.22: On the next day the crowd that stood on the other side of the sea saw that there was no other small boat there, except one, and that Yeshua had not entered I ittogether with His disciples into the boat, but His disciples had gone away alone.
6.23: However, other small boats came from Tiberius near to the place where they ate the bread after the Lord had given thanks.
6.24: When therefore the crowd saw that Yeshua was not there, nor His disciples, they themselves stepped onto the small boats, and came to K’far - Nachum, seeking Yeshua.
6.25: And having found Him on the other side of the sea, they said to Him, " Rabbi, when did You come here? "
6.26: Yeshua answered them and said, " Truly, truly, I say to you, you seek Me, not because you saw signs, but because you ate of the loaves I of bread, and were satisfied.
6.27: " Do not work for the eating which perishes, but for the eating which continues to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give to you, for on Him did the Father seal, God. "
6.28: They said therefore to Him, " What shall we do, that we I canwork the works of God? "
6.29: Yeshua answered and said to them, " This is the work of God, that you believe in Him Whom He has sent. "
6.30: They said therefore to Him, " Then what sign do You do that we may see and believe You? What do You work?
6.31: " Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness; as it is written, 'HE GAVE THEM BREAD OUT OF HEAVEN TO EAT. ' "
6.32: Yeshua therefore said to them, " Truly, truly, I say to you, Moshe has not given you bread out of Heaven, but My Father gives you the true bread out of Heaven.
6.33: " For the bread of God is that which comes down out of Heaven, and gives life to the world. "
6.34: They said therefore to Him, " Lord, always give us this bread. "
6.35: Yeshua said to them, " I am the bread of life; he who comes to Me shall not hunger, and he who believes in Me shall never thirst.
6.36: " But I said to you that you have seen Me and yet do not believe.
6.37: " All that the Father gives Me will come to Me, and he who comes to Me will not be cast out.
6.38: " For I have come down from Heaven, not to do My Own will, but the will of Him Who sent Me.
6.39: " And this is the will of Him Who sent Me, that all that He has given Me I may not lose of it, but raise it up on the last day.
6.40: " For this is the will of My Father, that everyone who beholds the Son and believes in Him should have eternal life; and I Myself will raise him up on the last day. "
6.41: The Yehudim, therefore, were murmuring about Him, because He said, " I am the bread that came down out of Heaven. "
6.42: And they said, " Is this not Yeshua, the son of Yosef, Whose father and mother we know? How does He now say, 'I have come down out of Heaven'? "
6.43: Yeshua answered and said to them, " Do not murmur among yourselves.
6.44: " No one has the power to come to Me, unless the Father Who sent Me draws Him; and I will raise Him up on the last day.
6.45: " It is written in the Prophets, 'AND THEY SHALL ALL BE TAUGHT BY GOD. ' Everyone who has heard and learned from the Father comes to Me.
6.46: " Not that anyone has seen the Father, except He Who is from God; He has seen the Father.
6.47: " Truly, truly, I say to you, he who believes has eternal life.
6.48: " I am the bread of life.
6.49: " Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, and they died.
6.50: " This is the bread which comes down out of Heaven, that a man may eat of it and not die.
6.51: " I am the living bread which came down out of Heaven; if anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever; and the bread also which I will give is My flesh, which I will give for the life of the world. "
6.52: The Yehudim, therefore, were fighting with one another, saying, " How does this one have the power to give us I Hisflesh to eat? "
6.53: Yeshua therefore said to them, " Truly, truly, I say to you, unless you eat of the flesh of the Son of Man and drink His blood, you have no life in yourselves.
6.54: " He who eats My flesh and drinks My blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day.
6.55: " For My flesh is true eating, and My blood is true drinking.
6.56: " He who gnaws at My flesh and drinks My blood abides in Me, and I in him.
6.57: " Even as the Living Father sent Me, and I live because of the Father, so he who gnaws on Me, even that one will live because of Me.
6.58: " This is the bread which came down out of Heaven; not as the fathers ate, and died. He who eats this bread will live forever. "
6.59: These things He said in a synagogue, teaching in K’far - Nachum.
6.60: Then many of His disciples, having heard, said, " This is a difficult word; who has the power to listen to it? "
6.61: But Yeshua, perceiving that His disciples were murmuring about this, said to them, " Does this cause you to stumble?
6.62: " Then I whatif you should behold the Son of Man ascending where He was before?
6.63: " It is the Spirit Who gives life; the flesh profits nothing; the spoken words that I have spoken to you are spirit and are life.
6.64: " But there are certain of you who do not believe. " For Yeshua knew from the beginning who they were who did not believe, and who it was who would deliver Him up.
6.65: And He said, " Because of this I have said to you, that no one has the power to come to Me, unless it has been granted him from the Father. "
6.66: From this I timemany of His disciples went away into the things behind, and were not walking with Him anymore.
6.67: Yeshua then said to the twelve, " Do you also wish to go away? "
6.68: Shimon Petros answered him, " Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the spoken words of eternal life.
6.69: " And we have believed and have known that You are the Holy One of God. "
6.70: Yeshua answered them, " Did I not choose you, the twelve? But one of you is a devil. "
6.71: Now He spoke of Yehudah, I the sonof Shimon I fromK’riot. For he, one of the twelve, was about to deliver Him up.

7.1: And after these things Yeshua was walking in Galil; for He was unwilling to walk in Yehudah, because the Yehudim were seeking to kill Him.
7.2: Now the festival of the Yehudim, Sukkot, was nearing.
7.3: Then His brothers said to Him, " Depart from here and go away into Yehudah, that Your disciples also may behold Your works that You are doing.
7.4: " For no one does anything in secret and himself seeks to be in public. If You do these things, manifest Yourself to the world. "
7.5: For not even His brothers were believing in Him.
7.6: Yeshua therefore said to them, " My season is not yet present, but your season is always prepared.
7.7: " The world does not have the power to hate you; but it hates Me because I testify concerning it, that its works are evil.
7.8: " Go up to the festival yourselves; I do not go up to this festival because My season has not yet been fulfilled. "
7.9: And saying these things to them, He remained in Galil.
7.10: But when His brothers had gone up to the festival, then He Himself also went up, not manifestly, but as in secret.
7.11: The Yehudim therefore were seeking Him at the festival, and were saying, " Where is He? "
7.12: And there was much muttering about Him among the crowds. Some said, " He is a good I One "; others said, " No, but He leads the crowds astray. "
7.13: Yet no one spoke openly of Him, because of the fear of the Yehudim.
7.14: But I beingthe middle of the festival Yeshua went up into the Temple, and was teaching.
7.15: The Yehudim therefore were marveling, saying, " How is it that this Man has learning, having never been taught? "
7.16: Yeshua therefore answered them, and said, " My teaching is not Mine, but His Who sent Me.
7.17: " If anyone is willing to do His will, he shall know concerning the teaching, whether it is of God, or I whetherI speak of Myself.
7.18: " He who speaks of himself seeks his own glory; but He Who seeks the glory of the One Who sent Him, this One is true, and unrighteousness is not in Him.
7.19: " Did not Moshe give you the Torah? And none of you keeps the Torah? Why do you seek to kill Me? "
7.20: The crowd answered, " You have a demon! Who seeks to kill You? "
7.21: Yeshua answered and said to them, " I did one work, and you all marvel.
7.22: " On this account Moshe has given you circumcision - - not that it is from Moshe, but from the fathers - - and on Shabbat you circumcise a man.
7.23: " If a man receives circumcision on Shabbat that the Torah of Moshe may not be loosed, are you angry with Me because I made an entire man healthy on Shabbat?
7.24: " Do not judge according to appearance, but judge with righteous judgment. "
7.25: Then some of the people of Yerushalayim were saying, " Is not this He Whom they are seeking to kill?
7.26: " And here He is, speaking openly, and they say nothing to Him. Do the rulers not truly know that this is the Messiah?
7.27: " But we know this One, where He is from. But whenever the Messiah comes, no one knows where He is from. "
7.28: Yeshua therefore cried out in the Temple, teaching and saying, " You both know Me and know where I am from; and I have not come of Myself, but He Who sent Me is true, Whom you do not know.
7.29: " I know Him, because I am from Him, and He sent Me. "
7.30: They were seeking, therefore, to seize Him; and no one laid his hand on Him, because His hour had not yet come.
7.31: But many of the crowd believed in Him, and they said, " The Messiah, when He comes, will He work more signs than those which this Man has done? "
7.32: The Pharisees heard the crowd muttering these things about Him; and the chief priests and Pharisees sent officers to seize Him.
7.33: Yeshua then said, " For a little while I am with you, and I go to Him Who sent Me.
7.34: " You will seek Me and you will not find Me; and where I am You do not have the power to come. "
7.35: The Yehudim therefore said to one another, " Where does this Man intend to go that we shall not find Him? He is not intending to go to the Diaspora among the Greeks, and teach the Greeks, is He?
7.36: " What is this word that He said, 'You will seek Me and you will not find Me; and where I am You do not have the power to come. ' "
7.37: Now on the last day, the great I dayof the festival, Yeshua stood and cried out, saying, " If any one is thirsty, let Him come to Me and drink.
7.38: " He who believes in Me, as the Scripture has said, 'Out of His belly shall flow rivers of living waters. ' "
7.39: Now this He spoke concerning the Spirit, which those who believe in Him were to receive; for the Spirit was not yet I given, because Yeshua was not yet glorified.
7.40: I Some, therefore, out of the crowd, when they heard these words, said, " This is truly the Prophet. "
7.41: Others said, " This is the Messiah. " But some said, " No! For does the Messiah come out of Galil?
7.42: " Have not the Scripture said that the Messiah comes from the sperm of Daveed, and from Beit - Lechem, the village where Daveed was? "
7.43: So there was a schism in the crowd because of Him.
7.44: And certain of them wanted to seize Him, but no one laid hands on Him.
7.45: The officers then came to the chief priests and Pharisees, and they said to them, " Why did you not bring Him? "
7.46: The officers answered, " Never did a man speak as this. "
7.47: The Pharisees therefore answered them, " Have you also been led astray?
7.48: " Did any one of the rulers or Pharisees believe in Him?
7.49: " But this crowd which does not know the Torah is accursed. "
7.50: Nakdimon said to them - - he who came to Him before, being one of them - -
7.51: " Does our Torah judge a man, unless it first hears from him and knows what he is doing? "
7.52: They answered and said to him, " Are you also from Galil? Search, and see that a prophet has not been raised out of Galil. "
7.53: I And everyone went to his house.

8.1: But Yeshua went to the Mount of Olives.
8.2: And at dawn, He again arrived into the Temple; and all the people were coming to Him, and He was teaching them.
8.3: And the scribes and the Pharisees brought a woman who had been caught in adultery, and set her in the middle,
8.4: they said to Him, " Teacher, this woman has been caught in the very act - - committing adultery.
8.5: " Now in the Torah, Moshe commanded that such should be stoned. What therefore do You say? "
8.6: And this they said, tempting Him, in order that they may accuse Him. But Yeshua bent down, and with His finger wrote on the ground.
8.7: But when they stayed on in asking Him, He straightened up and said to them, " Let he who is without sin among you I bethe first to throw a stone at her. "
8.8: And again He bent down, and wrote on the ground.
8.9: And when they heard it, they went out one by one, beginning with the elders, and He was left alone, and the woman standing in the middle.
8.10: And straightening up, Yeshua said to her, " Woman, where are they? Did no one condemn you? "
8.11: And she said, " No one, Lord. " And Yeshua said, " Neither do I condemn you. Go, and from now sin no more. "
8.12: Again therefore Yeshua spoke to them, saying, " I am the light of the world; he who follows Me will not walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life. "
8.13: The Pharisees then said to Him, " You testify concerning Yourself; Your testimony is not true. "
8.14: Yeshua answered and said to them, " Even if I testify concerning Myself, My testimony is true; for I know from whence I came and where I am going. But you do not know from whence I came or where I am going.
8.15: " You judge according to the flesh; I do not judge anyone.
8.16: " And even if I do judge, My judgment is true; because I am not alone, but I and the Father Who sent Me.
8.17: " And in your I ownTorah also it has been written, that the testimony of two men is true.
8.18: " I am I OneWho is testifying of Myself, and the Father Who sent Me testifies of Me. "
8.19: They then said to Him, " Where is Your Father? " Yeshua answered, " You know neither Me nor My Father; if you knew Me, you would know My Father also. "
8.20: These spoken words He spoke in the treasury, teaching in the Temple; but no one seized Him, because His hour had not yet come.
8.21: He said therefore again to them, " I go away, and you will seek Me and die in your sin. Where I am going, you do not have the power to come. "
8.22: Therefore the Yehudim said, " Will He kill Himself, because He says, 'Where I am going, you do not have the power to come'? "
8.23: And He said to them, " You are from below, I am from above; you are of this world, I am not of this world.
8.24: " I said therefore to you, that you would die in your sins; for if you do not believe I am I He, you will die in your sins. "
8.25: They therefore said to Him, " Who are You? " Yeshua said to them, " The Beginning, what I also say to you.
8.26: " I have much to say and to judge concerning you, but He Who sent Me is true; and what I heard from Him, these things I say to the world. "
8.27: They did not know that He spoke to them I ofthe Father.
8.28: Yeshua then said, " When you exalt the Son of Man, then you will know that I am I He; and I do nothing of Myself, but I speak these things as the Father taught Me.
8.29: " And He Who sent Me is with Me; He has not left Me alone, for I always do the things pleasing to Him. "
8.30: As He spoke these things, many believed in Him.
8.31: Yeshua therefore said to the Yehudim who had believed in Him, " If you abide in My word, you are truly My disciples;
8.32: " and you will know the truth, and the truth will make you free. "
8.33: They answered Him, " We are the sperm of Avraham, and have never been enslaved to anyone. How is it that You say, 'You will become free'? "
8.34: Yeshua answered them, " Truly, truly, I say to you, everyone who does sin is a slave of sin.
8.35: " And the slave does not stay in the house forever; the son stays forever.
8.36: " If therefore the Son makes you free, you will be free indeed.
8.37: " I know that you are the sperm of Avraham. But you seek to kill Me, because My word is not given room in you.
8.38: " I speak of what I have seen with I MyFather; therefore you also do what you have heard from I yourfather. "
8.39: They answered and said to Him, " Avraham is our father. " Yeshua said to them, " If you were Avraham’s children, do the works of Avraham.
8.40: " But now, you seek to kill Me, a Man Who has spoken the truth to you which I heard from God; this is not what Avraham did.
8.41: " You are doing the works of your father. " They said to Him, " We were not born of fornication. We have one Father, God. "
8.42: Yeshua said to them, " If God were your Father, you would love Me; for I came forth and have come from God. For neither have I come of Myself, but He sent Me.
8.43: " Why do you not know My speech? Because you do not have the power to hear My word.
8.44: " You are of I yourfather the Devil, and you want to do the lusts of your father. He was a murderer from the beginning, and does not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaks a lie, he speaks from his own; for he is a liar and the father of lies.
8.45: " But because I speak the truth, you do not believe Me.
8.46: " Which of you convicts Me of sin? If I speak truth, why do you not believe Me?
8.47: " He who is of God hears the spoken words of God; because of this you do not hear, because you are not of God. "
8.48: The Yehudim answered and said to Him, " Do we not say well that you are a Shomroni and have a demon? "
8.49: Yeshua answered, " I do not have a demon; but honor My Father, and you dishonor Me.
8.50: " But I do not seek My I ownglory; there is One Who seeks and judges.
8.51: " Truly, truly, I say to you, if anyone keeps My word He will never see death. "
8.52: The Yehudim said to him, " Now we know that you have a demon. Avraham died, and the prophets; and you say, 'If anyone keeps My word, he will never taste death. '
8.53: " Are You greater than our father Avraham who died? The prophets died also. Whom do You make Yourself? "
8.54: Yeshua answered, " If I glorify Myself, My glory is nothing; it is My Father Who glorifies Me, of Whom you say that He is your God.
8.55: " And you have not known Him; but I know Him; and if I say that I have not known Him, I would be a liar like you; but I do know Him and keep His word.
8.56: " Your father Avraham rejoiced to see My day; and he saw and rejoiced. "
8.57: The Yehudim then said to Him, " You are not yet fifty years old, and have you seen Avraham? "
8.58: Yeshua said to them, " Truly, truly, I say to you, before Avraham was, I AM. "
8.59: Therefore they took up stones to cast at Him; but Yeshua hid Himself and went out of the Temple.

9.1: And passing by, He saw a man blind from birth.
9.2: And His disciples asked Him, saying, " Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind? "
9.3: Yeshua answered, " Neither this one nor his parents sinned, but that the works of God might be manifest in him.
9.4: " It is necessary that we must work the works of Him Who sent Me, while it is day; night is coming, when no man has the power to work.
9.5: " When I am in the world, I am the Light of the world. "
9.6: Having said this, He spit on the ground and made clay of the spittle, and placed the clay upon his eyes,
9.7: and said to him, " Go, wash in the pool of Shiloach, " which is interpreted, Sent. And so he went away and washed, and came seeing.
9.8: The neighbors, therefore, and those who had seen him before as a beggar, said, " Is this not the one who used to sit and beg? "
9.9: Others said, " This is he "; others said, " No, but he is like him. " He said, " I am the one. "
9.10: They then said to him, " How then were your eyes opened? "
9.11: He answered, " The Man called Yeshua made clay and anointed my eyes, and said to me, 'Go to Shiloach and wash'; so I went away and washed and recovered my sight. "
9.12: And they said to him, " Where is He? " He said, " I do not know. "
9.13: They brought to the Pharisees him who had been once blind.
9.14: Now it was Shabbat and the day when Yeshua made the clay and opened his eyes.
9.15: Again, therefore, the Pharisees also were asking him how he recovered his sight. And he said to them, " He placed clay upon my eyes, and I washed, and I see. "
9.16: Of the Pharisees, therefore, certain said, " This Man is not from God, because He does not keep the Shabbat. " But others said, " How I doesa man, a sinner, have the power to work such signs? " And there was a division among them.
9.17: They said therefore to the blind man again, " What do you say concerning Him, because He opened your eyes? " And he said, " He is a prophet. "
9.18: The Yehudim, therefore, did not believe concerning him, that he had been blind and had recovered his sight, until they called the parents of the very one who had recovered his sight,
9.19: and questioned them, saying, " Is this your son, who you say was born blind? How then does he now see? "
9.20: His parents answered them and said, " We know that this is our son, and that he was born blind;
9.21: " but how he now sees we do not know, nor do we know who opened his eyes. Ask him; he is of maturity, he will speak for himself. "
9.22: His parents said this because they feared the Yehudim; for the Yehudim had already agreed that if anyone should confess Him to be Messiah, he was to be expelled from the synagogue.
9.23: Because of this his parents said, " He is of maturity; ask him. "
9.24: They therefore called, a second I time, the man who had been born blind, and said to him, " Give glory to God; we know that this Man is a sinner. "
9.25: He then answered, " Whether He is a sinner, I do not know; one thing I do know, that, being blind, I now see. "
9.26: They then said to him, " What did He do to you? How did He open your eyes? "
9.27: He answered them, " I have told you already, and you did not hear. Why do you want to hear again? Do you also wish to become His disciples? "
9.28: And they reviled him, saying, " You are His disciple, but we are disciples of Moshe.
9.29: " We know that God has spoken to Moshe, but this One, we do not know where He is from. "
9.30: The man answered and said to them, " For there is a marvel in this, that you do not know where He is from, and He opened my eyes!
9.31: " We know that God does not listen to sinners; but if anyone is God - fearing and does His will, He listens to him.
9.32: " From I the beginningof the age it has not been heard that anyone opened the eyes of one who has been born blind.
9.33: " If this Man were not from God, He would have the power to do nothing. "
9.34: They answered and said to him, " You were born wholly in sins, and you would teach us? " And they cast him out.
9.35: Yeshua heard that they cast him out; and having found him, He said, " Do you believe in the Son of Man? "
9.36: He answered and said, " And Who is He, Lord, that I may believe in Him? "
9.37: Yeshua said to him, " You have both seen Him, and it is He Who speaks to you. "
9.38: And he said, " Lord, I believe "; and he worshipped Him.
9.39: And Yeshua said, " For judgment I came into this world, that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind. "
9.40: Those of the Pharisees who were with Him heard these things, and said to Him, " Are we not also blind? "
9.41: Yeshua said to them, " If you were blind, you would have no sin; but now that you say, 'We see, ' your sin remains. "

10.1: " Truly, truly, I say to you, he who is not entering in through the door into the fold of the sheep, but goes up by another way, he is a thief and a robber.
10.2: " But he who is entering in through the door is shepherd of the sheep.
10.3: " To him the doorkeeper opens, and the sheep hear his voice, and he calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
10.4: " When he puts forth all his own, he goes in front of them, and the sheep follow him because they know his voice.
10.5: " But they will not follow a stranger. Instead they will flee from him, because they do not know the voice of strangers. "
10.6: Yeshua spoke this allegory to them, but they did not know what it was which He spoke to them.
10.7: Then Yeshua said to them again, " Truly, truly, I say to you, I am the door of the sheep.
10.8: " All who came before Me are thieves and robbers; but the sheep did not hear them.
10.9: " I am the door; if anyone enters through Me, he will be saved, and will go in and out, and find pasture.
10.10: " The thief comes only to steal, to kill, and to ruin; I came that they might have life, and have I itabundantly.
10.11: " I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down His life for the sheep.
10.12: " He who is a hireling and not a shepherd, whose own the sheep are not, sees the wolf coming and leaves the sheep and flees; and the wolf seizes them, and scatters I the sheep.
10.13: " He fleesbecause he is a hireling and is not caring concerning the sheep.
10.14: " I am the good shepherd; and I know My own, and My own know Me,
10.15: " just as the Father knows Me and I know the Father; and I lay down My life for the sheep.
10.16: " And I have other sheep, which are not out of this fold; I must bring them also, and they shall hear My voice; and they shall become one flock I withone shepherd.
10.17: " For this reason the Father loves Me, because I lay down My life that I may take it again.
10.18: " No one takes it from Me by violence, but I lay it down of Myself. I have authority to lay it down, and I have authority to take it again. This commandment I receive from My Father. "
10.19: There was a schism again among the Yehudim because of these words.
10.20: And many of them said, " He has a demon and is insane. Why listen to Him? "
10.21: Others said, " These are not the spoken words of one demon - possessed. Does a demon have the power to open the eyes of the blind? "
10.22: At that time Chanukah took place in Yerushalayim;
10.23: it was winter, and Yeshua was walking in the Temple in the portico of Shlomo.
10.24: Then the Yehudim encircled Him, and said to Him, " Until when do you lift up our soul? If You are the Messiah, tell us freely. "
10.25: Yeshua answered them, " I told you, and you do not believe. The works that I do in My Father’s name, these testify concerning Me.
10.26: " But you do not believe, because you are not of My sheep.
10.27: " My sheep hear My voice, and I know them, and they follow Me;
10.28: " and I give eternal life to them, and they shall not perish; and no one shall seize them out of My hand.
10.29: " My Father, Who has given I themto Me, is greater than all; and no one has the power to seize I themout of the hand of the Father.
10.30: " I and the Father are one. "
10.31: The Yehudim took up stones again to stone Him.
10.32: Yeshua answered them, " I have shown you many good works from the Father. For which of them do you stone Me? "
10.33: The Yehudim answered Him, " For a good work we do not stone You, but concerning blasphemy; and because You, being a Man, make Yourself God. "
10.34: Yeshua answered them, " Has it not been written in your own Torah, I SAID YOU ARE GODS'?
10.35: " If He called them gods, to whom the word of God came - - and the Scripture does not have the power to be loosened - -
10.36: " do you say of Him Whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world, 'You are blaspheming, ' because I said, 'I am the Son of God'?
10.37: " If I am not doing the works of My Father, do not believe Me;
10.38: " but if I do them, even if you do not believe Me, believe the works, that you may know and recognize that the Father is in Me, and I in the Father. "
10.39: Then again they sought to seize Him, and He came out from their hand.
10.40: And He went away again to the other side of the Yarden, to the place where Yochanan was first immersing, and He remained there.
10.41: And many came to Him and said, " Yochanan, indeed, did no sign; but all things that Yochanan said concerning this One were true. "
10.42: And many believed in Him there.

11.1: Now a certain one was sick, El’azar from Beit - Anayah, the village of Miriam and her sister Marta.
11.2: And it was Miriam who anointed the Lord with ointment and wiped His feet with her hair, whose brother El’azar was sick.
11.3: Then the sisters sent to Him, saying, " Lord, behold, he whom You love is sick. "
11.4: But when Yeshua heard it, He said, " This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, that the Son of God may be glorified through it. "
11.5: Now Yeshua loved Marta and her sister and El’azar.
11.6: When therefore He heard that he was sick, He remained in the place where He was two days.
11.7: Then after this He said to the disciples, " Let us go to Yehudah again. "
11.8: The disciples said to him, " Rabbi, just now the Yehudim were seeking to stone You, and You are going there again? "
11.9: Yeshua answered, " Are there not twelve hours in the day? If anyone walks in the day, he does not stumble, because he sees the light of this world.
11.10: " But if anyone walks in the night, he stumbles, because the light is not in him. "
11.11: These things He said, and after this He said to them, " Our friend El’azar has fallen asleep; but I go to awaken him out of sleep. "
11.12: The disciples therefore said to them, " Lord, if he has fallen asleep, he will be saved. "
11.13: Now Yeshua had spoken of his death, but they thought that He spoke of the sleep of slumber.
11.14: Therefore, then Yeshua said to them plainly, " El’azar is dead,
11.15: " and I rejoice, because of you, in order that you may believe, that I was not there. But let us go to him. "
11.16: Toma therefore, who is called Didumos, said to the fellow disciples, " Let us also go, that we may die with Him. "
11.17: Yeshua, therefore, having come, found that El’azar had already been in the tomb four days.
11.18: Now Beit - Anyah was near Yerushalayim, about fifteen stadia away;
11.19: and many of the Yehudim had come to Marta and Miriam, to console them concerning their brother.
11.20: Marta, therefore, when she heard that Yeshua was coming, met Him; but Miriam kept sitting in the house.
11.21: Marta therefore said to Yeshua, " Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.
11.22: " But even now I know that whatever you ask from God, God will give You. "
11.23: Yeshua said to her, " Your brother will rise again. "
11.24: Marta said to Him, " I know that he will rise again in the resurrection on the last day. "
11.25: Yeshua said to her, " I am the Resurrection and the Life; he who believes in Me, even if he may die, shall live,
11.26: " and everyone who lives and believes in Me shall never die. Do you believe this? "
11.27: She said to Him, " Yes, Lord; I believe that You are the Messiah, the Son of God, Who is coming to the world. "
11.28: And having said this, and called Miriam her sister, saying secretly, " The Teacher is present and is calling for you. "
11.29: And when she heard it, she arose quickly and went to Him.
11.30: Now Yeshua had not yet come into the village, but was still in the place where Marta had met Him.
11.31: Then the Yehudim who were with her in the house, and consoling her, seeing that Miriam quickly rose up and went out, followed her, supposing that she was going to the tomb to weep there.
11.32: Then Miriam, when she came where Yeshua was, seeing Him, fell at His feet, saying to Him, " Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died. "
11.33: Yeshua, therefore, when He saw her weeping, and the Yehudim who came with her I alsoweeping, was deeply moved in the spirit and troubled Himself,
11.34: and said, " Where have you placed him? " They said to Him, " Lord, come and see. "
11.36: The Yehudim, therefore, said, " Behold how He loved him! "
11.37: But certain of them said, " Did not this One, Who opened the eyes of him who was blind, have the power to have kept this I manfrom dying? "
11.38: Yeshua, therefore, deeply moved again, came to the tomb. And it was a cave, and a stone was lying upon I the entrance.
11.39: Yeshua said, " Take away the stone. " Marta, the sister of the one that had died, said to Him, " Lord, already there will be a stench, for he has been I in therefour days. "
11.40: Yeshua said to her, " Did I not tell you that if you would believe you would see the glory of God? "
11.41: They then took away the stone. And Yeshua lifted up His eyes and said, " Father, I thank You that You have heard Me.
11.42: " And I know that You always hear Me; but I have said this on account of the people standing around I Me, in order that they may believe that You have sent Me. "
11.43: And when He had said these things, He cried out with a great voice, " El’azar, come here! "
11.44: He who had died came out, being bound feet and hands with cloths, and his face was tied around with a head cloth. Yeshua said to them, " Loosen him, and let him go. "
11.45: Many, therefore, of the Yehudim who had come to Miriam and had beheld what He had done, believed in Him.
11.46: But certain of them went away to the Pharisees and told them what Yeshua had done.
11.47: Therefore the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered together I theSanhedrin, and said, " What are we doing? For this Man does many signs.
11.48: " If we let Him I alonethis way, all will believe in Him, and the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation. "
11.49: But a certain one of them, Kayafa, who was high priest that year, said to them, " You know nothing at all;
11.50: " nor consider that it is profitable for you that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation should not perish. "
11.51: But he did not say this of himself, but being high priest that year he prophesied that Yeshua was about to die for the nation,
11.52: and not for the nation only, but that also the children of God who have been scattered abroad might be gathered into one.
11.53: Then from that day, they took counsel I togetherto kill Him.
11.54: Yeshua therefore no longer walked openly among the Yehudim, but went away from there to the country near the wilderness, into a city called Ephraim; and there He stayed with the disciples.
11.55: Now the Pesach of the Yehudim was nearing, and many went up to Yerushalayim out of the country before the Pesach, to purify themselves.
11.56: Then they sought Yeshua, and said with one another, standing in the Temple, " What does it seem to you? That He does not come to the festival? "
11.57: Now the chief priests and the Pharisees had commanded that if anyone knew where He was, he should report it so that they might seize Him.

12.1: Yeshua, therefore, six days before the Pesach, came to Beit - Anyah where El’azar was, whom Yeshua had raised from the dead.
12.2: Then they made a supper there, and Marta served. But El’azar was one of those reclining with Him.
12.3: Miriam therefore took a litra of costly perfume of pure nard and anointed the feet of Yeshua and wiped His feet with her hair; and the house was filled with the aroma of the perfume.
12.4: But Yehudah I fromK’riot, one of His disciples, who was about to deliver Him up, said,
12.5: " Why was this perfume not sold for three hundred denarii, and given to the poor? "
12.6: Now he said this, not because he cared concerning the poor, but because he was a thief, and he had the money case and carried away what was put into it.
12.7: Yeshua therefore said, " Let her alone, so that she may keep it for the day of My burial.
12.8: " For the poor you will always have with you, but you will not always have Me. "
12.9: Then a great crowd of the Yehudim learned that He was there; and they came, not only because of Yeshua, but also to see El’azar, whom He raised from the dead.
12.10: But the chief priests took counsel to kill El’azar also;
12.11: because on account of him many of the Yehudim were going away, and believing in Yeshua.
12.12: On the next day the great crowd that had come to the festival, having heard that Yeshua had come to Yerushalayim,
12.13: took palm branches and went out to a meeting with Him, and were crying, " Hoshia - na! BLESSED IS HE WHO COMES IN THE NAME OF ADONAI, even the King of Yisrael! "
12.14: And Yeshua found a young donkey and sat upon it; as it is written,
12.15: " FEAR NOT, DAUGHTER OF TZIYON; YOUR KING IS COMING, SEATED ON THE FOAL OF A DONKEY. "
12.16: But His disciples did not recognize these things at first; but when Yeshua was glorified, then they remembered that these things were written of Him, and they did these things to Him.
12.17: Then the crowd that was with Him when He called El’azar out of the tomb, and raised him from the dead, bore witness.
12.18: Because of this also the crowd went and met Him, because they heard that He had done this sign.
12.19: The Pharisees therefore said to one another, " You see that you can do nothing profitable. Behold, the world has gone after Him. "
12.20: Now there were certain Greeks out of those who were going up to worship at the festival;
12.21: these therefore approached Philippos, who was from Beit - Tzaidah of Galil, and were asking him, saying, " Lord, we wish to see Yeshua. "
12.22: Philippos came and told Andreas; Andreas and Philippos came and they told Yeshua.
12.23: And Yeshua answered them, saying, " The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.
12.24: " Truly, truly, I say to you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the ground and dies, it remains by itself alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.
12.25: " He who loves his life looses it; but he who hates his life in this world shall keep it to life eternal.
12.26: " If anyone serves Me, let Him follow Me; and where I am, there also will My servant be; if anyone serves Me, the Father will honor him.
12.27: " Now My soul is troubled; and what shall I say? 'Father, save Me from this hour'? But because of this I came to this hour.
12.28: " Father, glorify Your name. " Then came a voice out of Heaven, " I have both glorified it, and will glorify it again. "
12.29: Then standing and hearing, the crowd said that thunder occurred. Others said, " An angel has spoken to Him. "
12.30: Yeshua answered and said, " This voice has not come because of Me, but because of you.
12.31: " Now judgment is of this world; now shall the ruler of this world be cast out.
12.32: " And I, if I be lifted up from the Earth, will draw all men to Myself. "
12.33: But He said this, signifying by what kind of death by which He was about to die.
12.34: The crowd therefore answered Him, " We have heard out of the Torah that the Messiah remains forever. And how can You say, 'It is necessary for the Son of Man to be lifted up? ' Who is this Son of Man? "
12.35: Yeshua therefore said to them, " Yet a little while the light is with you. Walk while you have the light, that darkness may not lay hold of you; he who walks in the darkness does not know where he goes.
12.36: " While you have the light, believe in the light, so that you may become sons of light. " These things Yeshua spoke, and He departed and hid Himself from them.
12.37: But though He had done so many signs before them, they were not believing in Him;
12.38: that the word of Yeshayahu the prophet might be fulfilled, " ADONAI, WHO HAS BELIEVED OUR REPORT? AND TO WHOM HAS THE ARM OF ADONAI BEEN REVEALED? "
12.39: Because of this they did not have the power to believe, for Yeshayahu said again,
12.40: " HE HAS BLINDED THEIR EYES AND HARDENED THEIR HEART; LEST THEY SHOULD SEE WITH THEIR EYES AND PERCEIVE WITH THEIR HEART, AND TURN BACK, AND I HEAL THEM. "
12.41: These things Yeshayahu said because he saw His glory and spoke of Him.
12.42: Still, however, many even of the rulers believed in Him, but because of the Pharisees they did not confess I it, lest they should be expelled from the synagogue;
12.43: for they loved the glory of men more than the glory of God.
12.44: And Yeshua cried out and said, " He who believes in Me, believes not in Me, but in Him Who sent Me.
12.45: " And he who beholds Me beholds Him Who sent Me.
12.46: " I have come I asa light to the world, that everyone who believes in Me may not remain in darkness.
12.47: " And if anyone hears My spoken words, and does not keep them, I do not judge him; for I did not come to judge the world, but save the world.
12.48: " He who rejects Me and does not receive My spoken words has that judging him; the word that I have spoken will judge him on the last day.
12.49: " Because I did not speak of Myself, but the Father Himself Who sent Me has given Me commandment what to say and what to speak.
12.50: " And I know that this commandment is eternal life. Therefore what I speak, as the Father has said to Me, so I speak. "

13.1: Now before the festival of the Pesach, Yeshua knew that His hour had come that He should move from this world to the Father, having loved His own who were in the world, to the end He loved them.
13.2: And supper having occurred, the Devil having already put in the heart of Yehudah I son ofShimon, I fromK’riot, to deliver Him up,
13.3: I Yeshua, knowing that the Father had given all things into His hands, and that He came out from God, and was going back to God,
13.4: rose up from the supper and laid aside His garments; and taking a towel, He girded Himself.
13.5: Then He poured water into the basin, and began to wash the feet of the disciples, and to wipe them with the towel with which He was girded.
13.6: He then came to Shimon Petros, I andthat one said to Him, " Lord, do You wash my feet? "
13.7: Yeshua answered and said to him, " What I am doing you do not know now, but you will know afterward. "
13.8: Petros said to him, " You shall never wash my feet. " Yeshua answered him, " If I do not wash you, you have no part in Me. "
13.9: Shimon Petros said to him, " Lord, not my feet only, but also my hands and head. "
13.10: Yeshua said to him, " He who has bathed has no need I otherthan to wash the feet, but is wholly clean; and you are clean, but not all. "
13.11: For He knew who was delivering Him up; because of this He said, " You are not all clean. "
13.12: Then when He had washed their feet and had taken His garments, reclining again, He said to them, " Do you know what I have done to you?
13.13: " You call Me Teacher and Lord; and you say well, for I am.
13.14: " If therefore I washed your feet, the Lord and Teacher, you also ought to wash the feet of one another.
13.15: " For I gave you an example, that according as I did to you, you should do also.
13.16: " Truly, truly, I say to you, a slave is not greater than his lord; nor an apostle greater than he who sent him.
13.17: " If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them.
13.18: " I do not speak concerning all of you. I know the ones I have chosen; but that the Scripture may be fulfilled, 'HE WHO EATS MY BREAD HAS LIFTED UP HIS HEEL AGAINST ME. '
13.19: " From just now I am telling you before I itoccurs, so that when it does occur, you may believe that I AM.
13.20: " Truly, truly, I say to you, he who receives whomever I send receives Me; and he who receives Me receives Him Who sent Me. "
13.21: When Yeshua had said this, He was troubled in the spirit, and testified, and said, " Truly, truly, I say to you, that one of you will deliver Me up. "
13.22: The disciples were looking at one another, perplexed concerning of whom He was speaking.
13.23: There was one of His disciples reclining on His breast, whom Yeshua loved.
13.24: Then Shimon Petros nodded to Him, and said to Him, " Tell I uswho it is concerning whom He speaks. "
13.25: And I the oneleaning back on the breast of Yeshua said to Him, " Lord, who is it? "
13.26: Yeshua answered, " That is the one for whom I shall dip this morsel and give it to him. " So when He had dipped the morsel, He took and gave it to Yehudah I son ofShimon, I fromK’riot.
13.27: And after the morsel, HaSatan then entered into him. Yeshua therefore said to him, " What you do, do quickly. "
13.28: But no one of those reclining knew this, for what He spoke to him.
13.29: For some thought, because Yehudah had the money case, that Yeshua was saying to him, " Buy the things we need for the festival "; or that he should give something to the poor.
13.30: Then, receiving the morsel, he immediately went out; and it was night.
13.31: When therefore he had gone out, Yeshua said, " Now is the Son of Man glorified, and God is glorified in Him;
13.32: " if God is glorified in Him, God will also glorify Him in Himself, and immediately will glorify Him.
13.33: " Little children, yet a little while I am with you. You will seek Me; and as I said to the Yehudim, I now say to you also, 'Where I am going, you do not have the power to come. '
13.34: " An unused commandment I give to you, that you love one another, even as I have loved you, that you also love one another.
13.35: " By this all will know that you are My disciples, if you have love for one another. "
13.36: Shimon Petros said to Him, " Lord, where are you going? " Yeshua answered, " Where I am going, you do not have the power to follow Me now, but you will follow later. "
13.37: Petros said to Him, " Lord, why do I not have the power to follow you just now? I will lay down my life for You. "
13.38: Yeshua answered, " Will you lay down your life for Me? Truly, truly, I say to you, a rooster will not crow until you deny Me three times.

14.1: " Let not your heart be troubled; believe in God, believe also in Me.
14.2: " In My Father’s House are many stations; if it were not so, I would not have told you; for I go to prepare a position I of authorityfor you.
14.3: " And if I go and prepare a position I of authorityfor you, I will come again and take you to Myself, that where I am, you may be also.
14.4: " And you know the way where I am going. "
14.5: Toma said to Him, " Lord, we do not know where You are going. How do we have the power to know the way? "
14.6: Yeshua said to him, " I am the way, and the truth, and the life; no one comes to the Father, but through Me.
14.7: " If you had known Me, you would have known My Father also; henceforth you have known Him and have seen Him. "
14.8: Philippos said to Him, " Lord, show us the Father, and it will suffice for us. "
14.9: Yeshua said to him, " Have I been with you so long, and you have not known Me, Philippos? He who has seen Me has seen the Father; how do you say, 'Show us the Father'?
14.10: " Do you not believe that I am in the Father, and the Father is in Me? The spoken words I say to you I do not speak of Myself, but the Father Who abides in Me, He does the works.
14.11: " Believe Me that I am in the Father, and the Father in Me; but if not, believe Me because of the works themselves.
14.12: " Truly, truly, I say to you, he who believes in Me, the works that I do he shall do also; and greater than these will he do; because I go to the Father.
14.13: " And whatever you may ask in My name, this I will do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
14.14: " If you ask anything in My name, I will do I it.
14.15: " If you love Me, you will keep My commandments.
14.16: " And I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Helper, that He may be with you forever;
14.17: " the Spirit of truth, Whom the world does not have the power to receive, because it neither beholds Him nor knows Him. I Butyou know Him because He abides with you and will be in you.
14.18: " I will not leave you as orphans; I will come to you.
14.19: " Yet a little while the world will behold Me no more, but you behold Me. Because I live, you shall also live.
14.20: " In that day you will know that I am in My Father, and you in Me, and I in you.
14.21: " He who has My commandments and keeps them, he it is who loves me; and he who loves Me shall be loved by My Father, and I will love him, and I will manifest Myself to him. "
14.22: Yehudah said to Him, not the I one fromK’riot, " Lord, what has happened that you are about to manifest Yourself to us, and not to the world? "
14.23: Yeshua answered and said to Him, " If anyone loves Me, He will keep My word; and My Father will love him, and We will come to Him and make Our station with him.
14.24: " He who does not love Me does not keep My words; and the word which you hear is not Mine, but the Father’s Who sent Me.
14.25: " These things I have spoken to you, remaining with you.
14.26: " But the Helper, the Holy Spirit, Whom the Father will send in My name, He will teach you all things, and bring to your remembrance all that I have said to you.
14.27: " Peace I leave with you; My peace I give to you; not as the world gives do I give to you. Let not your heart be troubled, nor let it be afraid.
14.28: " You heard Me say to you, 'I go away and will come to you. ' If you love Me, you would have rejoiced, because I go to the Father; because the Father is greater than I.
14.29: " And now I have told you before it takes place, so that when it does take place, you will believe.
14.30: " I will no longer speak many things with you, for the ruler of this world is coming, and he has nothing in Me;
14.31: " but that the world may know that I love the Father, and even as the Father commanded Me, so I do. Arise, let us go hence.

15.1: " I am the true vine, and My Father is the vinedresser.
15.2: " Every branch in Me not bearing fruit, He takes it away by violence; and every I branchwhich does not bear fruit, He cleanses, that it may bear more fruit.
15.3: " You are already clean on account of the word which I have spoken to you.
15.4: " Abide in Me, and I in you. As the branch does not have the power to bear fruit of itself, unless it abides in the vine, so neither I canyou, unless you abide in Me.
15.5: " I am the vine, you are the branches. He who abides in Me, and I in him, he bears much fruit; for apart from Me you have the power to do nothing.
15.6: " If anyone does not abide in Me, he is cast I outas a branch, and dries up; and they gather them, and cast them into the fire, and they are burned.
15.7: " If you abide in Me, and My words abide in you, ask whatever you wish, and it shall be done for you.
15.8: " In this is My Father glorified, that you bear much fruit, and I sobecome My disciples.
15.9: " According as the Father has loved Me, I have also loved you; abide in My love.
15.10: " If you keep My commandments, you will abide in My love; just as I have kept My Father’s commandments, and abide in His love.
15.11: " These things I have spoken to you, that My joy may be in you, and your joy may be made full.
15.12: " This is My commandment, that you love one another, just as I have loved you.
15.13: " Greater love has no one than this: that one lay down his life for his friends.
15.14: " You are My friends if you do what I command you.
15.15: " No longer do I call you slaves, because the slave does not know what his lord is doing; but I have called you friends, because all that I have heard from My Father I have made known to you.
15.16: " You did not choose Me, but I chose you and appointed you that you should go and bear fruit, and I thatyour fruit should abide, in order that whatever you ask of the Father in My name, He may give to you.
15.17: " This I command you, that you love one another.
15.18: " If the world hates you, know that it has hated Me before you.
15.19: " If you were of the world, the world would love its own; but because you are not of the world, but I chose you out of the world, therefore the world hates you.
15.20: " Remember the word that I said to you, 'A slave is not greater than his lord. ' If they persecuted Me, they also will persecute you. If they kept My word, they also will keep yours.
15.21: " But all these things they will do to you on account of My name, because they do not know Him Who sent Me.
15.22: " If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have sin; but now they have no excuse for their sin.
15.23: " He who hates Me hates My Father also.
15.24: " If I had not done among them the works which no one else did, they would not have sin; but now they have seen and hated both me and my Father.
15.25: " But I they have done thisso that the word may be fulfilled that is written in their I ownTorah, 'THEY HATED ME WITHOUT A CAUSE. '
15.26: " When the Helper comes, Whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth Who goes forth from the Father, He will testify of Me,
15.27: " and you also testify, because you have been with Me from the beginning.

16.1: " These things I have spoken to you, that you may not stumble.
16.2: " They will expel you from the synagogue, but an hour is coming so that everyone killing you will think that he is offering a service to God.
16.3: " And they will do these things because they do not know the Father nor Me.
16.4: " But these things I have spoken to you, that when their hour comes you may remember that I told you of them. But I did not say these things to you from the beginning, because I was with you.
16.5: " But now I am going to Him Who sent Me; and none of you asks Me, 'Where are You going? '
16.6: " But because I have said these things to you, grief has filled your heart.
16.7: " But I tell you the truth: it is profitable that I go away; for if I do not go away, the Helper will not come to you; but if I go, I will send Him to you.
16.8: " And having come, He will convict the world concerning sin, and concerning righteousness, and concerning judgment;
16.9: " concerning sin indeed; because they do not believe in Me;
16.10: " and concerning righteousness, because I go to the Father, and you no longer behold Me;
16.11: " and concerning judgment, because the ruler of this world has been judged.
16.12: " I have yet many things to say to you, but you do not have the power to bear I themnow.
16.13: " But when He, the Spirit of truth, comes, He will guide you into all the truth; for He will not speak of Himself, but whatever He hears He will speak; and He will declare to you the things that are to come.
16.14: " He will glorify Me, because He will receive of Mine and will declare I itto you.
16.15: " All things that the Father has are Mine; because of this I said that He receives of Mine, and will declare I itto you.
16.16: " A little while, and you will behold Me no more; and again a little while, and you will see Me. "
16.17: Then His disciples said to one another, " What is this that He says to us, 'A little while, and you will not behold Me; and again a little while, and you will see Me'; and, 'because I go to the Father'? "
16.18: They then said, " What is this that He says, 'A little while'? We do not know what He is talking I about. "
16.19: Yeshua knew that they wished to ask Him, and He said to them, " Concerning this do you seek with one another, because I said, 'A little while, and you will not behold Me, and again a little while, and you will see Me'?
16.20: " Truly, truly, I say to you, that you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice; you will be grieving, but your grief will become joy.
16.21: " When a woman brings forth she has grief, because her hour has come; but when she gives birth to the child, she remembers the tribulation no more, because of the joy that a man has been born into the world.
16.22: " Therefore you also have grief; but I will see you again and your heart will rejoice, and no one takes, by violence, your joy away from you.
16.23: " And in that day you will ask Me nothing. Truly, truly, I say to you, if you ask anything of the Father, He will give it to you in My name.
16.24: " Until just now you have asked nothing in My name; ask, and you will receive, that your joy may be fulfilled.
16.25: " These things I have spoken to you in allegories; an hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you in allegories but will tell you plainly of the Father.
16.26: " In that day you will ask in My name; and I do not say to you that I will ask to the Father concerning you;
16.27: " for the Father Himself loves you, because you have loved Me, and believed that I came out from God.
16.28: " I came out from the Father and have come into the world; I am leaving the world again and go to the Father. "
16.29: His disciples said, " Behold, now you are speaking plainly, not speaking any allegory.
16.30: " Now we know that You know all things, and have no need that anyone question You; by this we believe that you came out from God. "
16.31: Yeshua answered them, " Do you now believe?
16.32: " Behold, an hour is coming, and has come, in order for you to be scattered, each one to his own things, and you will leave Me alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with Me.
16.33: " These things I have spoken to you, that in Me you may have peace. In the world you have tribulation, but take courage, I have overcome the world. "

17.1: These things Yeshua spoke, and lifting up His eyes to Heaven, He said, " Father, the hour has come; glorify Your Son, that the Son may glorify You,
17.2: " accordingly as You have given Him authority over all flesh, that to all which You gave to Him, He may give eternal life.
17.3: " And this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Yeshua the Messiah Whom You have sent.
17.4: " I have glorified You on the Earth, having brought to the goal the work which You have given Me to do.
17.5: " And now, Father, glorify Me with Yourself, with the glory which I had with You before I the existenceof the world.
17.6: " I have manifested Your name to the men Whom You have given Me out of the world; Yours they were, and You have given them to Me, and they have kept Your word.
17.7: " Now they know that everything You have given Me is from You;
17.8: " for the spoken words which You have given Me I have given to them; and they received I them, and truly have known that I came out from You, and they believed that You have sent Me.
17.9: " I ask concerning them; I do not ask concerning the world, but concerning those whom You have given Me; for they are Yours;
17.10: " and all My things are Yours, and Yours I areMine; and I have been glorified in them.
17.11: " And no more am I in the world, but they are in the world, and I come to You. Holy Father, keep them in Your name which you have given Me, that they may be one, even as We I are one.
17.12: " While I was with them, I kept them in Your name which You have given Me; and I guarded them, and not one of them perished but the son of ruin, that the Scripture might be fulfilled.
17.13: " But now I come to You; and these things I speak in the world, so that they may have joy fulfilled in themselves.
17.14: " I have given them Your word; and the world has hated them because they are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.
17.15: " I do not ask You to take them out of the world, but to keep them out of the evil.
17.16: " They are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.
17.17: " Sanctify them in the truth; Your word is truth.
17.18: " As You have sent Me into the world, I also have sent them into the world.
17.19: " And on behalf of them I sanctify Myself, that they also themselves may be sanctified in truth.
17.20: " I do not ask concerning these alone, but also for those who believe in Me through their word;
17.21: " that they may all be one; just as You, Father, I arein Me, and I in You, that they also may be in Us; that the world may believe that You have sent Me.
17.22: " And the glory which You have given Me I have given to them; that they may be one, just as We are one;
17.23: " I in them and You in Me, that they may reach the goal as one, that the world may know that You have sent Me, and have loved them, even as You have loved Me.
17.24: " Father, I wish that they also, whom You have given Me, may be with Me where I am, in order that they may behold My glory which You have given Me; for You have loved Me before the foundation of the world.
17.25: " O righteous Father, although the world has not known You, yet I have known You; and these have known that You have sent Me;
17.26: " and I have made Your name known to them, and will make it known; that the love with which You have loved Me may be in them, and I in them. "

18.1: Having spoken these things, Yeshua went out with His disciples across the ravine of the Kidron, where there was a garden, into which He and His disciples entered.
18.2: Now Yehudah also, who was delivering Him up, knew the place; for Yeshua had often met there with His disciples.
18.3: Yehudah, therefore, having received the cohort and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees, came there with lanterns and torches and weapons.
