18.4: Yeshua therefore, knowing all the things that were coming upon Him, came out and said to them, " Whom do you seek? "
18.5: They answered Him, " Yeshua the Natzrati. " He said to them, " I AM. " And Yehudah also, who delivered Him up, was standing with them.
18.6: Then when He said to them, " I AM, " they drew back and fell to the ground.
18.7: Then He again asked them, " Whom do you seek? " And they said, " Yeshua the Natzrati. "
18.8: Yeshua answered, " I told you that I AM; if therefore you seek Me, allow these to depart, "
18.9: that the word might be fulfilled which He spoke, " Of those of whom You have given to Me, I lost not one. "
18.10: Then Shimon Petros, having a sword, drew it and struck the high priest’s slave and cut off his right ear; and the slave’s name was Melekh.
18.11: Yeshua therefore said to Petros, " Put the sword into the sheath. Shall I not drink the cup which the Father has given to Me? "
18.12: So the cohort and the chief captain and the officers of the Yehudim arrested Yeshua and bound Him,
18.13: and led Him to Anan first; for he was father - in - law of Kayafa, who was high priest that year.
18.14: Now Kayafa was he who had given counsel to the Yehudim that it was profitable that one man should die on behalf of the people.
18.15: And Shimon Petros followed Yeshua, and another disciple. Now that disciple was known to the high priest, and entered together with Yeshua into the courtyard of the high priest,
18.16: but Petros was standing at the door outside. So the other disciple, who was known to the high priest, went out and spoke to the doorkeeper, and brought in Petros.
18.17: Then the maidservant, the doorkeeper, said to Petros, " Are you not also I oneof this man’s disciples? " He said, " I am not. "
18.18: Now the slaves and the officers were standing I there, having made a charcoal fire because it was cold, and were warming themselves; Petros also was with them, standing and warming himself.
18.19: The high priest then questioned Yeshua concerning His disciples and concerning His teaching.
18.20: Yeshua answered him, " I have spoken openly to the world; I have always taught in the synagogues and in the Temple, where all the Yehudim come together, and I spoke nothing in secret.
18.21: " Why do you question Me? Question those who have heard what I spoke to them; behold, these know what I said. "
18.22: But having said these things, one of the officers standing by gave Yeshua a slap, saying, " Is that the way You answer the high priest? "
18.23: Yeshua answered him, " If I have spoken evil, bear witness of the evil; but if well, why do you beat Me? "
18.24: Anan then sent Him bound to Kayafa the high priest.
18.25: Now Shimon Petros was standing and warming himself. Then they said to him, " Are you not also I oneof His disciples? " He denied I itand said, " I am not. "
18.26: One of the slaves of the high priest, being a relative of the one whose ear Petros cut off, said, " Did I not see you in the garden with Him? "
18.27: Petros then denied I itagain; and immediately a rooster crowed.
18.28: They then led Yeshua from Kayafa into the Praetorium, and it was early; and they themselves did not enter into the Praetorium, in order that they might not be defiled, but might eat the Pesach.
18.29: Pilatos then went out to them and said, " What accusation do you bring against this Man? "
18.30: They answered and said to Him, " If He were not evil, we would not have handed Him over to you. "
18.31: Pilatos therefore said to them, " Take Him yourselves, and judge Him according to your I religiousLaw. " The Yehudim said to him, " We are not permitted to put anyone to death, "
18.32: that the word of Yeshua might be fulfilled, which He spoke, signifying by what kind of death He was about to die.

10.1: And a certain man, named Kornelios, was in Caesarea, a centurion of what was called the Italian Regiment,

10.20: " But arise, go down and go with them, not discriminating; for I have sent them Myself. "

10.23: Having called them in, therefore, he received them as guests. And on the next day he arose and went out with them, and some of the brethren from Yafo went together with them.
10.24: And on the next day they entered into Caesarea. Now Kornelios was waiting for them, and had called together his relatives and near friends.
10.25: And when it came that Petros entered, Kornelios met him and fell at his feet and bowed before I him.
10.26: But Petros raised him up, saying, " Stand up. I I alsomyself am I justa man. "
10.27: And he talked with him, he entered, and found I thatmany people had gathered together.
10.28: And he said to them, " You yourselves know how abominable it is for a man who is a Yehudi to associate with a foreigner or to visit him; but God has shown me that I should not call any man common or unclean.
10.29: " For this reason I came without raising any objection when I was sent for. And so I ask for what word you have sent for me. "
10.30: And Kornelios declared, " Four days ago to this hour, I was praying in my house at the ninth hour; and behold, a man stood before me in bright clothing,
10.31: " and he said, 'Kornelios, your prayer has been heard and your alms have been remembered before God.
10.32: " 'Send therefore to Yafo and call for Shimon, who is called Petros; he is lodging at the house of Shimon I thetanner by the sea. '
10.33: " At once, therefore, I sent for you, and you have been kind to arrive. Now then, we are all present before God to hear all that you have been commanded by the Lord. "
10.34: And opening his mouth, Petros said: " I most truly comprehend I nowthat God is not an accepter of a face,
10.35: " but in every nation the man who fears Him and does what is righteous, is acceptable to Him.

10.44: While Petros was still speaking these spoken words, the Holy Spirit fell upon all those who were hearing the word.

15.5: But certain ones of the faction of the Pharisees who had believed rose up, saying, " It is necessary to circumcise them, and to direct them to observe the Torah of Moshe. "

15.7: And after there had been much questioning I and debate, Petros rose and said to them, " Brethren, you know that in ancient times God made a choice among you, that by mouth the nations should hear the word of the good news and believe.
15.8: " And God, Who knows the heart, bore witness to them, giving them the Holy Spirit, just as He also did to us;
15.9: " and He made no difference between us and them, cleansing their hearts by faith.

15.12: And all the number I of themkept silent, and they were listening to Bar - Nabba and Paulos as they were explaining what signs and wonders God had done through them among the nations.

15.16: " 'AFTER THESE THINGS I WILL TURN BACK, AND I WILL BUILD AGAIN THE TABERNACLE OF DAVEED, WHICH HAS FALLEN, AND I WILL BUILD AGAIN ITS RUINS, AND I WILL SET IT UPRIGHT,
15.17: " 'SO THAT THE REST OF MANKIND MAY SEEK ADONAI, AND ALL THE NATIONS WHO ARE CALLED BY MY NAME,
15.18: " 'SAYS ADONAI, WHO MAKES THESE THINGS KNOWN FROM ANCIENT TIMES. '
15.19: " Therefore it is my judgment that we do not trouble those who are returning to God from among the nations,

15.22: Then it seemed I goodto the apostles and the elders, with the whole assembly, to choose men from among them to send to Antiocheia with Paulos and Bar - Nabba - - Yehudah called Bar - Sabba, and Sila, men who were leaders among the brethren,
15.23: writing by their hand these things: " The apostles and the elders and brethren, to those in Antiocheia and Suria and Kikilia who are out of the nations, greetings.

15.30: So when they were sent off, they went down to Antiocheia; and having gathered the great number together, they delivered the letter.

15.34: I But it seemed good to Sila to stay on there.

16.20: and having brought them to the magistrates, they said, " These men are throwing our city into confusion, being Yehudim,
16.21: " and are proclaiming ethics which it is not permitted for us to receive or to do, being Romans. "
16.22: And the crowd rose up together against them, and the magistrates tore their garments off them, and gave orders to beat them with rods.
16.23: And when they had laid many blows upon them, they threw them into prison, charging the jailer to guard them safely.
16.24: Having received this charge, he cast them into the inner prison, and fastened their feet in the stocks.
16.25: But about midnight Paulos and Sila were praying and singing hymns of praise to God, and the prisoners were listening to them;
16.26: and suddenly a great earthquake came, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken; and immediately all the doors were opened and everyone’s bounds were unfastened.
16.27: And when the jailer had been roused out of sleep and had seen the prison doors opened, he drew his sword and was about to kill himself, supposing that the prisoners had escaped.
16.28: But Paulos called out with a great voice, saying, " Do yourself no harm, for we are all here! "

16.30: and having brought them out, he said, " Lords, what must I do to be saved? "

16.32: And they spoke the word of the Lord to him with all who were in his house.
16.33: And he took them alongside in that hour and washed their wounds, and immediately he was immersed, he and all his I house.
16.34: And he brought them into his house, setting a table before I them, and rejoiced greatly, having believed in God with his whole house.
16.35: Now when the day came, the magistrates sent their rod - bearers, saying, " Release those men. "
16.36: And the jailer reported these words to Paulos, " The magistrates have sent to release you. Now therefore come out and go in peace. "

16.38: And the rod - bearers reported these spoken words to the magistrates. And they were afraid when they heard that they were Roman I citizens,
16.39: and they came and appealed to them, and when they had led them out, they asked them to leave the city.
16.40: And they came out of the prison and entered into I the house ofLudia, and having seen the brethren, they encouraged them and went out.

19.1: And it came to pass, in Apollos’ being in Korinthos, Paulos passed through the upper parts, I andcame to Ephesos, and found some disciples.

19.23: And about that season there was no small disturbance concerning the Way.
19.24: For a certain one named Demetrios, a silversmith, who made silver shrines of Artemis, was bringing no little business to the craftsmen;
19.25: these he gathered together with the workmen of similar I trades, and said, " Men, you know that our prosperity exists from this trade.
19.26: " And you see and hear that not only in Ephesos, but in almost all Asia, this Paulos has persuaded and perverted a considerable company of people saying that those made by hands are not gods.
19.27: " And there is danger not only that this trade of ours may come into disrepute, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis be regarded for nothing, and also her magnificence is about to be brought down, whom all Asia and the world worship. "
19.28: And when they heard I thisthey were full of anger, and were crying out, saying, " Great is Artemis of the Ephesians! "
19.29: And the city was filled with the confusion, and they rushed with one accord into the theater, dragging along Gaios and Aristarchos, Makedonians, Paulos’ traveling companions.
19.30: And when Paulos wanted to enter into the populace, the disciples would not let him.

19.37: " For you have brought these men I herewho are neither temple robbers nor blasphemers of our goddess.

19.39: " But if you inquire for anything beyond this, it will be settled in a lawful assembly.

20.10: But Paulos went down and fell upon him, and after embracing him, he said, " Do not be alarmed, for his soul in is him. "
20.11: And when he had gone up and had broken the bread and eaten, he conversed with them sufficiently until daybreak, I andthus went out.
20.12: And they brought the boy alive, and were comforted not a little.
20.13: But we, going ahead to the ship, set sail for Assos, there being about to take up Paulos; for thus he had arranged it, intending himself to travel by foot.
20.14: And when he met us at Assos, we took him up and came to Mituleinei.
20.15: And sailing from there we arrived the opposite day at Chios; and the next day we crossed over to Samos; and the following day we came to Mileitos.
20.16: For Paulos had to sail past Ephesos so that he may not have to spend time in Asia; for he was hastening to be in Yerushalayim, if possible, on the day of Shavuot.
20.17: And in Mileitos he sent to Ephesos, calling for the elders of the assembly.
20.18: And when they came to him, he said to them, " You yourselves know from the first day that I set foot in Asia how I was with you all the time,
20.19: " serving the Lord with all humility and with tears and with trials which befell me through the plots of the Yehudim;
20.20: " how I did not keep back from announcing to you anything that was profitable, and teaching you publicly and in every house,
20.21: " solemnly testifying to both Yehudim and Greeks of repentance toward God and faith in our Lord Yeshua the Messiah.
20.22: " And now, behold, bound in spirit, I am going to Yerushalayim, not knowing what will befall me there,
20.23: " except that the Holy Spirit solemnly testifies to me in every city, saying that imprisonments and tribulations continue.
20.24: " But I make account of nothing, nor do I hold my life precious to myself, in order that I may bring my course to its goal, and the ministry which I received from the Lord Yeshua, to testify solemnly of the good news of the grace of God.
20.25: " And now, behold, I know that you all will see my face no more, among whom I went about proclaiming the Kingdom.
20.26: " Therefore I testify to you this day, that I am innocent of the blood of all.
20.27: " For I did not keep back from announcing to you the whole counsel of God.
20.28: " Take heed to yourselves and to all the flock, among which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to shepherd the assembly of God which He purchased with His own blood.
20.29: " I know that after my departure fierce wolves will come in among you, not sparing the flock;
20.30: " and from among your own selves will arise men, speaking perverse things, to draw away the disciples after them.
20.31: " Therefore be awake, remembering that for three years I did not cease night or day to admonish every one with tears.
20.32: " And now I commend you to God and to the word of His grace, which has the power to build up and give I youan inheritance among all those who are sanctified.
20.33: " I coveting no one’s gold or silver or clothing.
20.34: " You yourselves know that these hands ministered to my needs and to those who were with me.
20.35: " In all things I have shown you that by toiling in this way it is necessary to help the weak and remember the words of the Lord Yeshua, that He Himself said, 'It is more blessed to give, than to receive. ' "
20.36: And when he had said these things, he knelt down and prayed with them all.
20.37: And they were weeping sufficiently and embraced Paulos, and ardently kissed him,
20.38: sorrowing most of all over the word that he had spoken, that they should see his face no more. And they went with him to the ship.

21.1: And when it came about that we had parted from them and had set sail, we ran a straight course to Cos, and the next day to Rhodos, and from there to Patara;
21.2: and having found a ship crossing over to Phoeinikei, we went aboard and set sail.
21.3: And sighting Kupros, and leaving it on the left, we sailed to Suria and landed at Tzor; for there the ship was to unload its cargo.
21.4: And finding the disciples, we stayed there seven days; and they said to Paulos through the Spirit not to go up to Yerushalayim.
21.5: But when it was I time forus to complete our days I there, we came out and went out on our journey; and they all, with wives and children went with us as far as outside the city. And kneeling down on the shore and praying, we took our leave of one another.
21.6: Then we went on board the ship, and they turned back to their home.
21.7: And when we had finished the voyage from Tzor, we arrived at Ptolemais; and we greeted and stayed with them for one day.
21.8: And on the next day we departed and came to Caesarea; and entered into the house of Philippos the evangelist, who was one of the seven, we stayed with him.
21.9: Now this I manhad four virgin daughters, who prophesied.
21.10: And remaining I manymore days, a certain prophet named Agabos came down from Yehudah.
21.11: And coming to us, he took Paulos’ belt and bound his own feet and hands, and said, " This is what the Holy Spirit says: 'In this way the Yehudim in Yerushalayim will bind the man who owns this belt and deliver him up into the hands of the nations. ' "
21.12: And when we heard these things, we and the local residents were begging him not to go up to Yerushalayim.
21.13: Then Paulos answered, " What are you doing, weeping and breaking my heart? For I am ready not only to be bound, but even to die at Yerushalayim for the name of the Lord Yeshua. "
21.14: And he not being persuaded, we were silent, saying, " The will of the Lord be done. "
21.15: And after these days, having been equipped, we went up to Yerushalayim.
21.16: And also I someof the disciples from Caesarea came together with us, leading us to Mnason of Kupros, an early disciple with whom we were to lodge.
21.17: And when we had come to Yerushalayim, the brethren received us gladly.
21.18: And on the following day Paulos went in with us to Ya’akov, and all the elders were present.
21.19: And having greeted them, he related one by one the things that God had done among the nations through his ministry.
21.20: And when they heard it, they were glorifying God; and they said to him, " You see, brother, how many thousands there are among the Yehudim of those who have believed, and they are all zealous for the Torah;
21.21: " and they have been told by word of mouth about you, that you are teaching all the Yehudim who are among the nations apostasy from Moshe, telling them not to circumcise their children nor to walk according to the ethic.
21.22: " What then is it? They will certainly hear that you have come.
21.23: " This, therefore, do what we tell you: There are four men who have a vow on themselves;
21.24: " take them alongside and purify yourself together with them, and pay their expenses so that they may shave their heads; and all will know that there is nothing to the things which they have been instructed concerning you, but that you yourself also walk orderly, keeping the Torah.
21.25: " Now concerning those of the nations who have believed, we wrote, judging that they should abstain from what has been sacrificed to idols, and from blood, and from I meatsstrangled, and from fornication. "
21.26: The Paulos took the men alongside, and the next day he purified himself with them, entered into the Temple, giving notice of the completion of the days of purification, until the sacrifice was offered for each one of them.
21.27: And when the seven days were almost completed, the Yehudim from Asia, noticing him in the Temple, were stirring up all the crowd and laid hands on him,
21.28: crying out, " Men of Yisrael, come to our aid! This is the man who teaches all men everywhere against our people, and the Torah, and this place; and besides he has even introduced Greeks into the Temple, and has made common this holy place. "
21.29: For they had previously seen Trophimos the Ephesian in the city with him, and they supposed that Paulos had brought him into the Temple.
21.30: And the whole city was aroused, and the people ran together and took hold of Paulos; they dragged him out of the Temple, and immediately the doors were shut.
21.31: And as they were seeking to kill him, information came up to the chief captain of the I Romancohort that all Yerushalayim was in confusion.
21.32: At once he took alongside soldiers and centurions, and ran down to them; and when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paulos.
21.33: Then the chief captain drew near and took hold of him, and ordered him to be bound with two chains; and he was asking who he was and what he had done.
21.34: But others cried something else in the crowd, some another; and as he did not have the power to know the facts because of the riot, he ordered him to be brought into the barracks.
21.35: And when he came to the steps, it happened he was carried away by the soldiers because of the violence of the crowd;
21.36: for the plethora of the people followed, crying, " Away with him! "
21.37: As Paulos was about to be brought into the barracks, he said to the chief captain, " May I say something to you? " And he said, " Do you know Greek?
21.38: " Then you are not the Mitzri who before these days stirred up a revolt and led the four thousand men of the Assassins out into the wilderness? "
21.39: But Paulos said, " I am a Yehudi of Tarseus in Kikilia, a city of no insignificant city; and I beg you, permit me to speak to the people. "
21.40: And permitting him, standing on the stairs, Paulos motioned to the people with his hand; and when there was a great silence, he spoke to them in the Iviri dialect, saying,

22.1: " Brethren and fathers, listen to my defense which I now I offerto you. "
22.2: And when they heard that he addressed them in the Ivri dialect, they showed more stillness; and he said,
22.3: " I am a Yehudi, born in Tarseus of Kilikia, but brought up in this city, educated I as a childbeside Gamli’el, I withexactness according to the Torah of our fathers, being zealous for God, just as you all are today.
22.4: " I persecuted this Way to the death, binding and delivering up both men and women into prison,
22.5: " as the high priest and the council of elders can bear me witness. From them also I received letters to the brethren, I went to Dammesek to bring even those who were there to Yerushalayim bound in order to be punished.
22.6: " And it happened that as I was going, nearing Dammesek about noontime, suddenly out of heaven a great light flashed around me,
22.7: " and I fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, 'Shaul, Shaul, why do you persecute Me? '
22.8: " And I answered, 'Who are You, Lord? ' And He said to me, 'I am Yeshua the Natzrati Whom you are persecuting. '
22.9: " Now those who were with me indeed beheld the light, but did not give heed to the voice of the One Who was speaking to me.
22.10: " And I said, 'What shall I do, Lord? ' And the Lord said to me, 'Arise, and go on into Dammesek; and there you will be told all which is appointed for you to do. '
22.11: " And as I did not see because of the glory of that light, I was led by the hand by those who were with me, and came into Dammesek.
22.12: " And a certain Chananyah, a devout man according to the measure of the Torah, I welltestified of by all the Yehudim dwelling I there,
22.13: " came to me, and standing by me said to me, 'Brother Shaul, receive your sight! ' And at that same hour I recovered my sight.
22.14: " And he said, 'The God of our fathers has appointed you to know His will, and to see the Righteous One, and to hear a voice out of His mouth.
22.15: " 'For you will be a witness for Him to all men of what you have seen and heard.
22.16: " 'And what do you now intend? Arise and be immersed, and wash away your sins, calling on His name. '
22.17: " And it came about when I turned back toward Yerushalayim and was praying in the Temple, that I fell into a trance,
22.18: " and I saw Him saying to me, 'Make haste, and quickly get out of Yerushalayim, because they will not accept your testimony concerning Me. '
22.19: " And I said, 'Lord, they themselves understand that I was imprisoning and beating those believing in You throughout the synagogues.
22.20: " 'And when the blood of Your witness Stephanos was being poured out, I was standing by and joined in approving, and watching out for the garments of those putting him to death. '
22.21: " And He said to me, 'Go! Because I will send you to the nations afar off. ' "
22.22: And they heard him until this word; and they lifted up their voice, saying, " Take by violence from the Earth one such as this, for it is not fitting that he should live! "
22.23: And as they cried out and tore off their garments and cast dust into the air,
22.24: the chief captain ordered him to be brought into the barracks, saying that he should be examined by scourging, to find out for what reason they were shouting against him in that way.
22.25: And when they stretched him out with straps, Paulos said to the centurion who was standing by, " Is it permitted for you to scourge a man who is a Roman I citizenand uncondemned? "
22.26: Now when the centurion heard I this, he went to the chief captain, and reported to him, saying, " What are you about to do? For this man is a Roman I citizen. "
22.27: And the chief captain approached and said to him, " Tell me, are you a Roman I citizen? " And he said, " Yes. "
22.28: And the chief captain answered, " I bought this citizenship with a large sum of money. " But Paulos said, " But I was actually born I a citizen. "
22.29: Then immediately those who were about to examine him let go of him; and the chief captain also was afraid when he recognized that he was a Roman I citizen, and because he had bound him.
22.30: But on the next day, wanting to know for certain why he had been accused by the Yehudim, he released him and ordered the chief priests and all the Sanhedrin to come together, and brought Paulos down and set him before them.

23.1: And Paulos, looking intently at the Sanhedrin, said, " Brethren, I have lived as a citizen in all good conscience toward God to this day. "
23.2: And the high priest Chananyah commanded those standing beside him to strike him on the mouth.
23.3: Then Paulos said to him, " God is about to strike you, you whitewashed wall! And do you sit judging me according to the Torah, yet in transgression of the Torah order me to be struck? "
23.4: But those standing by said, " Do you revile the high priest of God? "
23.5: And Paulos said, " I did not know, brethren, that he was high priest; for it is written, 'YOU SHALL NOT SPEAK EVIL OF A RULER OF YOUR PEOPLE. ' "
23.6: But knowing that one part were Sadducees and the other Pharisees, Paulos cried out in the Sanhedrin, " Brethren, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees! I am on trial concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead! "
23.7: And having said this, there came a riot between the Pharisees and the Sadducees; and the number was divided.
23.8: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, nor an angel, nor a spirit; but the Pharisees confess them both.
23.9: And there arose a great outcry; and some of the scribes of the Pharisees’ party stood up and were contending, saying, " We find nothing wrong in this man. I Whatif a spirit or an angel has spoken to him? "
23.10: And a great riot having come, the chief captain was afraid that Paulos would be torn to pieces by them and ordered the soldiers to go down and snatch him away, and bring him into the barracks.
23.11: But on the following night, the Lord stood by him and said, " Take courage; for as you have solemnly testified the things concerning Me in Yerushalayim, so it is necessary for you to also testify at Rome. "
23.12: And when it was day, the Yehudim made a conspiracy and anathemized themselves, saying neither to eat nor to drink until they had killed Paulos.
23.13: And there were more than forty who made this conspiracy.
23.14: And they approached the chief priests and the elders, and said, " With an anathema we have anathemized ourselves to taste nothing until we have killed Paulos.
23.15: " Now, therefore, you and the Sanhedrin notify the chief captain to bring him down to you, as though you were going to determine the things concerning him with exactness. And before his drawing near, we are ready to kill him. "
23.16: But the son of Paulos’ sister heard of their ambush, and he arrived and entered into the barracks and told Paulos.
23.17: And Paulos called one of the centurions and said, " Lead this young man to the chief captain, for he has something to report to him. "
23.18: So he took him alongside and led him to the chief captain and said, " Paulos the prisoner called me and asked me to lead this young man to you, as he has something to say to you. "
23.19: And the chief captain took him by the hand, and drawing aside privately, inquired, " What is it that you have to report to me? "
23.20: And he said, " The Yehudim have agreed to ask you to bring Paulos down tomorrow to the Sanhedrin, as though they were about to inquire somewhat more exactly concerning him.
23.21: " Therefore, you I mustnot be persuaded by them, for more than forty of them are lying in wait for him, having anathemized themselves neither to eat nor drink until they have killed him; and now they are ready, waiting for the promise from you. "
23.22: The chief captain, then, indeed, dismissed the young man, charging him, " Tell no one that you have notified me of these things. "
23.23: And having called to him certain two of the centurions, he said, " Get two hundred soldiers ready by the third hour of the night to go to Caesarea, and seventy horsemen and two hundred spearmen;
23.24: " also provide mounts for Paulos to ride, and bring him safely to Phelix the governor. "
23.25: And he wrote a letter having this form:
23.26: " Claudius Lysias, to the most excellent governor Phelix, greetings.
23.27: " This man was seized by the Yehudim and was about to be killed by them. I came upon them with troops and rescued him, having learned that he was a Roman I citizen.
23.28: " And wanting to know the reason for which they were accusing him, I brought him down to their Sanhedrin.
23.29: " I found him to be accused concerning points of disagreement concerning their I religiousLaw, but having no accusation worthy of death or imprisonment.
23.30: " And when I was informed that there was a plot against this man, I sent him to you at once, ordering his accusers to say the things against him before you. I Farewell. "
23.31: Then indeed the soldiers, according to I whatthey had been directed, took up Paulos and brought him by night to Antipatris.
23.32: But the next day, leaving the horsemen to go on with him, they turned back to the barracks.
23.33: And when they had come to Caesarea and delivered the letter to the governor, they also presented Paulos to him.
23.34: And having read it, he inquired what province he was from. And when he learned that he was from Kikilia,
23.35: he said, " I will hear you when your accusers arrive "; and he commanded him to be guarded in Herodes’ Praetorium.

24.1: And after five days the high priest Chananyah came down with some elders, with a certain spokesman Tertullos; and they brought charges to the governor against Paulos.
24.2: And when he was called, Tertullos began to accuse him, saying, " Since we have obtained much peace through you, and since by your foresight reforms are occurring for this nation,
24.3: " in every way and everywhere we acknowledge I this, most excellent Phelix, with all thankfulness.
24.4: " But, in order that I not impede you any further, I beseech you to hear us, by our kindness, a brief hearing.
24.5: " For we have found this man a pestilence, and I one whostirs up an insurrection among all the Yehudim throughout the inhabited Earth, and ringleader of the sect of the Natzarim,
24.6: " who also attempted to profane the Temple, but we arrested him. I And we wanted to judge him according to our own religiousLaw.
24.7: I " But Lusias the chief captain came up, and with much violence led him away out of our hands,
24.8: " ordering his accusers to come before you. And by examining him yourself concerning all these things, you will have the power to know exactly the things of which we accuse him. "
24.9: And the Yehudim also joined in, affirming that these things were so.
24.10: And when the governor had nodded for him to speak, Paulos answered, " Realizing that for many years you have been a judge over this nation, I cheerfully make my defense.
24.11: " You have the power to know exactly that no more than twelve days ago I went up to Yerushalayim to worship.
24.12: " And neither in the Temple did they find me discussing with any one, nor making a gathering of a crowd, neither in synagogues, nor in the city.
24.13: " Nor do they have the power to prove to you what they now accuse me.
24.14: " But this I acknowledge to you, that according to the Way which they call a heresy, I do serve the God of our fathers, believing everything that is in accordance with the Torah, and that is written in the Prophets;
24.15: " having a hope in God which these themselves accept, that there is to be a resurrection of both the righteous and the unrighteous.
24.16: " And in this I do exercise myself, to always have a blameless conscious toward God and men.
24.17: " Now after many years I arrived to bring alms to my nation and to make offerings;
24.18: " in which they found me purified in the Temple, without I anycrowd or commotion. But certain Yehudim from Asia,
24.19: " whom it is necessary I for themto be present before you, and to make accusation, if they have anything against me.
24.20: " Or else let these same say what wrongdoing they found when I stood before the Sanhedrin,
24.21: " except concerning this one voice, which I cried out while standing among them, 'Concerning the resurrection of the dead I am on trial before you today. ' "
24.22: But Phelix, knowing more accurately about the Way, put them off, saying, " When Lusias the chief captain comes down, I will decide the things concerning you. "
24.23: And he ordered the centurion to watch over him, and to have ease, and not to prevent any of his own to minister to him.
24.24: But after certain days, Phelix arrived with his wife Drousilla, who was a Yehudit, and sent for Paulos, and heard him concerning his faith in Messiah Yeshua.
24.25: And as he was discussing concerning righteousness, self - control, and the judgment that is to be, Phelix was terrified and said, " Go away for the present, when I find I theright time, I will summon you. "
24.26: And at once, hoping that money would be given him by Paulos, for this reason he frequently sent for him and would converse with him.
24.27: But after two years were fulfilled, Phelix welcomed a successor, Porkios Phestos; and wishing to do the Yehudim a favor, Phelix left Paulos imprisoned.

25.1: Phestos therefore, having come into the province, three days later went up to Yerushalayim from Caesarea.
25.2: And the chief priests and the principal men of the Yehudim informed him against Paulos; and they urged him,
25.3: requesting a favor against Paulos, so as he might send for him to Yerushalayim, making a plot to kill him on the way.
25.4: Phestos them answered that Paulos was being guarded at Caesarea, and that he himself was about to go there shortly.
25.5: " Therefore, " he said, " let the powerful ones among you go with me, and if there is anything out of place in this man, let them accuse him. "
25.6: And having spent among them not more than eight or ten days, he went down to Caesarea; and on the next day he took his seat on the bema and ordered Paulos to be brought.
25.7: And after he had arrived, the Yehudim who had come down from Yerushalayim stood around him, bringing many heavy charges against Paulos, which they were not strong enough to prove.
25.8: Paulos said in his defense, " Neither against the Torah of the Yehudim, nor against the Temple, neither against Caesar have I sinned. "
25.9: But Phestos, wishing to do the Yehudim a favor, answered Paulos and said, " Are you willing to go up to Yerushalayim to be judged before me there concerning these things? "
25.10: But Paulos said, " I am standing before Caesar’s bema, where it is necessary for me to be judged. I have done unrighteousness I tothe Yehudim I innothing, as you also very well know.
25.11: " If indeed I am unrighteous, and have practiced anything worthy of death, I do not refuse to die; but if there is nothing of which they accuse me, no one has the power to give me up to them. I appeal to Caesar! "
25.12: Then Phestos, when he had conferred with his council, answered, " You have appealed to Caesar; to Caesar you shall go. "
25.13: Now when certain days had elapsed, Agrippa the king and Bernike arrived at Caesarea to welcome Phestos.
25.14: And as they stayed there many days, Phestos submitted the things to the king concerning Paulos, " There is a certain man left behind I asa prisoner by Phelix;
25.15: " concerning whom, when I was at Yerushalayim, the chief priests and elders of the Yehudim notified me, asking for a sentence against him.
25.16: " I answered to them that it is not the ethic of the Romans to give up any man before the accused meets his accusers face to face, and has had a place of defense concerning the accusations.
25.17: " Then when they had come together here, I made no delay, but at the next day sat down upon the bema and ordered the man to be led in,
25.18: " concerning whom the accusers, having stood up, were bringing forth charges concerning him of which evils I had not expected.
25.19: " But they had certain points of disagreement with him concerning their own superstition and concerning a certain Yeshua Who was dead, Whom Paulos affirmed to be alive.
25.20: " And being perplexed how to investigate these things, I asked whether he would wish to go to Yerushalayim and there be judged concerning these things.
25.21: " But when Paulos appealed to be kept in custody for the decision of the Emperor, I ordered him to be kept in custody until I could send him to Caesar. "
25.22: And Agrippa I saidto Phestos, " I also wish to hear the man myself. " And he said, " Tomorrow you will hear him. "
25.23: Therefore on the next day Agrippa and Bernike coming with much pomp, and entering into the auditorium, together with the chief captains and the prominent men of the city, at the order of Phestos, Paulos was brought in.
25.24: And Phestos said, " King Agrippa, and all men who are present together with us, you behold this man concerning whom all the plethora of the people of the Yehudim petitioned me, both at Yerushalayim and here, shouting that he ought not to live any more.
25.25: " But I found that he had practiced nothing worthy of death; and as he himself has appealed to the Emperor, I have decided to send him,
25.26: " concerning whom I have nothing definite to write to my lord. Therefore I have brought him before you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that after the examination has occurred, I may have something to write.
25.27: " For it seems unreasonable, in sending a prisoner, not also to signify the charges against him.

26.1: And Agrippa said to Paulos, " You are entrusted to speak concerning yourself. " Then Paulos extended his hand and made his defense:
26.2: " Concerning all of which I am accused of by Yehudim, King Agrippa, I consider myself blessed, being about to make a defense before you today;
26.3: " because you are especially an expert in all ethics and controversies among Yehudim; on which account I entreat you to listen to me patiently.
26.4: " Indeed, then, all Yehudim know my manner of life from my youth, which from the beginning had been in my nation in Yerushalayim;
26.5: " who before knew me from the first, if they are willing to testify, that according to the strictest sect of our religion, I lived I asa Pharisee.
26.6: " And now I stand here I injudgment for the hope of the promise made by God to our fathers;
26.7: " to which our twelve tribes hope to attain, as they earnestly serve night and day. And for this hope, O King, I am accused by Yehudim.
26.8: " Why is it judged unbelievable by you if God raises the dead?
26.9: " I, indeed, then thought to myself that it was necessary for me to do many things opposing the name of Yeshua of Natzeret,
26.10: " which I also did in Yerushalayim; I not only shut up many of the saints in prisons, having received authority from the chief priests; and being put to death, I cast my stone against them.
26.11: " And I punished them often in all the synagogues, I compelled them to blaspheme; and being abundantly enraged against them, I kept persecuting them as far as foreign cities.
26.12: " In which things, going to Dammesek, with the authority and decision power of the chief priests,
26.13: " at midday, O King, I saw on the road a light from Heaven, brighter than the sun, shining around me and those who were going with me.
26.14: " And when we had fallen to the ground, I heard a voice saying to me in the Ivri dialect, 'Shaul, Shaul, why are you persecuting Me? It is difficult for you to kick against the prods. '
26.15: " And I said, 'Who are You, Lord? ' And the Lord said, 'I am Yeshua Whom You are persecuting.
26.16: " 'But arise and stand upon your feet; for this I have appeared for you, to appoint you an officer and a witness both of the things which you have seen and of the things I whichI will appear to you;
26.17: " 'delivering you out of the people, and the nations - - to whom I am sending you,
26.18: " 'to open their eyes that they may return from darkness to light and from the authority of HaSatan to God, in order that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an allotment among those who have been sanctified by faith in Me. '
26.19: " Wherefore, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the Heavenly vision,
26.20: " but to those first in Dammesek, and Yerushalayim, and throughout all the country of Yehudah, and to the nations, I announced that they should repent and return to God, practicing works worthy of repentance.
26.21: " Because of these things the Yehudim seized me in the Temple and were endeavoring to kill me.
26.22: " Having obtained, therefore, help from God to this day testifying to both small and great, saying nothing but what the Prophets and Moshe said was going to occur;
26.23: " that the Messiah was to suffer, and by I Hisresurrection from the dead He should be the first to proclaim light both to the people and to the nations. "
26.24: And while he thus made his defense, Phestos said in a great voice, " You are insane, Paulos! I Toomuch learning has turned you mad! "
26.25: But Paulos said, " I am not insane, most excellent Phestos, but I utter spoken words of sane truth.
26.26: " For the king knows concerning these things, and to him I speak with confidence; for I am persuaded that none of these things escape his notice, for this has not been done in a corner.
26.27: " King Agrippa, do you believe the Prophets? I know that you do. "
26.28: And Agrippa I saidto Paulos, " In a short time you think to make me a Christian! "
26.29: And Paulos I said, " I would pray to God, both in a little and in much, not only you, but also all who hear me today, might become such as I am - - except for these chains. "
26.30: And the king arose and the governor and Bernike and those who were sitting with them,
26.31: and when they had withdrawn, they were talking to one another, saying, " This man practices nothing worthy of death or imprisonment. "
26.32: And Agrippa said to Phestos, " This man had the power to have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar. "

27.1: And when it was judged for us to sail to Italia, they delivered Paulos and certain other prisoners to a centurion name Ioulios, of the cohort of the Emperor.
27.2: And embarking in a ship of Adramutteinos, which was about to sail to the places along the coast of Asia, we put to sea, accompanied by Aristarchos, a Makedonian of Thessalonikei.
27.3: The next day we put in at Tzidon; and Ioulios treated Paulos kindly and entrusted him to go to his friends and receive care.
27.4: And from there we put to sea and sailed under the shelter of Kupros because the winds were against us.
27.5: And when we had sailed across the sea along the coast of Kikilia and Pamphulia, we came to Mura in Lukia.
27.6: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing for Italia, and put us into it.
27.7: And having sailed for sufficient days, and with difficulty had come to Knidos, as the wind did not allow us I to gofurther, we sailed under the shelter of Kreitei, off Salmonei;

1.15: and His feet I werelike burnished bronze, as having been fired in a furnace, and His voice I waslike the sound of many waters.

1.17: And when I saw Him, I fell at His feet as I thoughdead. And He placed His right hand upon me, saying, " Do not be afraid, I am the First and the Last,
1.18: " and the Living One; and I was dead, and behold, I am alive forevermore, and I have the keys of Death and Sheol.
1.19: " Write therefore the things that you have seen, and the things that are, and the things that are to occur after these things.

2.1: " To the angel of the assembly in Ephesos write: The One Who holds the seven stars in His right hand, the One Who walks in the middle of the seven golden menorahs, says this:
2.2: " 'I know your works and toil and perseverance, and that you cannot bear evil men, and you test those who call themselves apostles, and they are not, and you found them false;
2.3: " 'and you have perseverance and have endured for My name’s sake, and have not grown weary.
2.4: " 'But I have I thisagainst you, that you have left your first love.
2.5: " 'Remember then from whence you have fallen, and repent, and do the first works. But if not I am coming to you and will remove your menorah out of its place, unless you repent.
2.6: " 'Yet this you have, you hate the works of the Nicolaitans, that I also hate.
2.7: " 'He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies. To him who overcomes, I will grant to eat of the tree of life, which is in the Paradise of God.
2.8: " 'And to the angel of the assembly of Smurna write: The First and the Last, Who was dead, and has come to life, says this:
2.9: " 'I know your tribulation and your poverty - - but you are rich, and the blasphemy by those who say they are Yehudim and are not, but are a synagogue of HaSatan.
2.10: " 'Do not fear what you are about to suffer. Behold, the Devil is about to cast some of you into prison, that you may be tested, and you will have tribulation ten days. Be faithful unto death, and I will give you the crown of life.
2.11: " 'He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies. He who overcomes shall not be hurt by the second death. '
2.12: " 'And to the angel of the assembly in Pergamos write: The One Who has the sharp two - edged sword says this:
2.13: " 'I know where you dwell, where HaSatan’s throne is; and you hold fast My name, and did not deny My faith, even in the days of Antipas, My witness, My faithful, who was killed among you where HaSatan dwells.
2.14: " 'But I have a few things against you, because you have there some who hold to the teaching of Bil’am, who kept teaching Balak to put a stumbling block before the sons of Yisrael, to eat things sacrificed to idols, and to commit fornication.
2.15: " 'In this way you also have some who likewise hold the teaching of the Nicolaitans.
2.16: " 'Repent then. If not, I am coming to you quickly, and I will make war against them with the sword of My mouth.
2.17: " 'He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies. To him who overcomes, to him I will give of the hidden manna, and I will give him a white stone, and a renewed name written on the stone which no one knows but he who takes it. '
2.18: " And to the angel of the assembly in Thuateira write: The Son of God, Who has eyes like a flame of fire, and Whose feet are like burnished bronze, says this:
2.19: " 'I know your works, and your love and faith and service and perseverance, and that your works of late are greater than at first.
2.20: " 'But I have I thisagainst you, that you leave that woman Izevel alone, who is calling herself a prophetess, and she teaches and leads My slaves astray, so that they commit fornication and eat I meatsacrificed to idols.
2.21: " 'And I gave her time to repent; but she refuses to repent of her fornication.
2.22: " 'Behold, I will cast her upon a bed I ofsickness, and those who commit adultery with her into great tribulation, unless they repent of her works.
2.23: " 'And I will kill her children in death; and all the assemblies will know that I am He Who is searching the minds and hearts; and I will give to each one of you according to your works.
2.24: " 'But I say to you, the rest who are in Thuateira, who do not hold this teaching, who have not known the deep things of HaSatan, as they call them - - I place no other burden on you.
2.25: " 'Nevertheless what you have, hold strong until I come.
2.26: " 'And he who overcomes, and he who keeps My works until the end, TO HIM I WILL GIVE AUTHORITY OVER THE NATIONS;
2.27: " 'AND HE SHALL RULE THEM WITH A ROD OF IRON, AS THE VESSELS OF THE POTTER ARE BROKEN TO PIECES, as I also have received from My Father;
2.28: " 'and I will give to him the morning star.
2.29: " 'He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies.

3.1: " 'And to the angel of the assembly in Sardeis write: He who has the seven Spirits of God, and the seven stars, says this: I know your works, that you have the name of being alive, but you are dead.
3.2: " 'Wake up, and strengthen the things that remain, which were about to die; for I have not found your works fulfilled in the sight of My God.
3.3: " 'Remember therefore what you have received and heard; and watch over I it, and repent. If therefore you will not wake up, I will come like a thief, and you will not know at what hour I come upon you.
3.4: " 'But you have a few names in Sardeis who have not defiled their garments; and they will walk with Me in white; for they are worthy.
3.5: " 'He who overcomes shall thus be clothed in white garments; and I will not erase his name from the scroll of life, and I will confess his name before My Father, and before His angels.
3.6: " 'He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies.
3.7: " 'And to the angel in the assembly in Philadelpheia write: He Who is holy, Who is true, Who has the key of Daveed, Who opens and no one will shut, and Who shuts and no one opens, says this:
3.8: " 'I know your works. Behold, I have put before you an open door which no one is able to shut, because you have a little power, and have kept My word, and have not denied My name.
3.9: " 'Behold, I will make I thoseof the synagogue of HaSatan, who say they are Yehudim and are not, but lie - - behold, I will make them come and bow down at your feet, and to know that I have loved you.
3.10: " 'Because you have kept the word of My perseverance, I will keep you out of the hour of testing that is about to come upon the whole world, to test those who dwell upon the Earth.
3.11: " 'I am coming quickly; hold strong what you have, in order that no one take your crown.
3.12: " 'He who overcomes, I will make you a pillar in the Temple of My God; and never shall he go out of it; and I will write upon him the name of My God, and the name of the city of My God, the renewed Yerushalayim, which comes down out of Heaven from My God, and My renewed name.
3.13: " 'He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies.
3.14: " 'And to the angel of the assembly in Laodikeia write: The Amein, the faithful and true Witness, the Beginning of the Creation of God, says this:
3.15: " 'I know your works, that you are neither cold nor hot; I would I preferthat you were cold or hot.
3.16: " 'So because you are lukewarm, and neither hot nor cold, I will vomit you out of My mouth.
3.17: " 'Because you say, " I am rich, and have become wealthy, and have need of nothing, " and you do not know that you are wretched and pitiable and poor and blind and naked,
3.18: " 'I counsel you to buy from me gold refined by fire, that you may become rich, and white garments, that you may clothe yourself, and I thatthe shame of your nakedness may not be made clear; and eye salve to anoint your eyes that you may see.
3.19: " 'Those whom I love, I reprove and instruct; be zealous, therefore, and repent.
3.20: " 'Behold, I stand at the door and knock; if anyone hears My voice and opens the door, I will enter into him and I will dine with him, and he with Me.
3.21: " 'He who overcomes, I will grant to him to sit down with Me on My throne, as I also overcame and sat down with My Father on His throne.
3.22: " 'He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies. ' "

4.1: After these things I saw, and behold, a door opened in Heaven, and the first voice which I had heard, as if of a trumpet speaking with me, said, " Come up here, and I will show you what must occur after these things. "

4.4: And around the throne I weretwenty four thrones; and upon the thrones were twenty - four elders seated, clothed in white garments, and golden crowns on their heads.

4.11: " Worthy are You, O Lord our God, to receive glory and honor and power; for You created all things, and by Your will they existed and were created. "

5.1: And I saw upon the right hand of Him Who was seated on the throne a scroll written within and on the back, sealed up with seven seals.
5.2: And I saw a strong angel proclaiming in a great voice, " Who is worthy to open the scroll and break its seals? "

5.7: And He came and took I the scrollout of the right hand of Him Who sat on the throne.

5.11: And I looked and I heard the voice of many angels round about the throne and the living creatures and the elders, and the number of them was myriad of myriads, and thousands of thousands,
5.12: saying with a great voice, " Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power and riches and wisdom and strength and honor and glory and blessing. "
5.13: And every created thing which is in Heaven and on the Earth and under the Earth and in the sea, and all things in them, I heard saying, " To Him Who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb, I beblessing and honor and glory and dominion forever and ever. "
5.14: And the four living creatures said, " Amein! " And the elders fell down and worshipped.

6.1: And I saw when the Lamb opened one of the seven seals, and I heard one of the four living creatures saying, as it were, with a voice of thunder, " Come. "

6.4: And there went out another horse, fiery red; and it was given to him who was seated on it to take peace from the Earth, and that they should slaughter one another; and a great sword was given to him.
6.5: And when He opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature saying, " Come. " And I saw, and behold, a black horse; and he who was seated on it had a balance in his hands.
6.6: And I heard, as it were, a voice in the middle of the four living creatures saying, " A choenix of wheat for a denarius, and three choenixes of barley for a denarius; and do not harm the oil and the wine. "

6.10: and they cried out with a great voice, saying, " How long, O Master, holy and true, will You not judge and avenge our blood on those who inhabit the Earth? "
6.11: And there was given to each one a white robe; and it was said to them that they should rest yet a little time, until I the number oftheir fellow slaves and their brethren should be fulfilled, who were to be killed even as they had been.
6.12: And I looked when He opened the sixth seal, and there was a great earthquake; and the sun became as sackcloth I madeof I goathair, and the full moon became as blood;
6.13: and the stars of the sky fell to the Earth, as a fig tree casts its unripe figs when shaken by a great wind.

6.16: and they said to the mountains and to the rocks, " Fall on us and hide us from the face of Him Who sits on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb;
6.17: " for the great day of Their wrath has come; and who has the power to make a stand? "

7.1: After these things I saw four angels standing upon the four corners of the Earth, holding the four winds of the Earth, that the wind should not blow on the Earth, nor upon the sea, nor upon any tree.
7.2: And I saw another angel ascending from the rising of the sun, having the seal of the Living God; and he cried out with a great voice to the four angels to whom it was given to them to harm the Earth and the sea,
7.3: saying, " Do not harm the Earth or the sea or the trees, until we seal the slaves of our God upon their foreheads. "
7.4: And I heard the number of those who were sealed, one hundred and forty - four thousand from every tribe of the sons of Yisrael:
7.5: from the tribe of Yehudah, twelve thousand were sealed, from the tribe of Reuven twelve thousand, from the tribe of Gad twelve thousand,
7.6: from the tribe of Asher twelve thousand, from the tribe of Naftali twelve thousand, from the tribe of Menashe twelve thousand,
7.7: from the tribe of Shimon twelve thousand, from the tribe of Levee twelve thousand, from the tribe of Yisakhar twelve thousand,

7.10: and crying out with a great voice, saying, " Salvation to our God Who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb! "
7.11: And all the angels were standing around the throne and the elders and the four living creatures; and they fell on their faces before the throne and worshipped God,
7.12: saying, " Amein! Blessing and glory and wisdom and thanksgiving and honor and power and might I beto our God forever and ever! Amein! "
7.13: And one of the elders answered, saying to me, " These who are clothed in the white robes, who are they, and from where have they come? "
7.14: And I said to him, " My lord, you know. " And he said to me, " These are the ones who are coming out of the great tribulation, and they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.
7.15: " Because of this they are before the throne of God; and they serve Him day and night in His Temple; and He Who is seated upon the throne shall tabernacle over them.
7.16: " They will not hunger still, nor thirst still, nor shall the sun fall down upon them, nor any heat;
7.17: " for the Lamb in the middle of the throne will be their Shepherd, and shall lead them to living springs of waters; and God shall wipe away every tear from their eyes. "

8.1: And when he opened the seventh seal, there was silence in Heaven for about half an hour.
8.2: And I saw the seven angels who stand before God; and seven trumpets were given to them.
8.3: And another angel came and stood at the altar, having a golden censer; and much incense was given to him, that he might give it to the prayers of all the saints upon the golden altar before the throne.
8.4: And the smoke of the incense went up with the prayers of the saints out of the hand of the angel before God.
8.5: And the angel took the censer and filled it with fire out of the altar and cast it to the Earth; and there occurred thunders and voices and lightnings and an earthquake.
8.6: And the seven angels who had the seven trumpets prepared themselves to trumpet.
8.7: And the first trumpeted, and hail and fire mixed with blood occurred, and they were cast to the Earth; and a third of the Earth was burned up, and all the green grass was burned up.
8.8: And the second angel trumpeted, and I somethinglike a great mountain burning with fire was cast into the sea; and a third of the sea became blood.
8.9: and a third of the creatures having souls died in the sea; and a third of the ships were destroyed.
8.10: And the third angel trumpeted, and a great star fell from Heaven, blazing like a torch, and it fell upon a third of the rivers and upon the springs of waters;
8.11: and the name of the star is called Wormwood; and a third of the waters became wormwood. And many men died from the waters, because they were embittered.
8.12: And the fourth angel trumpeted, and a third of the sun was struck, and a third of the moon, and a third of the stars, so that a third of them might be darkened; and the day might not shine for a third of it, and the night in like manner.
8.13: And I saw, and I heard an eagle flying in midheaven, saying with a great voice, " Woe, woe, woe, to those dwelling upon the Earth, because of the remaining sounds of the trumpet of the three angels who are about to trumpet. "

9.2: And he opened the pit of the abyss; and smoke ascended out of the pit, like the smoke of a great furnace; and the sun and the air were darkened by the smoke of the pit.
9.3: And out of the smoke came forth locusts upon the Earth; and authority was given to them, as scorpions of the Earth have authority.
9.4: And they were told that they should not hurt the grass of the Earth, nor any green thing, nor any tree, but only the men who do not have the seal of God upon their foreheads.
9.5: And they were not allowed to kill anyone, but to torment for five months; and their torment was like the torment of a scorpion when it stings a man.
9.6: And in those days men will seek death and will not find it; and they will long to die, but death will flee from them.
9.7: And the likenesses of the locusts I werelike horses prepared for battle; and on their heads, as it were, crowns resembling gold, and their faces were like the faces of men.
9.8: And they had hair like the hair of women, and their teeth were like I thoseof lions.
9.9: And they had breastplates like breastplates of iron; and the noise of their wings was like the noise of chariots, of many horses running to battle.
9.10: And they have tails like scorpions, and stings were in their tails; and their authority I isto harm men for five months.
9.11: They have as king over them the angel of the abyss; his name in Ivri is Avadon, and in Greek he has the name Apolluon.
9.12: The first woe has departed; behold, after these things come two woes.
9.13: And the sixth angel trumpeted, and I heard a voice from the four horns of the golden altar which is before God,
9.14: saying to the sixth angel who had the trumpet, " Release the four angels who are bound at the great river Euphrates. "
9.15: And the four angels were released, who had been prepared for the hour and day and month and year, in order that they might kill a third of mankind.
9.16: And the number of the armies of the cavalry was two hundred million; I heard the number of them.
9.17: And thus I saw the horses in the vision, and those sitting on them, having breastplates I the colorof fire and of hyacinth and of brimstone; and the heads of the horses are like heads of lions; and out of their mouths come forth fire and smoke and brimstone.
9.18: By these three plagues was a third of mankind killed, from the fire, and from the smoke, and from the brimstone, which come forth out of their mouths.
9.19: For the authority of the horses is in their mouth and in their tails; for their tails resemble serpents and have heads; and with them they do harm.
9.20: And the rest of mankind, who were not killed in these plagues, did not repent of the works of their hands, that they will not worship demons, and the idols of gold and of silver and of brass and of stone and of wood, which do not have the power to see nor hear nor walk;
9.21: and they did not repent of their murders, nor of their sorceries, nor of their fornication, nor of their thefts.

10.1: And I saw another strong angel coming down out of Heaven, wrapped in a cloud; and a rainbow was upon his head, and his face was like the sun, and his feet like pillars of fire;
10.2: and he had in his hand a little scroll having been opened. And he set his right foot upon the sea and his left upon the land;
10.3: and he cried out with a great voice, as a lion roars; and when he had cried out, the seven thunders spoke with their voices.
10.4: And when the seven thunders had spoken, I was about to write, but I heard a voice from Heaven saying, " Seal up the things that the seven thunders have spoken, and do not write them. "
10.5: And the angel whom I saw standing upon the sea and upon the land lifted up his right hand to Heaven,
10.6: and swore by Him Who lives forever and ever, Who created Heaven and the things in it, and the sea and the things in it, that time shall no longer be;
10.7: but in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he is about to trumpet, then the mystery of God is brought to its goal, as He announced to His slaves the prophets.
10.8: And the voice that I heard from Heaven was again speaking with me, and saying, " Go, take the scroll which is open in the hand of the angel who stands upon the sea and upon the land. "
10.9: And I went toward the angel, saying to him, " Give the little scroll to me. " And he said to me, " Take it and eat it up, and it will make your stomach bitter, but in your mouth it will be sweet as honey. "
10.10: And I took the little scroll out of the angel’s hand and ate it. And it was sweet as honey in my mouth; and when I had eaten it, my stomach was made bitter.
10.11: And they said to me, " You must prophecy again before many peoples and nations and languages and kings. "

11.1: And there was given to be a reed like a staff, and I was told, " Rise and measure the Temple of God and the altar and those who worship in it,
11.2: " but the court which is outside the Temple leave out, and do not measure it, for it has been given to the nations; and they will trample on the holy city for forty - two months.
11.3: " And I will give I authorityto my two witnesses, and they will prophecy one thousand two hundred sixty days, clothed in sackcloth.

11.5: And if anyone wishes to harm them, fire goes forth out of their mouth and consumes their enemies; and if anyone wishes to harm them, in this way it is necessary for him to be killed.
11.6: These have the authority to shut the sky, so that it might not rain during the days of their prophecy; and they have authority over the waters to change them into blood, and to strike the Earth with every plague, as often as they wish.
11.7: And they have accomplished the goal of their testimony, the beast that ascends out of the abyss will make war with them, and overcome them and kill them.
11.8: And their corpses I will liein the street of the great city which is spiritually called Sodom and Mitzrayim, where also their Lord was crucified,
